en.editorNote: For the worker who heard "working hard or hardly working?" for the thousandth time today. Send it with "try this next time." The line stopped being funny on day one.
variations: When they ask "slow day, huh?" they're really just checking whether they can cut the line.
He's not asking if you're tired. He's asking if someone will help him faster.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the classic 'I'll take my business elsewhere' threat trope in customer-service memes; rewritten as a two-line exchange

zh-tw.content:
「我以後不會再來了！」
「好的，路上小心。」
「你這什麼態度！」
先生，您剛剛才是威脅我的那位。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被客人用「我再也不來了」勒索過的同事。這句話的威力，通常跟他消費的金額成反比。
variations: 「我不會再來了」是奧客版的「我數到三」，數完他還是站在原地。
威脅要走的客人，往往是最捨不得走的那一個。

en.content:
"I'm never coming back here again!"
"Understood. Take care getting home."
"What kind of attitude is that?!"
Sir, you're the one who just threatened to leave.
en.editorNote: For the coworker held hostage by "I'm never coming back." The power of that threat is usually inversely proportional to how much they actually spend.
variations: "I'm never coming back" is the customer version of "I'm counting to three" — and they're still standing there after three.
The customer who threatens to walk is usually the one least willing to.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'closing time customer' recurring service-industry pain point; original scenario built around a Taiwan 打烊 setting

zh-tw.content:
打烊前五分鐘，門推開。
「還沒關吧？」
沒關，因為就差你這一位還沒進來。
燈是為你亮的，也是為你關不掉的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天都在打烊前被最後一組客人「加時賽」的餐飲同事。你不是討厭客人，你只是想準時看到自己家的燈。
variations: 打烊前推門的那一位，通常也是點最多、走最慢的那一位。
「還沒關吧」——這四個字讓下班時間變成一個傳說。

en.content:
Five minutes to close, the door swings open.
"You're not closed yet, right?"
No — you were the only one we were waiting on.
The lights are on for you. They also won't turn off because of you.
en.editorNote: For the food-service worker who plays overtime every night thanks to the last table in. You don't hate the customer — you'd just like to see your own front door before midnight.
variations: The one who pushes the door at closing time usually orders the most and leaves the slowest.
"You're not closed yet, right?" — four words that turn clocking out into a legend.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'call center runs on passive aggression and deep breathing' pun; rewritten as an internal-monologue call-center piece

zh-tw.content:
「您好，很高興為您服務。」
這句話我今天說了兩百次，
開心指數一次比一次低，
但語氣一次比一次穩——
這就是專業。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天要把同一句歡迎詞說到失去意義的客服同事。聲音的穩定，是用心裡的崩潰換來的。
variations: 客服的專業，是把「我快瘋了」講成「很高興為您服務」。
電話那頭的笑聲是免費的，但那笑聲的成本，只有戴耳機的人知道。

en.content:
"Hello, thank you for calling — how can I help?"
I've said it two hundred times today.
My joy drops with each one,
but my tone gets steadier with each one —
that's what they call professional.
en.editorNote: For the call-center agent who has to say the same greeting until it loses all meaning. A steady voice is bought with the meltdown you're hiding behind it.
variations: Call-center professionalism is saying "I'm losing it" as "how can I help you today?"
The cheerful voice on the line is free. Only the person in the headset knows what it cost.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Dcard 心情 board 奧客語錄 thread; rewritten around the condescending 'you must be new here' put-down

zh-tw.content:
「你新來的喔？這都不會。」
我在這五年了。
只是規定沒有為您改，
您就當作我還沒學會。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天被客人用「你新來的喔」瞧不起的同事。你不是不會，你是不肯為一個人破壞所有人的規矩。
variations: 「你新來的喔」翻譯過來就是「你怎麼敢不聽我的」。
資歷五年，還是輸給一句「別家都可以」——但輸的是規定，不是你。

en.content:
"You must be new here — you don't even know this?"
I've been here five years.
The rule just didn't bend for you,
so you decided I hadn't learned it yet.
en.editorNote: For the worker talked down to with "you must be new" today. You're not incompetent — you just won't break everyone's rules for one person.
variations: "You must be new here" translates to "how dare you not do what I say."
Five years in and still losing to "other places allow it" — but it's the rule that lost, not you.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 customer-service burnout reporting noting agents now absorb a higher concentration of emotionally charged calls as self-service handles the easy ones; rewritten as a first-person voice quote

zh-tw.content:
機器人負責回答簡單的問題，
我負責承接崩潰的人。
升級的是系統，
耗損的是我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被自動化留下最難那一塊的客服。你面對的不是問題，是已經被機器人惹到爆炸才轉給你的人。
variations: 自助結帳搶走了輕鬆的單，把「我要投訴」全部留給了人類。
科技進步的意思是：簡單的都不用人做了，只剩最傷的那些是我的。

en.content:
The bot handles the easy questions.
I handle the people falling apart.
The system got the upgrade;
I got the wear and tear.
en.editorNote: For the agent automation left with the hardest slice. You're not facing a problem — you're facing someone the bot already pushed over the edge before transferring them to you.
variations: Self-checkout took all the easy orders and left every "I want to complain" for the humans.
Progress means the simple stuff no longer needs a person — only the parts that hurt are still mine.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Dcard 奧客語錄 thread featuring 'I was able to do this before, why not now'; rewritten around a customer treating a one-time exception as a permanent right

zh-tw.content:
「上次你們可以，這次為什麼不行？」
上次是我通融，
您把好心當成菜單，
以為每一次都能點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天因為「上次好心幫忙」被當成永久福利的同事。通融一次是人情，不是簽約，別讓善意變成把柄。
variations: 「上次可以」的意思是「有人幫你破例」，不是「規定改了」。
把別人的通融記成自己的權利，是奧客最擅長的記帳方式。

en.content:
"You let me last time — why not now?"
Last time I bent the rule for you.
You filed a kindness as a menu item
and assumed you could order it every visit.
en.editorNote: For the coworker whose one-time favor got logged as a permanent perk today. Bending a rule once is a courtesy, not a contract — don't let goodwill become leverage.
variations: "You did it last time" means "someone made an exception," not "the rule changed."
Booking someone else's kindness as your own entitlement is a difficult customer's favorite accounting trick.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 2026 burnout reporting on the demand to always be 'on'; rewritten around the gap between the smile at work and the silence at home

zh-tw.content:
上班笑一整天，
回家一句話都不想說。
不是你變冷淡了，
是你的溫柔都被今天的客人領走了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給下班後只想安靜的服務業家人朋友。他們不是不愛你，是那份笑容已經被上班用完，需要時間重新長回來。
variations: 服務業的沉默不是生氣，是把整天的笑臉還完之後，剩下的那一點自己。
白天發完了全世界的耐心，晚上就沒力氣對最愛的人多說一句了。

en.content:
Smiling all day at work,
then not a word left at home.
You didn't turn cold —
your warmth just got claimed by today's customers.
en.editorNote: For the service-industry loved one who only wants quiet after a shift. It's not that they stopped caring — that smile got spent on the job and needs time to grow back.
variations: A service worker's silence isn't anger. It's the little bit of self that's left after handing out smiles all day.
Give the whole world your patience by daylight and there's none left for the people you love by night.

items.sourceNote: internal only

zh-tw.content: 非常抱歉讓您久等了，這次的狀況確實是我們這邊的疏失。退款我已經幫您立即處理，款項會在三到五個工作天內退回原付款帳戶。造成您的不便，真的很不好意思。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：處理已確認為公司疏失的退款客訴，先道歉再給明確時程
variations: 這部分是我們沒做好，退款我馬上為您送出，三到五個工作天會入帳，還請您稍等一下。
真的很抱歉造成您的困擾，退款已經在處理中，我會全程幫您盯著進度。

en.content: I'm really sorry for the wait, and this one is on us. I've gone ahead and processed your refund right away. It should land back on your original payment method within three to five business days. I truly apologize for the hassle.
en.editorNote: For refund complaints confirmed as company error: apologize, then give a clear timeline
variations: That's on us, and I've already pushed your refund through. It'll show up in three to five business days. Sorry for the trouble.
I'm so sorry about this. Your refund is being processed now, and I'll keep an eye on it until it's done.

items.sourceNote: internal only

zh-tw.content: 您想要的這款目前暫時缺貨，預計下週會補到貨。如果方便的話，我先幫您登記，一到貨就馬上通知您，這樣就不用擔心錯過囉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：商品缺貨時主動提供到貨通知服務，降低顧客流失
variations: 這款剛好賣完了，下週會再進貨，我幫您留個聯絡方式，補到貨第一時間通知您好嗎？
目前沒有現貨，不過很快就會補上，要不要我先幫您預留一組？到貨立刻聯絡您。

en.content: The one you're after is out of stock right now, but we're expecting more next week. If you'd like, I can put you on the list and give you a heads-up the moment it's back, so you don't miss it.
en.editorNote: When an item is out of stock: proactively offer a back-in-stock notification to keep the customer
variations: We just sold out of that one, but a new batch is coming next week. Want me to grab your info and ping you as soon as it lands?
No stock at the moment, but it won't be long. I can set one aside for you and reach out the second it arrives.

items.sourceNote: internal only

zh-tw.content: 這個部分依照我們目前的規定沒辦法直接處理，真的很抱歉。不過我幫您想了另一個做法，應該可以達到差不多的效果，我說明給您聽看看合不合適？
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：無法答應顧客原始要求時，改以替代方案軟性婉拒
variations: 很抱歉這樣做我們這邊沒辦法，但我有另一個建議，或許更符合您的需求，讓我跟您分享一下。
這項目前規定上真的不行，不好意思，我幫您找了個替代方案，聽聽看有沒有幫助？

en.content: I'm sorry, but under our current policy I'm not able to do that directly. That said, I've thought of another approach that should get you pretty much the same result. Can I walk you through it and see if it works for you?
en.editorNote: When you can't grant the original request: soften the no with an alternative
variations: Unfortunately that's not something we can do on our end, but I've got another idea that might fit even better. Mind if I share it?
I really can't do that one, sorry, but here's a workaround I found. Let me know if it helps.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「叫你們店長出來」奧客經典行為，改寫成內心 OS 反轉哏

zh-tw.content:
客人：「叫你們店長出來！」
我：「好的，我就是店長。」
客人：「⋯⋯那叫你們老闆出來。」
原來所謂的「找上面的人」，
真正的意思是
「找一個會答應我的人」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：傳給每天被要求「叫上面出來」的門市主管。重點是奧客要的從來不是層級，是妥協。
variations: 「我要投訴，叫主管來。」主管來了，是我。他的臉瞬間垮下來——因為他要的不是主管，是靠山。
客人堅持要找「有權限的人」，找到最後發現，最有權限說不的那個人，一直站在他面前。

en.content:
Customer: "Get me your manager!"
Me: "Sure — I'm the manager."
Customer: "...then get me the owner."
Turns out "talk to someone higher up"
never meant higher up.
It meant
"find someone who'll say yes."
en.editorNote: For any shift lead who gets 'let me speak to your manager' daily. The demand was never about rank — it was about finding a yes.
variations: "I want to file a complaint. Get your supervisor." The supervisor showed up. It was me. His face dropped — he didn't want a supervisor, he wanted an ally.
He insisted on someone "with the authority." Turns out the person with the most authority to say no was standing in front of him the whole time.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「掃不出來就是免費」retail 經典哏，改寫成台灣賣場語氣

zh-tw.content:
商品條碼掃不出來，
客人眼睛一亮：「那是不是免費的？」
第一次聽覺得好笑，
第一百次聽——
我開始相信，
這句話是全國同步發布的公告，
只是沒人通知店員。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：傳給收銀台的戰友。這句話的殺傷力不在內容，在於每個人都以為自己是第一個想到的。
variations: 掃不出來的當下，總有人要補一句「那免費囉？」我都想回：先生，這台機器壞的是感應器，不是店規。
條碼一嗶不過，客人的反應永遠只有兩種：嘆氣，或者眼睛發亮說「免費喔」。後者，我一天要拒絕八次。

en.content:
The barcode won't scan,
and the customer lights up: "Guess it's free, then?"
The first time, it was funny.
By the hundredth time,
I'm convinced
this line went out as a nationwide memo —
nobody just forgot to tell the cashiers.
en.editorNote: For the folks behind the register. The joke doesn't hurt because of what it says — it hurts because everyone thinks they invented it.
variations: Every time the scanner chokes, someone has to add "so it's free?" Sir, the broken part is the sensor, not the price policy.
When the barcode won't beep, there are only two reactions: a sigh, or the eyes lighting up with "free, right?" I turn down the second one eight times a day.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「別家都可以只有你們不行」奧客語錄，改寫成金句

zh-tw.content:
「別家店都可以，只有你們不行。」
那您真的很推薦別家，
連他們的規定都幫他們記得這麼清楚。
只是我很好奇：
如果別家真的什麼都可以，
您今天為什麼還站在我面前？
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：傳給被「別家都可以」情緒勒索過的每一位。這句話的破綻，往往就在說話的人自己身上。
variations: 客人說「別人家都通融」，我心裡想：那家店真幸運，被您這樣天天惦記著，卻剛好今天沒開。
「你們是我遇過最不方便的一家。」謝謝您把這句話，用同樣的語氣，說給每一家聽。

en.editorNote: For anyone guilt-tripped with 'everyone else allows it.' The hole in that line usually sits with the person saying it.
variations: The customer says "everyone else makes an exception." Lucky them — remembered so fondly, yet somehow closed today.
"You're the most inconvenient place I've ever been to." Thanks — I'm sure you deliver that same line, same tone, to every place you've ever been.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 情緒勞動/微笑面具主題，延續 svc-021、svc-081 的心聲風格

zh-tw.content:
下班脫下制服的那一刻，
我以為我卸下了工作。
其實真正卸不下的，
是那張掛了一整天的笑臉。
它太久沒放下，
連要恢復成自己的表情，
都得練習一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每個回到家還笑不出來、也哭不太出來的服務業朋友。情緒勞動最重的部分，是下班後還在結帳。
variations: 制服可以掛回衣櫃，可是那個微笑，常常掛在臉上忘了拿下來，一路帶回家。
有人問我下班怎麼都面無表情。因為我一整天的表情，早就在櫃檯前用完了。

en.content:
The moment I take off the uniform after a shift,
I think I've left the job behind.
But the thing I can't take off
is the smile I wore all day.
I've held it up so long
that getting my own face back
takes a little practice.
en.editorNote: For every service worker who gets home and can't quite smile — or cry. The heaviest part of emotional labor is the bill that comes due after clocking out.
variations: The uniform goes back in the closet, but the smile? It stays stuck on and rides all the way home with me.
Someone asked why I look blank after work. Because I spent every last expression I had at the counter today.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「你怎麼不笑」被要求微笑的橋段（2026-04 viral），改寫成情緒勞動心聲

zh-tw.content:
「你上班怎麼都不笑一個？」
因為我的笑，是有配額的。
那一份，我留給了
三分鐘前對我大吼的那位。
您來的時候，剛好用完了，
下一批要等我把心情補貨。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給被要求「笑一個」的服務業朋友。微笑是我們的工具，不是你的權利；用完了，就是用完了。
variations: 客人嫌我臭臉，可是他不知道，我這張臉今天已經對五十個人笑過了，剩下的額度，真的擠不出來。
「服務業就是要笑口常開。」是啊，只是沒人告訴客人，那個笑，是我們自己一格一格充上去的。

en.content:
"Why don't you ever smile at work?"
Because my smiles come with a daily quota.
That one, I already gave
to the guy who screamed at me three minutes ago.
You showed up right as it ran out —
the next batch is still restocking.
en.editorNote: For anyone told to 'give us a smile.' The smile is our tool, not your entitlement. When it's spent, it's spent.
variations: A customer called me sour-faced. He didn't know this face already smiled at fifty people today — there's just none left to squeeze out.
"Service work means smiling all day." Sure — nobody tells the customer that smile gets charged back up one bar at a time, by us.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 客人把店員當「情緒支援專員」倒垃圾（2026-05 viral），改寫成心聲金句

zh-tw.content:
我只是問了一句「今天還好嗎」，
您就把整個禮拜的委屈，
連同對前老闆、對前任、對這個世界的怒火，
全部倒進我這個小小的櫃檯。
我的職稱是店員，
不是您沒付錢的情緒回收站。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：傳給那個下班回到家、還在幫全世界收情緒的客服或櫃檯朋友。禮貌問候不等於免費諮商。
variations: 客人把我當樹洞，問題是樹洞不用上班，也沒有業績壓力，還可以裝作沒聽到。
我這個位置，聽過的心事比里長還多，領的卻是最低時薪。

en.content:
I just asked, "How's your day going?"
and you poured a whole week's worth of hurt into me —
the rage at your last boss, your ex, the entire world —
all dumped onto my little counter.
My title is clerk,
not the unpaid recycling bin for your feelings.
en.editorNote: For the counter or call-center friend who gets home still carrying everyone else's emotions. A polite hello is not free therapy.
variations: Customers treat me like a confession booth — except the booth doesn't clock in, doesn't have sales targets, and can pretend it didn't hear.
This seat has heard more secrets than a priest, and gets paid minimum wage to do it.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 2026 餐飲業缺工潮（每4家1家缺人），改寫成缺工現場心聲

zh-tw.content:
客人問：「怎麼這麼慢，你們人呢？」
我想說：人就是我。
外場我、內場我、收銀我，
連剛剛幫您帶位的，也是我。
我不是動作慢，
我是同時在當三個人，還要記得微笑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給缺工現場一打三、一打五的每一位。你不是慢，你是把整間店扛在肩上。
variations: 「你們可以多派幾個人嗎？」可以啊，等你先告訴我上哪找。
以前一個蘿蔔一個坑，現在是一個蘿蔔補三個坑，還要笑著跟你說歡迎光臨。

en.content:
The customer asks, "Why so slow? Where's your staff?"
I want to say: the staff is me.
Front of house — me. Kitchen — me. Register — me.
The one who seated you just now? Also me.
I'm not slow —
I'm being three people at once, and still remembering to smile.
en.editorNote: For everyone running a whole floor solo during the staffing crunch. You're not slow — you're carrying the entire place on your shoulders.
variations: "Can't you put more people on?" Sure — right after you tell me where to find them.
It used to be one person per station. Now it's one person covering three, still cheerfully saying 'welcome in.'

items.sourceNote: internal only — 2026-05 Dcard 調查局「台灣服務業有多累」影片，第一線人員怕被客訴、被公司河蟹只能隱忍的心聲，改寫成台前微笑台後吞聲的對照

zh-tw.content:
您說要客訴我，
我點點頭，說「好的，這是意見卡」。
您不知道的是——
在您寫下第一個字之前，
公司已經先寫好我的道歉，
連我有沒有錯都不用問。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給那些一被威脅客訴，公司連問都不問就先要你道歉的第一線同事。你不是怕客人，你是怕沒人站在你這邊。
variations: 「我要投訴」四個字，在我們公司的意思是「你先道歉，理由之後再說」。
客人手上那張意見卡，比我三年的年資還有份量。

en.content:
You said you'd file a complaint about me.
I nodded and said, "Of course — here's a feedback card."
What you don't know:
before you write the first word,
the company already drafted my apology —
no one even asked whether I did anything wrong.
en.editorNote: For the frontline coworker whose company makes them apologize before anyone checks the facts. You're not scared of customers — you're scared no one's on your side.
variations: "I want to complain" translates, in my company, to "you apologize first, we'll find a reason later."
That feedback card in the customer's hand carries more weight than my three years of tenure.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 2026-05 顧客把酸黃瓜丟到店員臉上要求重做、拿到後又問酸黃瓜在哪的荒謬案例，改寫成餐飲現場的無限迴圈

zh-tw.content:
「這個我不要，重做。」
（重做）
「欸，我要的那個呢？」
先生，您剛剛親手把它丟到我臉上了，
它現在跟您的耐心一樣，
在地上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每天被「重做」跟「你們怎麼做的」夾殺的餐飲人。你沒做錯，只是站在客人記性最差的那一天。
variations: 客人要的東西，通常在他自己剛剛丟掉的那個袋子裡。
重做三次還是同一份，因為問題從來不在那份餐點。

en.content:
"I don't want this. Remake it."
(remade)
"Hey, where's the thing I wanted?"
Sir, you threw it at my face two minutes ago.
It's on the floor now,
right next to your patience.
en.editorNote: For the food-service crew stuck in the loop of "remake it" and "how'd you mess this up." You didn't do anything wrong — you just caught the customer on the day their memory took off.
variations: The thing the customer's asking for is usually in the bag they just threw out.
Third remake, same order — because the problem was never the food.

items.sourceNote: internal only — Not Always Right 零售員工「先服務排隊守規矩的人，把插隊奧客留到最後」的經典還擊，改寫成排隊正義

zh-tw.content:
您大聲說「我很急，先幫我」，
於是我很有效率地，
先幫了您前面那七位，
每一位都幫得特別仔細。
輪到您的時候我笑著說：
「久等了，急的人我都服務完了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給那些不能翻臉、只能用流程反擊的第一線英雄。守規矩的客人，值得你把最好的耐心留給他們。
variations: 插隊的人最怕的不是拒絕，是我照順序、慢慢來、完全合規。
我沒有偏心，我只是對排隊的人特別溫柔。

en.content:
You announced, "I'm in a hurry, help me first."
So I got very efficient —
I helped the seven people ahead of you,
each one with extra care.
When it was finally your turn I smiled:
"Thanks for waiting. I've served everyone who was in a rush."
en.editorNote: For the frontline hero who can't snap back, only fight with process. Customers who wait their turn deserve your very best patience.
variations: The line-cutter's real fear isn't being refused — it's me going in order, slowly, completely by the book.
I'm not playing favorites. I'm just extra gentle with the people who waited.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「顧客永遠是對的」被濫用來合理化奧客行為的討論，改寫成拆穿這句話的心聲

zh-tw.content:
「顧客永遠是對的。」
這句話原本的意思是，
客人喜歡什麼，我們就多賣什麼。
不是——
客人想羞辱誰，我們就得站著讓他羞辱誰。
這中間差了一整個人的尊嚴。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每個被這句話壓著吞下委屈的人。這句話從來不包含「員工要無條件被欺負」，是有人故意讀錯。
variations: 「顧客永遠是對的」下一句，其實是「在他選要買什麼的時候」，不是在他選要罵誰的時候。
把一句行銷格言，硬凹成欺負人的免罪金牌，這才是真正的斷章取義。

en.content:
"The customer is always right."
The phrase originally meant:
sell more of whatever customers want to buy.
It did NOT mean:
whoever a customer wants to humiliate, we stand there and take it.
The difference between those two is one whole person's dignity.
en.editorNote: For everyone who's had this line used to make them swallow abuse. It never meant "staff must be mistreated on demand" — someone's just reading it wrong on purpose.
variations: "The customer is always right" ends with "about what they want to buy" — not about who they get to yell at.
Twisting a marketing slogan into a permission slip for cruelty — that's the real quote taken out of context.

items.sourceNote: internal only — Bored Panda 客服員工回顧「至今仍難忘」的離奇互動，改寫成下班了腦中還在重播的職業病

zh-tw.content:
下班了，制服脫了，
可是那句「你們這什麼態度」，
還在我腦裡循環播放。
奇怪的是，我明明笑到臉都僵了，
他卻聽成了態度。
原來我最需要客訴的人，是我自己——
客訴我把別人的情緒帶回了家。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給那個下班很久、還在腦中重播白天那句話的服務業朋友。把制服掛回衣櫃時，記得把那句話也一起留在那裡。
variations: 職業病就是：客人早就忘了那句話，我卻幫他記了一整晚。
我微笑的肌肉記得所有客人，客人卻連我長怎樣都不記得。

en.content:
Off the clock, uniform off,
but that line — "what kind of attitude is this" —
is still on loop in my head.
The weird part: I smiled till my face went numb,
and he still heard an attitude.
Turns out the person I most need to complain about is me —
for carrying someone else's mood home.
en.editorNote: For the service friend who clocked out hours ago and is still replaying today's line. When you hang the uniform back up, try to leave that sentence hanging there too.
variations: Occupational hazard: the customer forgot that line instantly, and I remembered it for them all night.
My smile muscles remember every customer. The customers don't even remember my face.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「隔壁店可以，你們為什麼不行」是 Dcard 奧客語錄的經典開場，改寫成拆穿這句話邏輯的心聲

zh-tw.content:
「隔壁那家可以，你們為什麼不行？」
那請問，
您現在是站在隔壁那家，
還是站在我這家？
如果隔壁真的什麼都比較好，
那您走進來的這扇門，
應該是走錯了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每天被拿去跟「隔壁那家」比較的第一線人員。奇怪的是，那家什麼都好，客人卻永遠站在你面前。
variations: 客人口中的「隔壁那家」，永遠比較便宜、比較快、比較好——好到他還是選擇來罵你這家。
「別家都可以」如果是真的，那您真的可以去別家，我是認真的。

en.content:
"The place next door can do it — why can't you?"
Quick question:
are you standing next door right now,
or are you standing in front of me?
Because if next door really does everything better,
then the door you just walked through
was the wrong one.
en.editorNote: For the front-liner who gets compared to "the place next door" every single day. Funny how that place is better at everything, yet the customer keeps choosing to stand here yelling at you.
variations: The customer's "other store" is always cheaper, faster, and nicer — so nice they still came here to complain instead.
"Everywhere else lets me" — great, then everywhere else is genuinely welcome to have you. I mean that.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 零售員工最受不了的「掃不到就免費啦」客人自以為幽默的老哏，改寫成聽第八百遍的心聲

zh-tw.content:
商品掃不到，
客人笑著說：「那就免費送我啦！」
先生，這句話
今天您是第七位講的，
上一位在上午十點半，
他也覺得只有他想到。
我的笑是真的，
笑點不是。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每個被「掃不到就免費」「你們生意這麼好一定賺翻」這種自以為新哏轟炸的收銀朋友。你的笑肌很敬業，你的耳朵很想罷工。
variations: 「掃不到免費」這句哏的專利，早在二十年前就過期了，但客人每天都以為是自己剛發明的。
客人以為講了全場最好笑的話，其實他是今天的第七個接力棒。

en.content:
The item won't scan,
and the customer grins: "Guess it's free then!"
Sir, that line —
you're the seventh person to say it today.
The last one was at ten thirty a.m.,
and he also thought he was the only one clever enough.
My smile is real.
The joke isn't.
en.editorNote: For every cashier bombed with "it won't scan, so it's free!" and "business is booming, you must be rich!" Your smile muscles are consummate professionals. Your ears want to file for leave.
variations: The patent on the "guess it's free" joke expired twenty years ago — customers just reinvent it fresh every single morning.
The customer thinks he just landed the funniest line of the day. He's actually the seventh runner in the relay.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「叫你們經理出來」的 Karen 老哏，改寫成基層員工其實比誰都希望經理趕快出現的心聲

zh-tw.content:
「叫你們經理出來！」
好的，我這就去叫——
其實這句話，
我一天想喊八百遍。
您以為經理出來會站您那邊，
他其實只是負責
用比較貴的薪水，
講一模一樣的那句「不好意思」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每個被吼著要找主管的第一線人員。祕密是：你比客人更想把經理挖出來，只是你的理由跟他不一樣。
variations: 客人喊「找你們主管」的那一刻，其實是我今天離下班最近的一次。
經理出來不會改變答案，只會用更貴的時薪講同一句「抱歉，沒辦法」。

en.content:
"Get me your manager!"
Sure, right away —
honestly, that's a sentence
I want to shout eight hundred times a day myself.
You think the manager will take your side.
He's actually just here to say
the exact same "I'm so sorry,"
only on a bigger salary.
en.editorNote: For every front-liner screamed at to "fetch a supervisor." The secret: you want the manager out there even more than the customer does — you two just have different reasons.
variations: The moment a customer yells "get your supervisor," that's the closest I've felt to clocking out all day.
The manager coming over won't change the answer — it just delivers the same "sorry, no can do" at a higher hourly rate.

items.sourceNote: internal only — 「假裝客人是對的」主管建議 vs 員工「我一天已經假裝八小時了」的對照哏，改寫成服務業自嘲心聲

zh-tw.content:
主管教我：
「遇到難搞的客人，就假裝他是對的。」
我說：
「這個我很熟，我一天已經假裝八小時了。」
這份工作最累的
從來不是站著，
是笑著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 使用場景：給每個把「配合演出」當基本功的服務業朋友。體力可以練，臉部肌肉的耐力才是真本事。
variations: 服務業的隱藏技能欄第一格，永遠是「假裝」，而且熟練度早就滿等。
客人以為他遇到很好講話的員工，其實他遇到的是一個演技很好的。

en.content:
My supervisor coached me:
"With a difficult customer, just pretend they're right."
I said:
"Oh, I've got that down — I already pretend for eight hours a day."
The hardest part of this job
was never the standing.
It's the smiling.
en.editorNote: For everyone whose core skill is "playing along." You can train your legs for the standing — it's the facial-muscle endurance that's the real qualification.
variations: First slot on a service worker's hidden skill tree is always "pretending," and it maxed out years ago.
The customer thinks he found an easygoing employee. He actually found a really good actor.

items.sourceNote: Rebuilt from the canonical retail meme 'item won't scan / I guess it's free' — reworked into a zh-tw counter-dialogue with a fresh punchline about the barcode being the one thing not on sale

zh-tw.content:
商品刷不過。
客人：「刷不過就是免費的吧？」
我：「刷不過的是條碼，不是您的良心。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給收銀台朋友，附一句「今天第幾個想免費結帳的」。這句是心裡默念版，實際上你還是會笑著說『我幫您重刷一次喔』。
variations: 全店都在打折，唯一沒在特價的是客人那句『那就免費啦』的臉皮厚度。
條碼刷不過只代表機器累了，不代表宇宙決定請你吃這一單。

en.content:
Item won't scan.
Customer: "Guess it's free then?"
Me: "What won't scan is the barcode — not your conscience."
en.editorNote: Send to a cashier friend with "how many free-checkout attempts today?" This is the say-it-in-your-head version — out loud you still smile and go 'let me rescan that.'
variations: Everything in the store is on sale except the nerve it takes to say 'guess it's free.'
A barcode that won't scan means the machine is tired, not that the universe is buying your groceries.

items.sourceNote: Reworked from the 'agents run on passive aggression and deep breathing' meme — turned into an internal-monologue battery-metaphor line for call-center 客服

zh-tw.content:
客服的日常燃料表：
三成微笑、兩成深呼吸、五成把『你在公三小』翻譯成『我了解您的心情』。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合客服朋友下班後 IG 限動，配一張耳機麥克風照。翻譯是一種專業，也是一種消耗。
variations: 客服不是不生氣，是把生氣即時同步翻譯成敬語，還要秒回。
接一整天電話的續航力，靠的不是咖啡，是把髒話換成『非常抱歉』的自動校正功能。

en.content:
A support agent's daily fuel gauge:
30% smile, 20% deep breathing, 50% translating "what is your problem" into "I completely understand."
en.editorNote: For a call-center friend's after-work story, paired with a headset photo. Live translation is a skill — and a slow drain.
variations: Support agents do get angry. They just live-translate it into honorifics before it reaches the mic.
The stamina to take calls all day doesn't run on coffee. It runs on autocorrecting swear words into 'so sorry about that.'

items.sourceNote: Rebuilt from the 'retail is hide-and-seek, the customer always finds you' meme — localized to the exact moment a staffer clocks out for break

zh-tw.content:
服務業版的躲貓貓：
我躲進倉庫、關燈、憋氣，
休息鈴一響，客人準時在門口喊『不好意思有人嗎』。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛被『下班前最後三分鐘客人』堵到的同事。這不是巧合，是奧客的雷達精準得可以拿去做導航。
variations: 客人找不到商品的耐心是零，找正在休息的店員的雷達卻是軍規等級。
只要我一坐下吃飯，門口就會生出一個『請問一下』——這是服務業的物理定律。

en.content:
Retail hide-and-seek:
I duck into the stockroom, kill the lights, hold my breath —
the second my break bell rings, a customer at the door goes "excuse me, anyone here?"
en.editorNote: Send to a coworker who just got ambushed in their last three minutes on shift. It's not coincidence — a difficult customer's radar is accurate enough to sell as GPS.
variations: A customer has zero patience finding a product, but military-grade radar for finding the one clerk on break.
The moment I sit down to eat, a 'quick question' spawns at the door. It's a law of retail physics.

items.sourceNote: Rebuilt from the 'this job builds character — and a dark sense of humor' meme — reframed as a resignation-letter-style reflection on what service work actually installs in you

zh-tw.content:
都說服務業能磨練人。
磨出來的不是耐心，
是一種笑著把髒話吞下去、
回家還能拿今天的奧客當笑話講的黑色幽默。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合做滿一年、突然發現自己變了的服務業朋友。這份工作給你的履歷技能，通常不會寫在履歷上。
variations: 服務業真正教會你的，不是話術，是怎麼把最爛的一天，講成朋友聚餐時最好笑的段子。
在服務業待久了會有兩種收穫：一種叫抗壓性，一種叫黑到發亮的笑點。

en.content:
They say service work builds character.
What it actually builds
isn't patience —
it's the dark humor to swallow a swear with a smile
and retell today's worst customer as tonight's best story.
en.editorNote: For a friend one year in who suddenly realizes they've changed. The résumé skills this job installs are never the ones you put on the résumé.
variations: What service work really teaches you isn't scripts — it's how to turn your worst day into the funniest bit at dinner with friends.
Stay in service long enough and you leave with two things: a high stress tolerance and a sense of humor black enough to shine.

items.sourceNote: Reworked from the 2026 'the best customer service tool is a fake smile and an internal scream' meme circulating on support-team socials

zh-tw.content:
臉上：「好的沒問題，很樂意為您服務～」
心裡：（尖叫三十秒，重開機，繼續營業）
這份工作最強的工具，
從來不是話術，是這張切換自如的臉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天上班要開兩個分頁的服務業朋友——一個對客人微笑，一個在後台默默崩潰。這張臉練成了，什麼奧客都打不倒你。
variations: 服務業的臉部肌肉，比誰都懂什麼叫『表裡不一是專業』。
嘴角上揚十五度，內心已經跑完一整套髒話——這叫服務業的基本功。

en.content:
Face: "Absolutely, happy to help you with that!"
Brain: (screams for thirty seconds, reboots, resumes business)
The strongest tool in this job
was never the script — it's this face that switches on command.
en.editorNote: For the friend who runs two tabs at work every day: one smiling at the customer, one quietly crashing in the back. Once you master this face, no customer can knock you down.
variations: A service worker's facial muscles understand better than anyone that 'looking calm while dying inside' is a professional skill.
Corners of the mouth up fifteen degrees, a full string of curses already finished inside — that's the basics of service work.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from Dcard 心情 board complaints about customers assuming staff are 'chatting in the back' during long waits — turned into a monologue about invisible labor

zh-tw.content:
「怎麼那麼慢，你們是不是在後面聊天？」
後面沒有天可以聊，
只有三個人扛六個人的班、
手忙腳亂到連水都沒空喝。
慢的不是我們，是這條永遠補不滿的人力。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給尖峰時段被質疑『動作慢』的餐飲服務業朋友。客人看不到廚房，就以為後面很閒——其實那裡才是戰場。
variations: 客人以為的『後面』是休息室，實際上的『後面』是打仗現場。
不是我們慢，是老闆把三個人的班，排給了一個人跑。

en.content:
"Why's it so slow — are you all chatting in the back?"
There's no chatting back there.
Three people are covering a six-person shift,
too slammed to even sip water.
We're not the slow part — the staffing that never gets filled is.
en.editorNote: For food-service friends accused of being 'slow' at peak hours. Customers can't see the kitchen, so they assume it's relaxed back there — it's actually the battlefield.
variations: The 'back' customers imagine is a break room. The real 'back' is a war zone.
We're not slow — the boss handed a three-person shift to one person to run.

items.sourceNote: Reworked from the 2026 'customer service: therapy, unpaid edition' meme — expanded into a reflection on absorbing strangers' bad days

zh-tw.content:
客服這行，說穿了是免費的心理諮商——
只是沒有執照、沒有時薪加給，
還要在對方把整天的火氣倒完之後，
笑著說一句：「還有什麼可以為您服務的嗎？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天接電話接到耳朵發燙的客服朋友。你承接了多少陌生人的壞情緒，卻沒人問過你今天過得好不好。
variations: 客服的耳機裡，一天要裝下一百個人的壞心情，然後下班自己一個人慢慢倒出來。
別人的情緒垃圾桶當久了，記得也要找個人，把自己倒乾淨。

en.content:
Customer service, stripped down, is unpaid therapy —
no license, no hazard pay,
and after they've dumped a whole day's rage on you,
you still smile and say: "Anything else I can help you with?"
en.editorNote: For the call-center friend whose ears run hot by the end of every shift. You absorb so many strangers' bad moods, and nobody ever asks how your own day went.
variations: A support headset holds a hundred people's bad moods a day — then you clock out and pour your own out alone.
Be everyone's emotional trash can long enough, and you owe it to yourself to find someone to empty into too.

items.sourceNote: Built from the 2026 pun 'calm is my KPI' — reframed as a quiet flex about the composure service work forces you to grow

zh-tw.content:
別人的KPI是業績、是流量，
我的KPI是——
不管對面多離譜，都能維持那句平穩的『好的』。
這份工作最貴的產出，
是我這身怎麼激都不炸的鎮定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被客人罵到快理智斷線、卻還是穩穩收尾的服務業朋友。你的鎮定不是天生的，是被一個個奧客磨出來的高級技能。
variations: 服務業練最久的一項能力，叫『內心海嘯，語氣風平浪靜』。
能在被吼的當下還保持微笑，這種穩，其實比業績更難達標。

en.content:
Other people's KPI is sales, is traffic.
Mine is —
keeping that steady "of course" no matter how absurd the person across from me gets.
The most expensive output of this job
is a composure that won't detonate no matter how hard you poke it.
en.editorNote: For the friend one insult away from snapping who still closes the interaction calmly. Your composure isn't natural — it's a high-level skill ground into you one difficult customer at a time.
variations: The skill service work trains longest is 'tsunami inside, dead-calm tone outside.'
Holding a smile the moment you're being yelled at — that kind of steady is harder to hit than any sales target.

items.sourceNote: Built from the 2026 meme 'my brain has too many tabs open and they're all customer complaints' — rewritten as an end-of-shift mental-overload image

zh-tw.content:
下班了，腦子裡還開著三十幾個分頁，
每一頁都是一句沒回完的客訴。
身體躺在沙發上，
記憶體卻整晚都跑在滿載紅字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個明明下班了、卻還在腦內加班的服務業朋友。累的不只是腳，是那個關不掉的背景程式。
variations: 服務業的下班，是把店門關上，卻忘了把腦子裡那家店也關掉。
回到家才發現，最難清空的購物車，是腦袋裡那一整天沒處理完的情緒。

en.content:
Off the clock, and my brain still has thirty-some tabs open —
every one of them a half-answered complaint.
My body's on the couch,
but my memory's been maxed out in the red all night.
en.editorNote: For the friend who clocked out hours ago and is still working overtime inside their own head. It's not just the feet that ache — it's the background app you can't force-quit.
variations: Clocking out in service work means locking the store's door but forgetting to close the one still running in your head.
You get home and realize the hardest cart to empty is the day's worth of feelings still sitting in your brain.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 2026 'declining your business is a kindness to us both' 趕奧客 clip trend — reframed from the boss's side into a quiet self-respect message for frontline staff

zh-tw.content:
不是每一筆生意都值得接。
有些客人走了，
不是損失，是解脫。
對彼此的寬容，
有時候就是那句：『不好意思，我們可能不適合服務您。』
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總覺得『客人再爛也要忍』的服務業朋友。守住底線不是沒禮貌，是替自己、也替下一個同事，把那顆地雷擋在門外。
variations: 把最爛的那個客人請出去，是你能送給整組同事最溫柔的一件事。
有些業績不值得用你的尊嚴去換，錢再賺就有，人被踩碎了很難補。

en.content:
Not every sale is worth taking.
Some customers walking out
isn't a loss — it's relief.
Sometimes the kindest thing for both sides
is simply: "I'm sorry, we may not be the right fit to serve you."
en.editorNote: For the friend who believes they must endure any customer no matter how awful. Holding a boundary isn't rude — it's keeping that landmine outside the door, for yourself and for the next coworker.
variations: Showing the worst customer the exit is the gentlest gift you can hand the rest of your team.
Some sales aren't worth trading your dignity for — money you can earn back, but a person who's been ground down is hard to rebuild.

items.sourceNote: Reworked from the 2026 line 'I don't get paid enough for this, but I'm doing it anyway' — turned into a wry tribute to quiet professionalism under bad pay

zh-tw.content:
這份薪水，其實不夠付我今天吞下的委屈。
但客人一進門，
我還是把最標準的那個微笑掛好，
因為爛的是價碼，
不是我做事的樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個明知道錢少、卻還是把每一單做到位的服務業朋友。你把事情做好，從來不是因為它值得，而是因為你就是這種人。
variations: 薪水配不上你的專業，但你的專業從來不肯配合薪水擺爛。
老闆給的是最低時薪，你交出的卻是滿分服務——這差額，叫做骨氣。

en.content:
This paycheck doesn't cover half the grief I swallowed today.
But the second a customer walks in,
I hang the standard smile back up,
because what's cheap is the wage —
not the way I do my job.
en.editorNote: For the friend who knows the pay is bad and still nails every single order. You do it right not because it's worth it, but because that's just the kind of person you are.
variations: The wage doesn't deserve your craft, but your craft has never agreed to slack off to match the wage.
They pay you minimum, you hand back a perfect shift — that gap right there is called self-respect.

items.sourceNote: Built from the 2026 pun 'my patience has unlimited minutes' — extended into a data-plan metaphor about patience quietly running out of coverage

zh-tw.content:
以前總說自己耐心吃到飽、用不完。
做久了才發現，
那個『無限方案』其實一直在偷偷限速——
上午還滿格，
到了第三個奧客，就只剩龜速陪笑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個從早到晚被慢慢磨掉耐心的客服朋友。你不是變冷淡了，是這個月的耐心流量，真的被人用超了。
variations: 耐心也是有流量的，超過就會降速——只是沒人幫你儲值。
早上的『好的沒問題』和下午的『……好』，中間差的不是態度，是剩下的耐心格數。

en.content:
I used to say my patience was an unlimited plan — never runs out.
Do this long enough and you learn
that 'unlimited plan' has been quietly throttling me all along:
full bars in the morning,
by the third difficult customer, just a crawling, forced smile.
en.editorNote: For the support friend whose patience gets slowly worn down from open to close. You didn't turn cold — you just went over your patience data for the month, and nobody topped it up.
variations: Patience has a data cap too; go over it and you get throttled — except nobody's refilling yours.
The gap between morning's 'sure, no problem' and afternoon's '…fine' isn't attitude — it's how many bars of patience you've got left.

items.sourceNote: 東森新聞雲『餐廳奧客語錄』中『認識老闆想凹折扣』與『老樣子誰記得』的橋段，重新改寫

zh-tw.content:
「我跟你們老闆很熟。」
「那要幫您打幾折？」
「你打了老闆會生氣吧？」
熟到不敢讓老闆知道，這種交情我也想要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個又被「我認識你們老闆」開場的餐飲朋友。真的熟的客人，通常安安靜靜就把錢付了。
variations: 真的認識老闆的人，不會需要一直提自己認識老闆。
「我跟老闆很熟」後面接的通常不是問候，是折扣。

en.content:
"I'm good friends with your boss."
"Great — how big a discount should I apply?"
"Well, wouldn't the boss get mad if you did?"
So close you can't let the boss find out — I'd love a friendship like that.
en.editorNote: For the restaurant friend who got the 'I know your owner' opener again. The customers who actually know the boss usually just pay quietly and leave.
variations: People who genuinely know the owner don't need to keep announcing they know the owner.
'I'm tight with your boss' is almost never followed by 'send them my regards' — it's followed by 'so, a discount?'

items.sourceNote: Pleated-Jeans 2026 客服迷因輯中『對著答案發問』『Employees Only 當建議』的橋段，改寫成雙語版

zh-tw.content:
客人指著寫「本日公休」的牌子問：「你們今天有開嗎？」
我看著那塊牌子，
牌子看著我，
我們都很想知道答案。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給零售櫃檯的朋友。有些問題的答案就貼在客人的正前方，但他們選擇相信活人比字大。
variations: 答案就貼在門上，客人卻寧願問一個更累的活人。
「你們有開嗎」——先生，我要是沒開，是誰在跟您說話呢？

en.content:
Customer points at the sign that says 'CLOSED TODAY' and asks: "Are you open today?"
I look at the sign,
the sign looks at me,
and we're both dying to know the answer.
en.editorNote: For the friend behind a retail counter. Some answers are printed directly in front of the customer, but they've decided a live human outranks large print.
variations: The answer is taped to the door, yet they'd rather interrogate a tired human.
'Are you open?' — sir, if we weren't, who exactly do you think is talking to you?

items.sourceNote: Thunder Dungeon 2026 客服迷因『smiled so hard my face tried to unionize』與『therapy has a copay, customers don't』延伸改寫

zh-tw.content:
今天笑到臉部肌肉想成立工會，
要求加班費、休息時間，還有一條「不准對奧客再擠出笑容」的條款。
我理解它，但我還是得請它繼續營業——
因為房租不會因為我不想笑就變便宜。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個下班後臉還僵著的服務業朋友。你的笑容今天真的加班了，記得回家讓它下班。
variations: 情緒勞動也是勞動，只是薪水單上永遠不會有這一欄。
下班第一件事，是把整天掛在臉上的那個笑容，輕輕拿下來放好。

en.content:
Smiled so hard today my face tried to unionize —
demanding overtime, breaks, and a clause that says 'no more forced smiles at difficult customers.'
I hear it out, then ask it to please keep operating,
because rent doesn't get cheaper just because I don't feel like smiling.
en.editorNote: For the service friend whose face is still stiff after clocking out. Your smile really did work overtime today — remember to let it clock out once you're home.
variations: Emotional labor is still labor; it just never shows up as a line on the paycheck.
First thing after your shift: gently take off the smile you wore all day and set it down.

items.sourceNote: 延伸自 2026-07 新竹奧客點餐嗆店員「你審犯人啊」新聞；改寫為店員回擊的一問一答，去掉原始人物與地點

zh-tw.content:
「請問內用還是外帶？」
「你審犯人啊，問這麼多？」
「先生，這是點餐，不是做筆錄。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天被客人嫌「問太多」的外場朋友。你只是照 SOP 問一句，對方卻演得像被上銬——記得，問問題的是你，該冷靜的是他。
variations: 把最基本的服務流程當成刑求的人，通常最禁不起別人對他有一點點要求。
「你問這麼多幹嘛」——因為不問，等等被客訴的還是我啊。

en.content:
"For here or to go?"
"What is this, an interrogation?"
"Sir, this is an order — not a deposition."
en.editorNote: For the front-of-house friend who got told they "ask too much" today. You ran one line of the SOP; they performed a whole arrest scene. Remember: you asked the question, and they're the one who needs to calm down.
variations: People who treat a basic service question like a cross-examination usually can't handle the tiniest request in return.
"Why are you asking so much?" Because if I don't, I'm the one getting the complaint later.

items.sourceNote: 延伸自 2026-07 新竹「店長護員工、嗆奧客回來道歉」新聞；改寫為店長的護短宣言，強調挺員工的療癒面

zh-tw.content:
我的員工可以低頭跟客人賠不是，
但沒有人可以對我的員工丟東西。
你的錢，我可以不賺；
我的人，我一定得護。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個曾經被主管挺過、或一直偷偷渴望被主管挺一次的服務業朋友。好的店長不是最會賠笑的那個，是願意站在你前面的那個。
variations: 會護員工的主管很少，所以遇到一個，要記得一輩子。
客人永遠是對的？不，我的員工被欺負的時候，客人就是錯的。

en.content:
My staff can bow their heads and apologize to a customer.
But nobody gets to throw things at my staff.
Your money — I can afford to lose.
My people — I will always cover.
en.editorNote: For the service friend who's been shielded by a good manager, or the one still quietly hoping to be shielded just once. The best manager isn't the one who smiles hardest — it's the one willing to stand in front of you.
variations: Managers who protect their staff are rare, so if you find one, remember them for life.
The customer is always right? No — the moment my employee gets bullied, the customer is wrong.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 2026 客服迷因『demand magic then get angry at physics』；換成台式手搖飲「不要冰但要透心涼」情境

zh-tw.content:
客人要一杯「不加冰、但要透心涼」的飲料。
我說辦不到，他說「你們服務業就是不用心」。
先生，我是店員，不是能違反物理定律的巫師。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個今天被要求「變出不可能」的手搖店同事。奧客要的不是飲料，是奇蹟；而你的時薪，真的不包含施法。
variations: 客人對物理定律生氣的時候，最無辜的永遠是站在櫃檯的那個人。
「這你們也做不到？」對，因為地球還是有重力，我也還是人類。

en.content:
A customer wants a drink that's "no ice, but ice-cold."
I say it can't be done; he says, "you service people just don't try."
Sir, I'm a clerk — not a wizard who breaks the laws of physics.
en.editorNote: For the boba-shop coworker who got asked to "conjure the impossible" today. The difficult customer doesn't want a drink — they want a miracle, and your hourly wage does not include casting spells.
variations: When a customer gets mad at the laws of physics, the most innocent person is always the one standing at the counter.
"You can't even do that?" Correct — because gravity still exists and so, unfortunately, do I.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 2026 客服迷因『customer pressing face to the glass before opening, museum exhibit titled Employee Trying Not To Scream』

zh-tw.content:
還沒開門，客人已經把臉貼在玻璃上，
像在看一場展覽，展名叫〈努力憋著不尖叫的店員〉。
我們十點營業，不是十點「差不多」營業。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每天被客人隔著玻璃盯著開門的零售朋友。營業時間是時間，不是建議；你有權利在鐵門拉開前，先好好呼吸一下。
variations: 把「營業時間」當成參考答案的客人，通常也把「排隊」當成別人家的事。
開門前那十分鐘的玻璃對視，是服務業每天限定的恐怖片。

en.content:
We're not open yet, but the customer's already got their face on the glass,
staring like it's an exhibit titled "Employee Trying Not to Scream."
We open at ten — not ten-ish.
en.editorNote: For the retail friend who gets watched through the glass every single morning. Opening time is a time, not a suggestion — and you're allowed one full breath before the shutters go up.
variations: Customers who treat "opening hours" as a rough guess usually treat "the line" as someone else's problem.
That ten-minute glass stare-down before opening is the daily horror short film of service work.

items.sourceNote: 改寫自 2026 客服迷因『when the worst customer threatens to never come back, that's a legendary drop』；換成台式「掉寶／放煙火」比喻

zh-tw.content:
最盧的那位客人撂下狠話：「我以後再也不來了！」
全店員工在心裡，默默放了一串隱形的煙火。
有些客人的離開，不是損失，是掉寶。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個今天被威脅「不來了」還得強忍笑意的同事。不是每個客人都值得挽留——有些人走了，店裡的空氣都變甜了。
variations: 「我要客訴你們！」——好的，麻煩慢走，記得別再回頭。
有的客人是常客，有的客人是我們每天祈禱他變成前客的那種。

en.content:
The most exhausting customer drops the line: "I'm NEVER coming back!"
Every employee sets off a silent, invisible firework inside.
Some customers leaving isn't a loss — it's a legendary drop.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who got threatened with "never again" today and had to bite back a grin. Not every customer is worth keeping — some leave, and the whole shop's air tastes sweeter.
variations: "I'm filing a complaint!" — Of course, mind the door, and please don't circle back.
Some customers are regulars; others are the ones we quietly pray will become former customers.

items.sourceNote: Service-industry meme trope: customer arrives before opening, presses face to the glass, stares at staff like a museum exhibit

zh-tw.content:
還沒開門，客人已經把臉貼在玻璃上盯著我。
「營業時間」對他來說，好像只是一個參考數字。
我也想開門，真的，等我先把靈魂裝回身體。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每天提早半小時被玻璃外眼神施壓的早班同事。門上的時間是規定，不是建議。
variations: 十點開門，九點五十就有人用眼神撬鎖。
隔著玻璃被盯到準備開門，我不是店員，我是水族箱裡的展示品。

en.content:
We're not open yet, but the customer's already got their face pressed to the glass, staring at me.
To them, "business hours" is more of a rough estimate.
I want to open too, I promise — right after I finish loading my soul back into my body.
en.editorNote: For the opening-shift coworker who gets stared down through the glass every single morning. The time on the door is a rule, not a suggestion.
variations: Doors open at ten; someone's been picking the lock with their eyeballs since 9:50.
Getting stared at through the glass before open — I'm not a clerk, I'm an aquarium exhibit.

items.sourceNote: Customer-service meme trope: the moment you finally sit down for a break, a customer materializes with a question

zh-tw.content:
我的休息時間五分鐘後開始，
那個要來問問題的客人，也是五分鐘後到。
我們像是被同一條命運線牽著，只是我想休息，他想毀掉它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個便當才扒兩口就被叫回櫃檯的同事。宇宙好像有雷達，專門偵測你剛坐下的瞬間。
variations: 屁股碰到椅子零點五秒，客人自動生成。
休息室的椅子還是溫的，我人已經回到現場了。

en.content:
My break starts in five minutes.
So does the customer speed-walking over with a question.
We're tied to the same thread of fate — I just want to rest, and they want to destroy it.
en.editorNote: For the coworker dragged back to the counter after two bites of lunch. The universe has a radar tuned to the exact second you finally sit down.
variations: Butt touches chair for 0.5 seconds; customer spawns automatically.
The break-room seat is still warm and I'm already back on the floor.

items.sourceNote: Customer-service meme line: 'customer service memes exist because therapy has a copay and customers don't' — reframed into a self-care punchline

zh-tw.content:
有人問我下班為什麼都不講話。
因為我一天的字數，早就在電話裡對陌生人用完了。
我的耐心不是無限的，是每天早上重新充電、下午就見底的那種。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個接了一整天電話、回到家只想安靜的客服朋友。他不是冷淡，是額度用光了。
variations: 客服的情緒不是免費的，只是沒有收費機制而已。
白天對客人溫柔，是因為我把脾氣預支給了晚上的自己。

en.content:
People ask why I go quiet after work.
Because my daily word count got used up on strangers over the phone.
My patience isn't unlimited — it recharges every morning and runs flat by mid-afternoon.
en.editorNote: For the call-center friend who answers phones all day and just wants silence at home. They're not cold — the meter just hit zero.
variations: A service worker's emotional labor isn't free; there's just no billing system for it.
I'm gentle with customers all day because I borrowed the temper from tonight's version of me.

items.sourceNote: Customer-service meme trope: the customer demands a manager, the manager shows up and repeats word-for-word what the employee already said

zh-tw.content:
「叫你們經理出來！」
經理出來，講了跟我一模一樣的話。
客人沉默三秒：「……那你剛剛怎麼不早說？」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個今天被客人指定「換一個人來講」的同事。同一句話，從店員嘴裡是狡辯，從經理嘴裡就是政策。
variations: 客人要的不是正確答案，是一個階級比較高的人來講同一句話。
經理的功能，有時候就是把我的話重講一次，然後被相信。

en.content:
"Get me your manager!"
The manager comes out and says the exact same thing I just said.
Three seconds of silence, then: "...well why didn't you say so?"
en.editorNote: For the coworker who got told today to "send someone else over." Same sentence — coming from the clerk it's an excuse, coming from the manager it's policy.
variations: The customer didn't want the right answer. They wanted a higher rank to say it.
Sometimes a manager's whole job is repeating my sentence and getting believed.

items.sourceNote: Retail meme trope: customers who treat posted opening time as a suggestion, pressing their face to the glass before the doors unlock

zh-tw.content:
門上寫十點開，
九點四十五就有人把臉貼在玻璃上，
用那種「我在看你，你為什麼不動」的眼神盯著我準備。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個開店前十五分鐘就被客人隔著玻璃監視的零售同事。營業時間是承諾，不是挑戰書。
variations: 貼在玻璃上的那張臉，是每個店員上班前的第一個問候。
還沒開門就在門口排隊，你當我是演唱會售票嗎。

en.content:
The door says we open at ten.
By 9:45 someone's got their face pressed to the glass,
staring at me setting up with a look that says "I see you. Why aren't you moving."
en.editorNote: For the retail coworker surveilled through the window fifteen minutes before open. The posted hours are a promise, not a dare.
variations: That face on the glass is every clerk's first greeting of the shift.
Lining up before we unlock — what do you think this is, a concert drop?

items.sourceNote: Sparked by a 2026 新竹 news clip where a couple accused an early-brunch clerk of 「在審問我」 for asking sweetness/ice level — reframed into a service-worker POV punchline

zh-tw.content:
「甜度冰塊要正常還是少一點？」
「你這樣一直問，是在審問我嗎？」
先生，我只是想把您的飲料做對，不是想知道您昨晚在哪。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個問個甜度都會被翻白眼的飲料店同事。問清楚是敬業，不問才會被客訴，怎麼做都是錯的那種日子。
variations: 問甜度是審問，不問是擅自作主，服務業的標準答案永遠在下一頁。
我問三個字是為了不讓你等等來罵五分鐘。

en.content:
"Normal or less sweet? Regular ice or light?"
"Why do you keep interrogating me?"
Sir, I'm trying to make your drink right, not find out where you were last night.
en.editorNote: For the drink-shop coworker who gets an eye-roll just for asking about sweetness. Asking is diligence, not asking is a complaint waiting to happen — one of those no-win days.
variations: Ask about the sweetness and it's an interrogation; don't ask and it's overstepping. The right answer is always on the next page.
Those three words I asked are so you don't spend five minutes yelling later.

items.sourceNote: Customer-service meme theme: constant task-switching as the unspoken job requirement — phone, counter, and floor all demanding you at once

zh-tw.content:
一手接電話，一手結帳，
眼睛盯著門口那位在找我的客人，
嘴巴還要對第四個人說「馬上為您處理」。
我不是店員，我是同時開四個分頁的瀏覽器。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一個人被當三個人用的同事。老闆說這叫「靈活」，我們自己知道這叫「快當機」。
variations: 服務業的多工，不是能力，是沒人手逼出來的求生技能。
同時處理四件事的我，其實四件都只做到六成。

en.content:
Phone in one hand, ringing up a sale with the other,
eyes locked on the customer by the door looking for me,
mouth telling a fourth person "right with you."
I'm not a clerk. I'm a browser running four tabs at once.
en.editorNote: For the coworker doing the work of three people alone. The boss calls it "flexible." We know it's one keystroke from crashing.
variations: Multitasking in service isn't a skill. It's a survival trick beaten out of us by understaffing.
Handling four things at once means I'm doing all four at 60 percent.

items.sourceNote: Reframed from 2026 news coverage of Taiwan's service-sector staffing crisis (500,000 unfilled openings) — the worker's-eye view of why nobody wants the job

zh-tw.content:
新聞說服務業五十萬個職缺沒人要做。
主管皺眉問：「現在的人怎麼都不願意吃苦？」
不是不願意吃苦，是我們終於發現，這個苦不值那個薪水。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被說「草莓」、其實只是算清楚一筆帳的同事。願意留下來的人不是比較耐操，是還沒找到更好的出口而已。
variations: 缺工不是年輕人怕苦，是這份苦終於被標上了它真實的價格。
留下來的不一定是最堅強的，只是還在等更好的那一個。

en.content:
The news says service jobs have 500,000 openings nobody wants.
My manager frowns: "Why won't people these days work hard?"
It's not that we won't. It's that we finally did the math — this much pain isn't worth that little pay.
en.editorNote: For the coworker called "soft" who actually just ran the numbers. The ones who stay aren't tougher — they just haven't found a better exit yet.
variations: The labor shortage isn't young people fearing hard work. It's the work finally getting priced at what it really costs.
The ones who stay aren't the strongest. They're just still waiting on something better.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 超商板店員荒謬經驗討論串，職業病延伸發想

zh-tw.content:
回到家開門的那一刻，
我對著空無一人的客廳說了聲「歡迎光臨」。
沒有人回我，只有貓抬頭看了一眼。
那一秒我才發現，
這份工作已經住進我的反射神經裡了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在打工族群組，或傳給那個下班還會脫口說「這樣好嗎」的朋友。職業病不是笑話，是身體記住了太多次的證據。
variations: 我的嘴巴比我的意識早下班兩小時，可惜它下的是另一種班。
有些話說了幾千次之後，就不再需要經過大腦，也不再屬於你。

en.content:
I opened my front door and said "Welcome in!" to an empty living room.
Nobody answered. The cat just looked up.
That's when it hit me —
this job has moved into my reflexes and started paying no rent.
en.editorNote: For the group chat of part-timers, or the friend who still says "sorry for the wait" at their own dinner table. The muscle memory isn't a joke — it's proof of how many times your body did it.
variations: My mouth clocks out two hours after my brain, and it's still on someone else's shift.
Say anything a few thousand times and it stops needing your brain — and stops being yours.

items.sourceNote: 護理人員被以「你們也是服務業」為由要求無理服務的新聞討論

zh-tw.content:
家屬吼我：「你們不就是服務業嗎？」
是啊，我是。
但服務業不等於你想怎樣就怎樣，
我賣的是專業，不是我的尊嚴。
這兩樣東西，從來沒有一起標價。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給被「你們就是服務業」這句話壓過的任何人——護理師、老師、櫃檯、客服。用得上的時候，這句話很有力量。
variations: 「服務業」這三個字，被太多人當成免責聲明在用。
我提供的是服務，不是任你處置的權利，這中間差了一整個人的份量。

en.content:
A patient's family yelled at me: "Aren't you people just service workers?"
Sure. I am.
But service doesn't mean whatever you feel like.
I'm selling my expertise, not my dignity.
Those two were never on the same price tag.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's been flattened by the phrase "you're just customer service" — nurses, teachers, front desk, support reps. Keep it in your pocket for the day you need it.
variations: "It's a service job" has become the most overused permission slip in the country.
I offer you service. I never offered you a person to do whatever you want with.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 服務業甘苦談，好客人一句謝謝的療癒效果

zh-tw.content:
今天有位客人走之前，
把杯子疊好、發票撿起來、椅子推回桌下，
然後說了句「辛苦了」。
他大概花不到十秒，
卻幫我把一整天被踩扁的地方，慢慢撐了回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給你認識的服務業朋友當作提醒：真的有人記得你。也適合當作提醒自己——當客人的時候，那十秒不難。
variations: 有些客人不用多做什麼，光是把自己收拾好，就已經是溫柔了。
一句「辛苦了」不會改變薪水，但會改變我今晚睡前想到的畫面。

en.content:
A customer stacked his cups, picked up his receipt,
pushed the chair back under the table,
and said "thanks, long day huh?" on his way out.
Ten seconds, tops.
And somehow it propped back up everything that got stepped on all day.
en.editorNote: Send it to a friend in service as proof that someone notices. Also a reminder for when you're the customer — those ten seconds are cheap.
variations: Some customers don't do anything special. They just clean up after themselves, and that alone is kindness.
"Long day, huh" doesn't change my paycheck. It changes what I replay before I fall asleep.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 服務業日常觀察，櫃檯看盡人生百態

zh-tw.content:
站在櫃檯後面第三年，
我看過分手、求婚、逃家的國中生、
和一個把整包零錢倒出來數了十分鐘的阿嬤。
這裡每天都在演一齣沒有劇本的連續劇，
而我是唯一那個不能笑場的演員。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合當作服務業朋友的貼文配文，或用在「這份工作教會我什麼」的分享。收銀機後面的視野，其實比很多人想的寬。
variations: 櫃檯是全世界最便宜的觀眾席，門票是我的下班時間。
我不是在收銀，我是在看一整條街的人生，一次一位。

en.content:
Three years behind this counter and I've watched
a breakup, a proposal, a runaway middle schooler,
and a grandma count out a whole bag of coins for ten minutes.
It's an unscripted drama running daily,
and I'm the one actor who isn't allowed to break character.
en.editorNote: Good caption for a service-industry friend's post, or for the "what this job taught me" genre. The view from behind a register is wider than people think.
variations: The counter is the cheapest theater seat in town. Admission is my evening.
I'm not ringing up groceries. I'm watching a whole street's worth of lives, one at a time.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 超商板：客人無法描述商品的日常對話

zh-tw.content:
「你們有沒有那個⋯⋯就那個啊。」
「請問是哪一個呢？」
「就上次那個啊，藍藍的。」
「上次是哪一次？」
「你怎麼會不知道？」
先生，我是店員，不是您的記憶體外接硬碟。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給零售、超商同事，笑一下就好。這種對話每天上演，重點從來不是商品，是那句理直氣壯的「你怎麼會不知道」。
variations: 客人：「就那個。」我：「哪個？」客人：「你們自己賣的東西你不知道？」我知道，我只是不知道『那個』。
全台灣最難解的謎題，是客人口中那個藍藍的、上次那個。

en.content:
"Do you guys have the, you know — that thing?"
"Which thing, sir?"
"The one from last time. It was blue."
"Which last time?"
"How do you not know?"
Sir, I'm a clerk, not an external hard drive for your memory.
en.editorNote: Send it to your retail coworkers for a quick laugh. This conversation runs daily, and the punchline is never the product — it's the total confidence behind "how do you not know."
variations: "That one." "Which one?" "You work here and you don't know your own stock?" I know the stock. I don't know "that one."
The hardest riddle in retail: the blue one, from that time.

items.sourceNote: 2026 負評勒索現象：奧客以 Google 一星負評要脅免單／退款，鋪成一個服務業新痛點角度

zh-tw.content:
「你再不退我錢，我就給你們一顆星。」
先生，那顆星我收下了。
您給的一星會被路人看穿，
而我守的規矩，會被同事記得。
您能砸的是評分，
砸不動的是我今天沒做錯這件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給被『一星負評』威脅過的店家或店員。重點不是評分幾顆，是把『你沒做錯』這件事講清楚——星星可以刷，良心不行。
variations: 客人：「我要給你一顆星。」我：「謝謝，這是您今天唯一沒有要求打折的東西。」
他以為一顆星能讓我低頭，其實看評論的人，都看得出誰在鬧。

en.content:
"Refund me or I'm leaving you one star."
Sir, I'll take the star.
Strangers reading it will see right through you,
and the rule I held will be remembered by my coworkers.
You can dent the rating.
You can't dent the fact that I did nothing wrong today.
en.editorNote: For any shop or clerk who's been threatened with a one-star review. It's not about the number of stars — it's about naming, out loud, that you did nothing wrong. Ratings can be gamed; a clear conscience can't.
variations: "I'm giving you one star." "Thanks — that's the only thing you didn't ask for a discount on today."
He thought one star would make me fold. But everyone reading reviews can tell who's throwing the tantrum.

items.sourceNote: 服務業被客人舉手機錄影、威脅『PO 上網讓你紅』的現場情境，改寫成新角度（前面題材未涵蓋直播／錄影）

zh-tw.content:
客人舉起手機對著我：「我錄下來了，要 PO 上網喔。」
請便，記得拍清楚——
畫面裡那個從頭到尾好好講話的，是我；
那個對著陌生人大吼的，是您。
您想讓我紅，
可惜鏡頭很誠實。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給被客人舉手機威脅過的服務業朋友。這年頭誰都能開錄影，但鏡頭不會替情緒說謊——好好講話的那個人，通常不是喊最大聲的那個。
variations: 客人：「我要 PO 上網喔！」我：「麻煩橫著拍，直的畫質不好。」
他以為錄影能威脅我，卻忘了鏡頭裡失控的那位，不是穿制服的。

en.content:
The customer aims his phone at me: "I'm recording this. Going straight online."
Go ahead — just film it clearly.
The one speaking calmly the whole time is me.
The one screaming at a stranger is you.
You want to make me go viral?
Too bad the camera's honest.
en.editorNote: For any service worker who's had a phone shoved in their face. Anyone can hit record now, but the lens doesn't lie for anyone's temper — the person speaking calmly usually isn't the one yelling.
variations: "I'm posting this online!" "Please film in landscape — portrait looks terrible."
He thought recording me was a threat. He forgot the one losing it on camera isn't wearing the uniform.

items.sourceNote: 櫃姐／服務業職業傷害：站八小時、不能坐、憋尿到膀胱發炎、靜脈曲張——把身體代價寫成有溫度的語錄（前面題材偏情緒，未寫身體）

zh-tw.content:
客人問我為什麼站著還能笑得這麼甜。
因為我的腿三年前就不是我的了，
它們替我撐著這份薪水。
下班脫下鞋的那一刻，
我才把腳還給自己——
這份工作最沉默的成本，
不是委屈，是我這雙再也直不起來的小腿。
zh-tw.editorNote: 獻給站整天、憋著沒空喝水的櫃姐、外場、店員。這行的痛不只在心裡，也在腿上、在膀胱裡。傳給那位總說『還好』的朋友，叫他今天記得坐下、喝口水。
variations: 同事問我腳還好嗎，我說還好——好到我已經忘了不痠是什麼感覺。
微笑是表演，靜脈曲張才是這份工作真正的年資證明。

en.content:
A customer asks how I still smile this sweetly on my feet all day.
Because my legs stopped being mine three years ago —
they hold up this paycheck for me.
Only when I pull off my shoes after clocking out
do I get my feet back.
The quietest cost of this job
isn't the humiliation. It's the calves that won't straighten anymore.
en.editorNote: For the counter staff, servers, and clerks who stand all day and never get a minute to drink water. The pain of this work isn't only in your chest — it's in your legs and your bladder. Send it to the friend who always says "I'm fine," and tell them to sit down and drink something today.
variations: A coworker asked if my feet were okay. I said fine — so fine I've forgotten what "not aching" feels like.
The smile is the performance. The varicose veins are the real proof of seniority.

items.sourceNote: 試吃／免費樣品被當正餐吃、還嫌切太小的服務業日常，改寫成新角度（前面未寫試吃 sample 題材）

zh-tw.content:
試吃區的客人吃完第五塊，
看著我說：「你們這切太小了吧。」
先生，那叫試吃，
不叫免費午餐吃到飽。
您試的是味道，
不是我今天的耐心底線。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給站試吃台、被『免費就要吃夠本』客人磨過的餐飲朋友。試吃的本意是嚐一口決定買不買，不是把一頓飯拆成十小塊來領。
variations: 客人試吃第八塊，我很想問：您是在試味道，還是在試我會不會翻臉？
試吃切小塊不是我小氣，是那本來就只夠您『試』，不夠您『吃』。

en.content:
The sample-stand customer finishes his fifth piece,
looks at me and says, "You cut these way too small."
Sir, it's called a sample,
not an all-you-can-eat free lunch.
You're tasting the flavor,
not testing the last of my patience today.
en.editorNote: For the food-service friends working the sample counter, worn down by the "if it's free I'll get my money's worth" crowd. A sample is one bite to decide whether to buy — not a meal broken into ten little pieces to collect.
variations: By his eighth sample I wanted to ask: are you tasting the food, or testing whether I'll snap?
The small pieces aren't me being stingy — they're just enough to "sample," not enough to "dine."

items.sourceNote: 自助結帳機普及後，客人仍全程叫店員代操作、最後反問『那還要你幹嘛』——前面未寫 self-checkout 題材，為新角度

zh-tw.content:
自助結帳機前，客人揮手叫我：
「這台我不會，你幫我用。」
我從頭刷到尾、幫他付好、裝好袋，
他轉頭說：「那還要這台機器幹嘛。」
先生，機器是給會用的人用的，
我是留下來收拾『不會用』的那部分。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被『自助結帳』四個字整到的零售朋友。機器省的是排隊，不是店員；真正被自動化的，從來不是那台會嗶的機器。
variations: 自助結帳的意思是您自己助自己，不是我隔著機器再服務您一次。
老闆買機器是想省一個人力，結果那個人力現在站在機器旁邊，服務不會用機器的人。

en.content:
At the self-checkout, the customer waves me over:
"I can't work this thing — you do it."
I scan it all, pay for him, bag it up,
and he goes: "So what's the machine even for?"
Sir, the machine is for people who can use it.
I'm the one left to clean up the "can't use it" part.
en.editorNote: For retail friends worn down by the words "self-checkout." The machine saves the line, not the clerk — and the thing that actually got automated was never the beeping box.
variations: "Self-checkout" means you check yourself out — not that I serve you a second time through a screen.
The boss bought the machine to save one headcount. That headcount now stands beside it, serving the people who can't use it.

items.sourceNote: 客人邊講電話邊點餐、抬手要店員安靜，餐點做錯又回頭怪店員——前面未寫『講電話點餐』題材

zh-tw.content:
客人一手貼著電話，
另一手抬起來要我閉嘴，
對我比了三根手指就走。
餐做好了，他回頭：「我不是點這個。」
先生，您剛剛在跟我點餐，
還是在跟電話那頭的人點？
我只能聽見我聽得見的那半句。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給常被『半通電話點餐』搞到做錯的餐飲朋友。你不是通靈的，客人吞進電話裡的那半句，本來就不該算在你頭上。
variations: 您用三根手指點的餐，我只能用三分猜的做。
點餐時請掛掉電話，不然我聽到的永遠是您人生的另一半劇情。

en.content:
One hand pressed to his phone,
the other raised to shush me,
he flashes three fingers and walks off.
The food's ready, he turns back: "That's not what I ordered."
Sir, were you ordering from me,
or from whoever's on the line?
I can only hear the half of the sentence I was allowed to hear.
en.editorNote: For food-service friends who keep getting orders "wrong" because they were placed through half a phone call. You're not a mind reader — the half the customer swallowed into his phone was never yours to get right.
variations: You ordered with three fingers, so I made it with three guesses.
Please hang up before you order — otherwise all I hear is the other half of your life's plot.

items.sourceNote: 回應『現在服務業態度越來越差』的社會討論，改寫成第一線員工的反思角度——區隔於前面既有的微笑盔甲題材

zh-tw.content:
客人說：「你們服務態度是不是越來越差？」
是啊，越來越差。
差在我終於學會，
把最好的笑容留給好好說話的人，
把剩下的力氣，留給下班後的自己。
態度沒有變差，
是我開始把它花在值得的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被『態度越來越差』一句話否定掉整天努力的服務業朋友。你的笑不是義務，是禮物；收回一份錯給的禮物，不叫變差，叫終於學會分辨。
variations: 不是我們態度變差，是我們終於捨得不對爛態度陪笑。
服務可以無限，尊重不行；您感覺到的『變差』，只是我把界線畫回原本該在的地方。

en.content:
The customer says, "Is your service getting worse or what?"
Yes. Worse and worse.
Worse because I've finally learned
to save my best smile for the ones who speak kindly,
and save what's left for myself after the shift.
The attitude didn't get worse —
I just started spending it where it's worth spending.
en.editorNote: For service friends whose whole day gets erased by one line: "your attitude's gotten worse." Your smile was never an obligation, it's a gift — taking back a gift given to the wrong person isn't getting worse, it's finally learning to tell them apart.
variations: It's not that our attitude got worse — we just stopped being willing to smile at a bad one.
Service can be unlimited; respect can't. The "worse" you feel is just me drawing the line back where it always belonged.

items.sourceNote: No-show/放鴿子 restaurant reservation trope — 2026 coverage of Taiwan's chronic no-show culture (518 職場熊報, NOM Magazine 餐廳心痛告白); no existing item covers reservations

zh-tw.content: 六個人的位子，週六晚上最好的那桌，/我幫您留了兩個小時。/推掉三組現場客，/看著空椅子等到打烊。/您沒來，也沒一通電話。/先生，您訂走的不是位子，/是我今晚整整六個人份的生意。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被放鴿子過的餐廳老闆跟外場。放鳥不是「反正我沒去消費」，是店家把黃金時段壓在你身上，你連一句取消都懶得說。
variations: 訂位不來又不取消，您省下的是一頓飯，我賠掉的是一整晚。
空著的那桌會自己算帳：三組被我推掉的客人，加上您那句沒說出口的『抱歉今天不去了』。

en.content:
A table for six, the best one, prime Saturday night —
I held it for you for two hours.
Turned away three walk-in groups,
watched the empty chairs until closing.
You never came. Never called.
You didn't just cancel a table —
you canceled a whole night's worth of six covers on me.
en.editorNote: Send this to any restaurant owner or host who's been stood up. A no-show isn't "I just didn't feel like going" — it's the shop betting its prime slot on you, and you not even bothering to text a cancellation.
variations: Skip the reservation without a word and you save one dinner; I eat a whole empty evening.
That empty table keeps its own ledger: three groups I turned away, plus the "sorry, not coming" you never sent.

items.sourceNote: Delivery-rider POV — Dcard 2025-12 「第一天做外送超血汗」 + rider rating culture; service-industry collection has no rider/外送 angle yet

zh-tw.content: 雨下得像不用錢，/我爬上沒有電梯的五樓，/敲門、等了三分鐘您才來開。/您接過餐第一句：「怎麼有點涼了？」/先生，涼的不是這份餐，/是我在您樓下淋的那十分鐘，/跟您給的那顆一星。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給風雨無阻的外送夥伴。他們的辛苦被壓縮成一顆星，而那顆星常常跟他們無關——是天氣、是電梯、是等你來開門的那三分鐘。
variations: 我準時到您樓下，是您讓那份餐等了三分鐘才涼的。
外送這行最公平的地方是給小費，最不公平的是打分數——一顆星不會問你當天下多大的雨。

en.content:
The rain's coming down like it's free,
I climb five floors with no elevator,
knock, wait three minutes for you to open.
First thing you say taking the bag: "This is kind of cold?"
Sir, it's not the food that went cold —
it's the ten minutes I stood in the rain downstairs,
and the one star you just gave me.
en.editorNote: For every delivery rider out in all weather. Their whole shift gets flattened into one star — and that star is usually about the weather, the elevator, or the three minutes you took to answer the door, not them.
variations: I got to your building on time; you're the one who let it sit three minutes and go cold.
The fairest thing about this job is the tip; the cruelest is the rating — one star never asks how hard it was raining.

items.sourceNote: Working the holiday while everyone else reunites — Dcard 服務業辛酸史; no existing item covers 過年/連假 emotional core (svc-035 is scheduling for weddings)

zh-tw.content: 除夕夜，全世界都在吃團圓飯，/我在櫃檯，把「新年快樂」說了一百次，/收下一百個沒空回頭的背影。/我家的那桌，也留了我的位子——/只是它跟客人的桌子一樣，/都得等我打烊，才輪得到我坐下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給連假、過年還在上班的服務業朋友。別人的團圓，是靠有人放棄自己的團圓撐起來的。你今天扛的不只是班，是別人的年味。
variations: 過年最忙的不是廚房，是把「回不了家」四個字吞下去還要笑著找錢。
全家都在守歲，我在守櫃台——同一個夜晚，兩種等待。

en.content:
New Year's Eve, the whole world's at the reunion dinner,
and I'm at the counter, saying "Happy New Year" a hundred times,
collecting a hundred backs that never turn around.
My family saved me a seat too —
it's just like the customers' tables:
I don't get to sit down until we close.
en.editorNote: For anyone working the holidays while everyone else is home. Other people's reunions are held up by someone giving up their own. What you're carrying today isn't just a shift — it's the holiday itself, for everybody else.
variations: The busiest thing on New Year's isn't the kitchen — it's swallowing "I can't go home" and still smiling as you count out change.
The whole family's up celebrating; I'm up minding the register — same night, two kinds of waiting.

items.sourceNote: Customer falsely insisting they were shortchanged — classic register 奧客 scenario; not covered (svc-180 is about coins rolling off the counter, different core)

zh-tw.content: 「你少找我五百。」/「先生，您給我一千，找您三百二十。」/「我明明給你一千五。」/我打開收銀機，抽屜裡沒有一張一千五的鈔票，/監視器也沒有。/唯一有一張一千五的地方，/是您希望我沒膽對帳的那個賭注。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被硬凹少找錢的收銀夥伴。他賭的不是那五百，是賭你會為了息事寧人自己掏。守住收銀機，就是守住一件你今天沒做錯的事。
variations: 『你少找我』這句話，通常跟『我朋友比較便宜』住在同一個查無此人的區。
少找的五百我找不到，因為它從來只存在您的說法裡，不在我的抽屜裡。

en.content:
"You shorted me five hundred."
"Sir, you gave me a thousand, I gave you back three-twenty."
"No, I definitely handed you fifteen hundred."
I open the register — there's no fifteen-hundred bill in the drawer,
and none on the camera.
The only place a fifteen-hundred exists
is the bet you're making that I won't dare check.
en.editorNote: For every cashier strong-armed over "wrong change." They're not betting on the five hundred — they're betting you'll pay it out of your own pocket to make them go away. Standing by the register is standing by the one thing you didn't get wrong today.
variations: "You shorted me" usually lives in the same no-record-found zip code as "my friend got it cheaper."
I can't find the missing five hundred, because it only ever existed in your version — never in my drawer.

items.sourceNote: 2026-07 颱風期間全市百貨僅一家開館、員工被要求出勤引發論戰的新聞討論；檔案內原本沒有颱風／天災出勤題材

zh-tw.content:
風大到招牌在叫，
捷運停駛，路樹倒了一整排，
我還是穿上制服來開櫃。
因為今天全市只有我們有開。
您走進來說：「難得放假，出來走走。」
先生，您的颱風假，
是拿我的颱風班換來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給颱風天還被要求出勤的百貨、門市夥伴。你不是「順便來上班」，你是別人休假日的電梯、冷氣和收銀機。記得：業績再好看，也沒有你平安到家重要。
variations: 「今天有開嗎？」有，因為有人冒著風雨替您開。
全市停業那天最忙的不是氣象局，是唯一沒停業的那家店的樓面。

en.content:
The wind is loud enough to make the signage scream,
the trains are stopped, a whole row of street trees is down,
and I still put on the uniform and open the counter.
Because today we're the only place in the city that's open.
You walk in and say, "Rare day off — figured we'd get out of the house."
Sir, your typhoon day off
was paid for with my typhoon shift.
en.editorNote: For everyone made to work through a storm so a store can stay open. You're not "just clocking in" — you're the elevator, the AC, and the register of somebody else's day off. No sales figure is worth more than you getting home safe.
variations: "Are you open today?" We are — because somebody rode out the storm to open us.
On the day the whole city closes, the busiest people aren't at the weather bureau. They're on the floor of the one store that didn't.

items.sourceNote: 2026-07 報導：天熱手搖飲外送訂單較去年同期成長逾四成、午間為下訂高峰；改寫為飲料店員視角。既有冰塊／甜度題材（svc-002、svc-148、svc-242、svc-251）都是客人矛盾要求，本則核心是尖峰爆單，不重複

zh-tw.content:
外面三十九度，
店裡的封口機比我還燙。
外送單一張接一張吐出來，
像一條用收據做的瀑布。
客人在門口探頭：「怎麼那麼慢？」
因為在您前面，
還有四十七杯跟您一樣渴的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給夏天被外送單淹沒的飲料店夥伴。單子噴出來的速度不是你決定的，但每一杯都是你親手搖的——慢的不是你，是這個夏天。
variations: 夏天的手搖店沒有尖峰，只有一條從中午拉到打烊的直線。
您在等一杯飲料，我在等那台出單機閉嘴三十秒。

en.content:
It's a hundred and two outside,
and the sealing machine is running hotter than I am.
Delivery tickets keep spitting out, one after another,
a waterfall made of receipt paper.
A customer leans in the door: "What's taking so long?"
Because ahead of you
there are forty-seven other people exactly this thirsty.
en.editorNote: For every boba shop crew buried under summer delivery orders. You don't control how fast the tickets print, but every single cup gets shaken by your hands. It's not you that's slow — it's the summer.
variations: There's no rush hour at a drink shop in July, just one flat line from noon to close.
You're waiting on one drink. I'm waiting for that printer to shut up for thirty seconds.

items.sourceNote: 暑假「一杯坐整天」佔位客題材，取自服務業討論串；檔案內「座位／內用久坐」尚無題材（svc-041 是被彈手指叫人，核心不同）

zh-tw.content:
一杯最小杯的冰美式，
從開店坐到打烊，
筆電、延長線、還外加一句「可以請他們小聲一點嗎」。
先生，這裡是店，不是您家的書房。
我不介意您吹冷氣，
我介意的是您把我當成
這杯咖啡附贈的靜音功能。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給暑假被長期佔位搞到翻桌率歸零的咖啡店、速食店夥伴。座位是店家實實在在的成本，不是無限暢飲的公共財；願意讓人坐是好意，不是義務。
variations: 冰美式的續杯上限是零，冷氣不是。
我們很歡迎您坐，只是那張椅子今天也有它自己的業績要跑。

en.content:
One small iced americano,
parked from open to close —
laptop, power strip, plus "could you ask them to keep it down?"
Sir, this is a shop, not the study in your house.
I don't mind you enjoying the AC.
I mind that you've decided I'm
the mute button that came free with the coffee.
en.editorNote: For cafe and fast-food crews whose summer table turnover has flatlined. Seats are a real cost the shop pays, not a public utility with free refills. Letting you stay is a kindness, not an obligation.
variations: The refill limit on an iced americano is zero. The AC's isn't.
You're welcome to sit — it's just that the chair has sales targets today too.

items.sourceNote: 暑期工讀生被客訴、資深同事出面擋下的暖心角度；svc-085 是新人被罵的笑話，本則核心是資深者的保護與傳承，不重複

zh-tw.content:
暑假來的工讀生被客人指著鼻子罵，
我把她拉到我身後，
說：「這位先生，這一班我負責。」
她小聲說學姐對不起。
傻瓜，你沒有做錯。
我擋在你前面，
不是因為我比較厲害，
是因為當年沒有人擋在我前面。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給願意替新人擋一句話的資深夥伴。服務業真正的傳承不是教人怎麼結帳，是教人「被罵不等於做錯」。你擋下的那一句，很可能就留住了一個人。
variations: 帶新人最重要的一課不是 SOP，是「客人罵你的時候，我會在」。
我沒辦法讓你不被罵，但我可以讓你不是一個人被罵。

en.content:
A customer is jabbing a finger at our summer part-timer,
so I pull her behind me and say,
"Sir, this shift is mine. Talk to me."
Afterward she whispers that she's sorry.
Sweetheart, you did nothing wrong.
I stepped in front of you
not because I'm tougher,
but because nobody stepped in front of me.
en.editorNote: For every veteran who takes the hit for a new kid. What actually gets passed down in this industry isn't how to work a register — it's that being yelled at is not the same as being wrong. The line you absorb might be the reason they stay.
variations: The most important thing you teach a new hire isn't the SOP. It's "when they yell at you, I'll be there."
I can't keep you from getting yelled at, but I can keep you from getting yelled at alone.

items.sourceNote: 夏季跳電／系統當機仍須營業的門市情境，取自服務業第一線壓力報導；檔案內尚無停電、設備故障題材

zh-tw.content:
三十八度的下午，冷氣跳電，
收銀機黑掉，只能拿紙筆記帳，
我一邊流汗一邊道歉。
客人說：「你們也太不專業。」
先生，如果專業的定義包含發電，
那我下班先去應徵台電。
我做得到的，是在沒有冷氣的店裡，
還把您的找零算對。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給遇過跳電、系統當機還得硬撐營業的門市夥伴。設備壞掉不是你的錯，但收場的永遠是你——留一點力氣給自己，別連停電都跟人道歉。
variations: 停電的時候，全店最先恢復運作的永遠是店員的嘴，不是電。
系統當機我可以手寫，冷氣停了我可以流汗，但請別把電力公司的帳算到我頭上。

en.content:
A hundred degrees out, and the AC trips the breaker.
The register goes dark, so we're on pen and paper,
and I'm apologizing while sweating through my shirt.
The customer says, "Wow, so unprofessional."
Sir, if professionalism includes generating electricity,
I'll go apply at the power company after my shift.
What I can do is get your change right
in a store with no air conditioning.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's kept a store running through an outage or a system crash. Broken equipment isn't your fault, but you're always the one who cleans it up — save a little energy for yourself, and don't apologize for the power grid.
variations: During a blackout, the first thing in the store to come back online is always the clerk's mouth, never the power.
I'll handwrite receipts when the system dies and sweat through the heat when the AC quits — just don't put the utility company's bill on my tab.

items.sourceNote: Sparked by NOWnews 可不可店員「不爽客人打烊前點餐」 controversy; rewritten from the worker's POV as a closing-time monologue, no incident details copied

zh-tw.content:
門上寫十點打烊。
九點五十九，您推門進來，
說：「還沒關吧？隨便點一下就好。」
先生，「隨便一下」是您的三分鐘，
是我的洗鍋、關機、拖地、還有回不去的末班車。
我沒有不歡迎您，
我只是也想準時把今天還給自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天都要跟「最後一分鐘客人」拔河的餐飲夥伴。打烊時間不是參考值，是有人在那頭等著他回家。
variations: 「隨便點一下」這四個字，從來沒有一次是真的隨便。
客人的最後一單，通常是我今晚睡眠的第一筆扣款。

en.content:
The sign says we close at ten.
At 9:59 you push the door open and say,
"You're not closed yet, right? I'll just grab something quick."
Sir, your "quick" is three minutes.
Mine is the scrubbed pans, the shutdown, the mopping, and the last bus I won't catch.
I'm not turning you away —
I'd just like to hand today back to myself on time too.
en.editorNote: For anyone in food service who plays tug-of-war with the last-minute customer every night. Closing time isn't a suggestion — someone on the other end of it is waiting to go home.
variations: "I'll just grab something quick" has never once actually been quick.
The customer's last order is usually the first withdrawal from tonight's sleep.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 104 職場力 「每一種客制化服務都有價」 article on unpaid extra service; rewritten as a service-fee comeback, original phrasing

zh-tw.content:
「收什麼服務費，你們是有服務到什麼？」
先生，剛剛幫您併桌、加水三次、
換掉您嫌太吵的位子、
還把您小孩打翻的那杯默默擦乾淨的，
就是那個「什麼」。
服務不是沒發生，
是它做得太順，順到您以為它免費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被嫌「服務費收假的」的外場夥伴。做得好的服務常常隱形——安靜到客人以為那是空氣，其實那是有人在忙。
variations: 服務費最尷尬的地方，是它證明你做得越好，客人越覺得你沒做事。
「你們有服務到什麼」——有啊，服務到您有空好好問這句話。

en.content:
"A service charge? What service did you even do?"
Sir, the table we pushed together for you, the water refilled three times,
the seat we swapped when you said it was too loud,
and the drink your kid knocked over that we quietly wiped up —
that's the "what."
The service didn't fail to happen.
It happened so smoothly you assumed it was free.
en.editorNote: For the floor staff who get told the service charge is a scam. Good service is often invisible — quiet enough that the customer mistakes it for air, when really it's someone hustling.
variations: The awkward thing about a service charge is that the better you do the job, the more the customer thinks you did nothing.
"What service did you do?" — enough that you had the free time to stand there and ask.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Dcard 職場篇 「服務業的邊界」 post; the restroom-without-purchase boundary is a canonical retail scenario, freshly written

zh-tw.content:
客人衝進來：「廁所借一下！」
用完出來，經過我，
頭也不回地走出門。
我沒有要您買東西，
我只是有點希望，
進來時那句「借一下」，
出去時能變成一句「謝謝」。
這家店不是收費的，
但基本的來回，是我唯一的找零。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給常被當成「免費公廁管理員」的門市夥伴。不是計較那一次廁所，是那句連頭都不回的無視，比奧客的大小聲還涼。
variations: 客人的「借一下」很大聲，出門的那聲「謝謝」通常太小聲，小聲到不存在。
我不介意借您廁所，我介意的是您把整間店當成理所當然。

en.content:
A customer bursts in: "Can I use your restroom?"
Comes out, walks past me,
and leaves without a glance back.
I wasn't asking you to buy anything.
I just quietly hoped
that the "can I" on the way in
would become a "thanks" on the way out.
This store doesn't charge for it —
but a little back-and-forth is the only change I get.
en.editorNote: For the retail folks treated like unpaid public-restroom attendants. It's not about the one restroom trip — it's that the glance-free walk-out lands colder than any yelling customer.
variations: The "can I" on the way in is always loud; the "thanks" on the way out is usually too quiet to exist.
I don't mind lending you the restroom. I mind you treating the whole store like it owes you one.

items.sourceNote: Original scenario extending the Dcard 「做服務業的人都在想什麼」 motif; the endless photo-retake request is a common café/tourist-spot experience, freshly written

zh-tw.content:
「不好意思，幫我們拍一張。」
第一張，說眼睛閉了。
第二張，說想換直的。
第八張，開始指導我要蹲低、要仰角、
要把後面那盞燈拍進來。
先生，我是店員，
不是您這趟旅行的隨行攝影師。
您的回憶很重要，
但我後面還有五桌，也很重要。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被無限重拍綁架過的外場夥伴。幫拍一張是人情，拍到會操作單眼是義務——這兩件事中間，隔著五桌等上菜的客人。
variations: 從「幫我拍一張」到「這樣不行再一張」，中間隔了我整個休息時間。
客人的第一張是請託，第八張是外包，我沒簽這份合約。

en.content:
"Excuse me, could you take one photo of us?"
First shot: someone blinked.
Second: they want it vertical.
By the eighth, they're directing me — crouch lower, tilt up,
get that light in the background.
Sir, I'm a store clerk,
not the official photographer for your trip.
Your memories matter,
but so do the five tables waiting behind me.
en.editorNote: For the floor staff hijacked by the endless-retake request. Taking one photo is a kindness; being coached into a full photoshoot is a job — and between the two sit five tables waiting on their food.
variations: From "take one photo" to "no, one more like this" is exactly the length of my entire break.
The first shot is a favor, the eighth is outsourcing, and I never signed that contract.

items.sourceNote: Bored Panda hospitality-worker encounters thread — the 'customer switches face between counters' behavior is a recurring theme; rewritten as a two-faced-customer scenario

zh-tw.content:
剛剛在隔壁櫃檯，
他把我同事罵到眼眶紅，
轉過來到我這，
聲音突然軟成一團棉花：
「小姐，麻煩妳囉，謝謝喔。」
先生，我親眼看到您三十秒前那張臉，
那張臉才是您，
這張是您裝的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給剛在隔壁看完一場、輪到自己還要笑臉相迎的夥伴。奧客最恐怖的不是兇，是他選擇性地兇——代表他其實控制得了，只是不想對你客氣。
variations: 會看人下菜單的客人，最不缺的就是那張隨時能收回去的笑臉。
他對我同事的音量，才是他真正的音量；對我的溫柔，只是換了個對象繼續演。

en.content:
Thirty seconds ago at the next counter,
he made my coworker's eyes go red.
Then he turned to me,
and his voice melted into cotton:
"Miss, so sorry to trouble you, thank you."
Sir, I saw the face you had a moment ago —
that one's the real you,
this one's the costume.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who just watched the show at the next register and now has to smile for the same guy. The scary part of a difficult customer isn't the yelling — it's that they pick who gets it, which means they could always have chosen not to.
variations: A customer who's polite to some and cruel to others isn't out of control — he's just decided you don't rate the kindness.
The volume he used on my coworker is his real volume; the sweetness he uses on me is the same act with a new audience.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 工作板 service-industry venting thread — the 'I'm in a hurry so let me cut in, then can't decide' contradiction is a common 奧客 complaint; rewritten fresh

zh-tw.content:
「我很趕，先幫我用可以嗎？」
我讓他插了隊。
然後他站在櫃檯前，
菜單看了兩分鐘、
打了三通電話問家人要吃什麼、
最後說：「那我再想一下。」
先生，您趕的到底是什麼？
是我後面那八個人的時間吧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被『我很急』開頭插隊、結果對方比誰都慢的夥伴。真正趕時間的人不會需要重看三次菜單——他們只是覺得自己的時間比別人的貴。
variations: 說「我很趕」的客人，通常趕的是別人的耐心，不是自己的行程。
您插的不是隊，是我後面每一個安靜等著、卻沒喊「我很急」的人的善良。

en.content:
"I'm in a rush — can you take me first?"
So I let him cut the line.
Then he stood at the counter,
stared at the menu for two minutes,
made three calls asking his family what they wanted,
