and finally said, "Let me think a bit more."
Sir, what exactly are you in a rush for?
Oh — the time of the eight people behind you.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who let someone cut in on 'I'm in a hurry' and then watched them move slower than anyone. People who are actually in a rush don't need to read the menu three times — they just think their time costs more than everyone else's.
variations: The customer who says 'I'm in a rush' is usually rushing everyone else's patience, not his own schedule.
You didn't cut a line — you cut in front of every quiet person behind you who was in just as much of a hurry and didn't say so.

items.sourceNote: Pleated-Jeans entitled-customer stories roundup — the 'I know it's not your fault, but...' disclaimer that precedes ten minutes of blame is a widely-shared trope; rewritten from worker POV

zh-tw.content:
「我知道這不是妳的錯——」
每次聽到這句開頭我都會抖一下，
因為接下來的十分鐘，
他就是要把那個「不是妳的錯」，
一句一句罵到妳身上。
先生，您都知道不是我的錯了，
那我們可以直接跳到解決問題嗎？
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被『我知道不是你的錯』當開場白、然後照樣挨罵十分鐘的客服夥伴。這句話從來不是體諒，是預告——他知道罵錯人，但還是選擇罵你。
variations: 「我知道不是妳的錯」後面接的「但是」，才是他真正想說的那句。
承認不是我的錯只花了三秒，把火出在我身上卻花了十分鐘——這道數學我算不平。

en.content:
"I know this isn't your fault, but—"
I flinch every time I hear that opener,
because the next ten minutes
are him taking that "not your fault"
and aiming it, line by line, straight at me.
Sir, if you already know it's not my fault,
can we just skip to fixing the problem?
en.editorNote: For the support agent who gets 'I know it's not your fault' as an opener and then eats ten minutes of blame anyway. That line was never sympathy — it's a warning label. He knows he's yelling at the wrong person and does it anyway.
variations: The word that matters in 'I know it's not your fault, but' is the 'but' — that's the part he actually meant.
Admitting it's not my fault took him three seconds; taking it out on me took ten minutes. That math doesn't balance.

items.sourceNote: 518 職場熊報 客訴-handling article — the customer who re-asks the same question hoping the policy will change is a common frontline scenario; rewritten fresh

zh-tw.content:
「所以真的不能退喔？」
「是的，超過期限了。」
「……那如果我說我很需要呢？」
「還是不行喔。」
「那我再問一次，真的不行？」
先生，我的答案不會因為您問第三次就改口，
我又不是自動販賣機，
投多幾次幣就掉不一樣的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被同一個問題輪番轟炸、答案講到自己都會背的夥伴。客人重複問，不是沒聽懂，是想用耐心磨掉你的規矩——別讓他磨成功。
variations: 同一個問題問三次，答案不會變，變的只有我的耐心存量。
規定不是我心情，不會您問得夠可憐它就自己鬆動。

en.content:
"So you really can't refund it?"
"Correct, it's past the window."
"...but what if I said I really need it?"
"Still no."
"Okay, let me ask one more time — really no?"
Sir, my answer doesn't change because you asked a third time.
I'm not a vending machine
that drops something different if you keep feeding it coins.
en.editorNote: For the coworker getting hit with the same question on a loop until they could recite the answer in their sleep. Re-asking isn't confusion — it's an attempt to wear down your policy with persistence. Don't let it work.
variations: Ask the same question three times and the answer won't change — only my patience reserves will.
The policy isn't my mood; it doesn't loosen just because you ask it sadly enough.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by TwistedSifter retail stories about kids destroying merchandise while parents claim the item was 'already defective'; rewritten into a zh-tw counter scene

zh-tw.content:
「你們這個本來就壞的吧？」
是您小孩剛剛拿起來、
砸在地上、再踩兩腳的那個。
先生，商品不會通靈，
它不會自己知道要在您進門前就壞掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種「小孩在店裡橫衝直撞、家長全程滑手機」的同業。孩子弄壞不可怕，可怕的是家長把「我沒看到」練成一句免責咒語。
variations: 您說「本來就壞」，那是壞在您小孩的手上，還是壞在您裝沒看到的那雙眼睛裡。
商品可以賠，我今天彎腰撿碎片的膝蓋，帳單上沒有那一欄。

en.content:
"This was already broken, right?"
It's the one your kid grabbed,
slammed on the floor, then stomped on twice.
Sir, merchandise isn't psychic —
it doesn't know to break itself before you walk in.
en.editorNote: For the coworker whose store turns into a demolition derby while the parent scrolls their phone. Kids breaking things isn't the crime — it's the parent who's trained "I didn't see it" into a get-out-of-jail spell.
variations: You say "already broken." Broken in your kid's hands, or broken in the eyes you kept pointed at your phone?
The product I can write off. The knees I bent to sweep up the pieces don't get a line on anyone's invoice.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 殺價 topic — customers haggling inside fixed-price stores is a recurring frontline complaint; rewritten fresh

zh-tw.content:
「這個算我便宜一點啦。」
「不好意思，我們是定價的。」
「你就少賺一點會怎樣？」
先生，這裡不是夜市，
牌子上那個數字不是開場價，
是句號。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給在「明碼標價」的店裡還天天被凹折扣的夥伴。殺價的人不是缺那幾十塊，是想確認你會不會為了成交，把自尊也一起打折。
variations: 我沒有把價格改低的權限，我只有微笑著把原價再講一次的權限。
「少賺一點」聽起來很輕鬆，那是因為要少的不是您的薪水。

en.content:
"Come on, cut me a little deal."
"Sorry, our prices are fixed."
"What's it gonna hurt to make a little less?"
Sir, this isn't a night market —
that number on the tag isn't an opening bid,
it's a period.
en.editorNote: For anyone haggled at daily inside a store with the price printed right there. Hagglers aren't short the few bucks — they're testing whether you'll mark down your own dignity to close the sale.
variations: I don't have the authority to lower the price. I only have the authority to smile and say it again.
"Make a little less" sounds easy — because the "less" isn't coming out of your paycheck.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by retail wear-and-return stories (worn once, insists 'brand new'); rewritten as an apparel-counter scene distinct from svc-003

zh-tw.content:
「這件我要退。」
標籤被塞回領口，
袖口有藏不住的一整晚，
還帶著昨天那場聚餐的味道。
「全新的喔，沒穿過。」
小姐，衣服不會說謊，
是您以為我不會看。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給收過「穿一次就來退、還堅稱全新」的門市朋友。難的從來不是判斷有沒有穿過，是要用最客氣的語氣，戳破對方以為天衣無縫的那個謊。
variations: 「沒穿過」三個字，被袖口那圈痕跡當場拆穿。
退貨政策保障的是您後悔的權利，不是您把我當瞎子的權利。

en.content:
"I'd like to return this."
Tag tucked back into the collar,
one whole evening soaked into the cuffs,
still carrying last night's dinner.
"Brand new, never worn."
Ma'am, the clothes don't lie —
you just assumed I wouldn't look.
en.editorNote: For the shop worker who's taken back a "never worn" item that's clearly been worn once. The hard part isn't spotting the wear — it's puncturing a lie the customer thought was seamless, in your most polite voice.
variations: "Never worn" — undone on the spot by the ring worn into the cuff.
The return policy protects your right to change your mind, not your right to treat me as blind.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 服務業甘苦談 — being treated as the block's free info desk (directions, recommendations) is a common frontline gripe; rewritten fresh

zh-tw.content:
「小姐，前面那家藥局怎麼走？」
「捷運出口在哪？」
「附近有沒有好吃的？」
我這個櫃檯，
默默兼了觀光服務中心、
Google 地圖，還有美食評論家，
薪水卻只有一份，
還是最基本的那一份。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給店門口天天被當成「人肉導覽機」的夥伴。回答一句沒什麼，累的是那句「謝謝」常常被省略，人就走了，好像你本來就內建在這條街上。
variations: 我知道整條街怎麼走，唯獨不知道我的休息時間什麼時候才能開始。
免費問路、免費推薦、免費指路——這條街最佛心的服務台，時薪裡沒有這幾項。

en.content:
"Miss, how do I get to the pharmacy up the street?"
"Where's the subway exit?"
"Anywhere good to eat around here?"
This counter of mine
quietly moonlights as a tourist info booth,
Google Maps, and a food critic —
for one paycheck,
the entry-level one.
en.editorNote: For the worker treated as the block's human information kiosk. Answering is no big deal — what wears you down is the "thanks" that usually gets skipped as they walk off, like you came pre-installed on this street.
variations: I know how to get everywhere on this street — except to the start of my own break.
Free directions, free recs, free wayfinding — the most generous info desk on the block, and none of it's in my wage.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 奧客 topic — the 'you recommend' then 'you gave me a bad rec' blame-shift is a common food-service scenario; rewritten fresh

zh-tw.content:
「你們哪個最好吃？」
「這個滿多人回購的。」
（吃一口）
「還好而已啊，你亂推薦。」
先生，我推的是大家的口味，
不是您的舌頭，
下次麻煩把「我不喜歡」
翻譯成「我不喜歡」，
不要翻成「你的錯」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天被「你推薦一下」拱上台、結果不合胃口就被回收檢討的夥伴。推薦是好意借給你的，不是拿來當事後究責的靶。
variations: 您要我推薦，又要我保證您一定喜歡，這兩件事我只能做到一半，而且是免費的那一半。
「你亂推薦」的意思，常常是「我不想承認是我自己選的」。

en.content:
"Which one's your best?"
"This one gets a lot of repeat orders."
(one bite)
"It's just okay — you gave me a bad rec."
Sir, I recommended the crowd's taste,
not your tongue.
Next time please translate "I don't like it"
as "I don't like it,"
not as "your fault."
en.editorNote: For the coworker pushed onstage with "just recommend something," then blamed when it doesn't hit. A recommendation is a favor lent to you, not a target for after-the-fact blame.
variations: You want a recommendation AND a guarantee you'll love it — I can only do half of that, and it's the free half.
"You gave me a bad rec" usually means "I don't want to admit I'm the one who chose."

items.sourceNote: 2026 客服現場常見情境：客人拿 AI 聊天機器人給的錯誤承諾要求兌現；檔案內 AI 題材（svc-094 對機器人有禮貌、svc-197 機器人接簡單問題）核心不同，本則是真人替 AI 的錯誤道歉

zh-tw.content:
「你們的 AI 說可以全額退。」
我調出對話紀錄，
那句話是機器人昨天半夜自己掰的。
先生，我很想幫您，
可是公司把嘴巴外包給了 AI，
只留下我這張臉，
負責當著您的面把話收回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在收 AI 客服爛攤子的客服夥伴。客人不是無理取鬧，他真的被答應了——只是答應他的那個東西不會被扣考績，站在最前面挨罵的還是人。
variations: 機器人答應的事，為什麼要真人來道歉？因為機器人不會被寫進當月的考核表。
系統升級了，話術升級了，唯一沒升級的，是負責善後的那個人。

en.content:
"Your AI told me I'd get a full refund."
I pull up the chat log —
the bot invented that at 2 a.m.
Sir, I really want to help,
but the company outsourced its mouth to an AI
and kept only my face,
to take the promise back to yours.
en.editorNote: For the agent cleaning up after a chatbot's confidently wrong answer. The customer isn't making it up — he really was promised. The thing that promised him just doesn't get a performance review.
variations: Why does a human have to apologize for what the bot promised? Because the bot never lands on anyone's quarterly review.
The system got an upgrade. The script got an upgrade. The person cleaning up after both did not.

items.sourceNote: 2026-07 熱浪期間餐廳內場高溫報導；改寫為內場／外場溫差視角。svc-274 是跳電、svc-166／227 是出餐慢，核心不同

zh-tw.content:
外場二十四度，內場四十一度。
爐火在我左邊，蒸氣在我右邊，
制服濕到可以擰出今天的中午。
客人探頭進來說：
「在冷氣房工作很爽吼。」
先生，這道牆的兩邊，
是兩個不同的季節。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給整個夏天站在爐前的內場夥伴。同一家店，客人吹的和你站的中間只隔一道牆，溫度卻差了十幾度——沒被看見，不代表沒發生。
variations: 我們把冷氣讓給客人，把溫度留給自己。那是默契，不是應該。
這件制服今天洗第二次了，不是它髒，是它替我把整個夏天吸走了。

en.content:
Front of house: 75 degrees. Back of house: 106.
Flame on my left, steam on my right,
uniform wet enough to wring the afternoon out of.
A customer leans in:
"Must be nice, working in the A/C."
Sir, the two sides of this wall
are two different seasons.
en.editorNote: For the back-of-house crew standing at the range all summer. Same restaurant, one wall, thirty degrees apart. Invisible doesn't mean it isn't happening.
variations: We give the cold air to the dining room and keep the temperature for ourselves. That's a habit, not a duty.
Second wash for this uniform today. It isn't dirty — it just absorbed the whole summer for me.

items.sourceNote: 2026-07 熱浪期間外送平台與騎手處境報導；改寫為「訂單外的追加任務＋評價要脅」情境。svc-267 是雨天爬樓被嫌餐涼、svc-271 是尖峰爆單，核心不同

zh-tw.content:
「餐放門口，順便幫我把這袋垃圾帶下去。」
「經過超商幫我買包菸，錢再給你。」
「不然評價就……你知道的。」
先生，我送的是那份餐，
不是您今天不想下樓的所有理由。
那顆星是用來評價一份餐的，
不是用來牽著人走的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天被追加任務、還被評價綁架的外送夥伴。幫忙是心意，不是內建服務——一顆星可以評價餐點，不該拿來換那些從來不在單子上的事。
variations: 訂單上寫的是餐點內容，不是我今天願意被使喚到多遠。
「不然我給你一星喔」這句一出口，「順便」就不叫順便了。

en.content:
"Leave it at the door — and take this trash bag down on your way."
"Stop at the store and grab me a pack of smokes, I'll pay you back."
"Otherwise the rating might, you know..."
Sir, I delivered the food.
I didn't deliver every reason you didn't want to go downstairs today.
That star rates a meal.
It isn't a leash.
en.editorNote: For riders getting bonus errands stapled onto a delivery with the rating held overhead. A favor is a favor — the second a star gets attached, "while you're here" stops being a request.
variations: The order lists the food. It doesn't list how far I can be sent for the same fee.
"Or I might have to leave one star" — the moment that's said, it isn't a favor anymore.

items.sourceNote: 夏季外場「冷氣戰爭」情境：同時收到嫌冷與嫌熱的抱怨。檔案內冷氣題材（svc-102 借冷氣久坐、svc-274 跳電）核心不同

zh-tw.content:
三桌喊冷，七桌喊熱，
九桌說有風一直吹到她的湯。
我手上只有一支遙控器，
和一個一定會得罪人的溫度。
外面三十八度，
店裡的天氣，卻要我一個人負責。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天被夾在冷氣戰爭中間的外場夥伴。溫度只有一個，體感有幾十種，最後被檢討的永遠是那個最沒有決定權的人。
variations: 我可以調冷氣，但我調不動每個人的體感，那支遙控器沒有那顆按鈕。
「你們冷氣太強」和「你們冷氣太弱」，常常發生在同一個晚上、同一台機器。

en.content:
Table 3 says it's freezing.
Table 7 says it's boiling.
Table 9 says the vent is blowing on her soup.
I have one remote
and one temperature guaranteed to offend somebody.
It's 100 degrees outside,
and somehow the weather in here is my personal fault.
en.editorNote: For the floor staff stuck in the daily thermostat war. One temperature, forty different body clocks, and the blame always lands on whoever has the least say over the remote.
variations: I can change the thermostat. I can't change how forty people feel. The remote doesn't have that button.
"Too cold in here" and "too warm in here" routinely arrive the same night, about the same machine.

items.sourceNote: 暑假旺季全員禁休的排班情境。svc-035 是排班決定人生規劃、svc-048 是人力不足，本則核心是旺季看著別人放暑假

zh-tw.content:
七月的班表貼出來，
右上角四個紅字：暫停排休。
朋友傳來海邊的照片問我去不去，
我把手機翻過來，繼續補貨。
別人的夏天在海邊，
我的夏天在班表上，
被畫成一整排連在一起的早班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給旺季全員禁休、只能看別人限時動態過暑假的夥伴。不是不想去，是這個月的日曆從貼出班表那天起就不歸自己管了。
variations: 我的暑假不是沒有，是被排在十月，而且還要看那時候缺不缺人。
限時動態看得到海，班表上看不到假。

en.content:
The July schedule goes up.
Four red words in the corner:
NO TIME OFF APPROVED.
A friend sends a beach photo, asks if I'm coming.
I turn my phone face down and keep restocking.
Everyone else's summer is at the shore.
Mine is on the schedule,
drawn as one unbroken row of openings.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose entire summer got blacked out because it's peak season. It's not that you don't want to go — the calendar stopped being yours the day that schedule went up.
variations: I do get a summer. It's in October, pending whether we're short-staffed.
The stories show me the ocean. The schedule shows me no days off.

items.sourceNote: 超商結帳時客人堅持載具已綁在行動支付裡、店員解釋機器分開感應仍鬼打牆的討論。檔內無載具／電子發票題材，svc-002 是點餐誤解、svc-054 是別家禮券，本則核心是客人自己的需求在同一次結帳裡改了三個版本

zh-tw.content:
「我載具綁在手機支付裡了，你不用問。」
「不好意思，我們這台是分開感應的。」
「都綁在一起了啊，你是不會用喔？」
於是我把發票印出來。
「誰叫你印的？我要存載具。」
同一個人，三十秒內給了我三種答案，
而這台機器，一次只讀得懂一個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在結帳台被「綁在一起就好了」鬼打牆的收銀夥伴。不是我們不肯，是機器讀不到您心裡那個版本的流程。
variations: 「你們系統怎麼這麼爛。」系統可能是爛的，但它至少每次都給我同一個答案。
我不怕操作複雜，我怕您的需求在我按下確認鍵之後才改版。

en.content:
"My receipt's already linked to my phone. Don't ask."
"Sorry, this terminal scans the payment and the receipt separately."
"They're linked. You don't know how to work your own register?"
So I print the paper receipt.
"Who told you to print it? I wanted it stored digitally."
Same guy. Three different answers in thirty seconds.
The scanner only reads one at a time.
en.editorNote: For every cashier stuck in the "it's all linked, just do it" loop. It's not that we won't — the terminal can't read the version of the process that exists only in your head.
variations: "Your system sucks." Maybe it does. But at least it gives me the same answer every time.
I can handle a complicated register. What I can't handle is the request changing after I hit confirm.

items.sourceNote: 勞動部關於雇主要求勞工下班後參加與業務相關教育訓練、其時間應否計入工作時間的解釋。檔內無教育訓練／線上課程題材，svc-053 是神秘客稽核、svc-023 是公司教微笑，本則核心是課程本身吃掉的無薪時間，以及課綱缺了下班那一段

zh-tw.content:
公司寄來十二堂線上課程，
標題叫「打造感動服務」，
限期兩週看完，測驗要八十分。
我在下班後的床上點開第九堂，
它教我把語調提高兩度、尾音上揚。
十二堂裡沒有一堂教我，
被吼完之後，
怎麼把自己的聲音調回原本的高度。
zh-tw.editorNote: 勞動部的說法很清楚：雇主要求、又跟業務相關的教育訓練，時間應計入工作時間。下次看到「限期兩週看完」，記得那兩週也是公司的時間，不是你的。
variations: 那十二堂課，公司算成「自我成長」，我算成無薪加班。
教微笑的課有十二堂，教怎麼把情緒收好再回家的，一堂都沒有。

en.content:
Corporate sent over twelve online modules.
Title: "Building Moments That Move Customers."
Two weeks to finish, 80% to pass.
I open module nine in bed after my shift.
It teaches me to lift my pitch two notes and end on an upswing.
Not one of the twelve teaches me
how to get my voice back down to its own pitch
after somebody finishes yelling at me.
en.editorNote: Taiwan's labor ministry is clear that mandatory, job-related training counts as work time. Next time a two-week deadline lands in your inbox, remember those two weeks belong to the company, not to you.
variations: Corporate calls those twelve modules "personal growth." I call them unpaid overtime.
Twelve modules on how to smile. Zero on how to put yourself back together and go home.

items.sourceNote: 服務業人力荒與現場負荷的深度報導。svc-247 是休息時間被客人卡掉、svc-222 是躲進倉庫喘一口，本則核心是一頓飯被切成七次、最後涼掉的具體畫面

zh-tw.content:
我的午餐十二點開始吃，
下午三點才吃完。
中間站起來七次，
每一次都只來得及咬一口。
最後那口飯，涼得非常徹底。
這份工作不是沒有吃飯時間，
是沒有一段不會被叫走的三分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個便當放到涼、卻還是把每一位客人服務完的自己。休息時間寫在班表上是一件事，能不能真的休息是另一件事。
variations: 別人問我午餐吃什麼，我說「吃了三小時，內容忘了」。
我的休息時間有三十分鐘，只是它被切成十份，每份三分鐘。

en.content:
I started lunch at noon.
I finished it at three.
I stood back up seven times.
Each time I got exactly one bite in.
That last bite was thoroughly cold.
This job isn't short on a lunch break.
It's short on three minutes nobody calls you away from.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose food went cold in the back while they finished taking care of everyone out front. A break on the schedule and a break you actually get are two different things.
variations: Someone asked what I had for lunch. I said "three hours, don't remember."
I get a thirty-minute break. It just shows up in ten pieces, three minutes each.

items.sourceNote: 2026 台灣餐飲趨勢報告：QR 掃碼點餐已成主流，業者以系統取代現場人力。svc-263 是自助結帳被客人叫去代操作、svc-197 是機器人接簡單問題，本則核心是「被精簡掉的那個人力其實被折進同一個人的班表」

zh-tw.content:
桌上多了一張掃碼點餐的貼紙，
公司說：上線之後，人力可以精簡一個。
於是我整晚都在做這些事——
教阿姨怎麼打開相機掃那個方框、
幫收訊不好的叔叔重整三次頁面、
把菜單的字放大再放大，
最後拿出紙筆，一道一道抄下來。
被精簡掉的那一個人，
沒有從店裡消失，
他只是被折進了我的班表裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給店裡上了掃碼點餐、工作卻只多不少的夥伴。系統換掉的是「點單」這個動作，換不掉的是「有人得站在旁邊解釋」這件事——而那個人一直是你。
variations: 菜單變成 QR Code 之後，我的職稱悄悄多了一個：現場教學。
自動化省下來的是老闆表格上的一格，不是我的腳。

en.content:
A QR-code sticker showed up on every table.
Corporate said the rollout meant we could run one person lighter.
So here's how my whole night went:
showing an auntie how to open her camera and find the square,
reloading the page three times for an uncle with one bar of signal,
bumping the menu font up two more sizes,
then pulling out a pad and writing the order down by hand.
The person we ran lighter by
never actually left the building.
They just got folded into my shift.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose place went digital and somehow got busier. The system replaced the act of ordering. It didn't replace the human standing there explaining it — that human is still you.
variations: Since the menu became a QR code, I quietly picked up a second job title: on-site tech support.
Automation saved a line on the manager's staffing sheet. It did not save my feet.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 公視報導：餐飲業職缺年增近 16%，連鎖業者起薪調至 35K。svc-147 與 svc-253 走的是「五十萬職缺沒人做」的新聞角度，本則核心是加薪新聞底下的老鳥薪資倒掛

zh-tw.content:
新聞跑馬燈說：連鎖餐飲起薪調到三萬五。
客人放下手機看著我：「你們現在很好賺喔。」
那個三萬五，
要加上全勤、夜班，還有月底那幾天的加班，
才勉強湊得出來；
而我在這裡第五年，
薪水跟今天早上才報到的新人，
停在同一格。
漲的是徵人啟事，
不是我的存摺。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每次看到「服務業加薪」新聞就被親友調侃的夥伴。加薪加在招募頁上是一回事，加在待了五年的人身上是另一回事——這種最安靜的委屈，叫薪資倒掛。
variations: 公司說今年調薪了。調的是新人的起點，不是我的位置。
「起薪三萬五」最關鍵的是那個「起」字——只有還沒進來的人領得到。

en.content:
The news ticker says chain restaurants raised starting pay to 35K.
A customer looks up from his phone: "Must be good money now, huh."
That 35K only adds up
with perfect attendance, the night differential,
and the overtime that piles on at month end.
I've been here five years.
My number sits in the same box
as the kid who clocked in this morning.
What went up was the job posting.
Not my bank balance.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose relatives keep quoting the 'service jobs pay more now' headline at them. A raise on the hiring page and a raise for the person who stayed five years are two different things. The quiet name for that gap is pay compression.
variations: The company announced a raise. It raised where new hires start, not where I stand.
Starting pay 35K. The load-bearing word is starting — you only get it if you haven't arrived yet.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 七年服務業心得中「職業被看輕」的討論串。svc-018 是提醒客人我們也是誰的家人、svc-192 是客人撂話不再來，本則核心是同學會上被一聲「喔」帶過的職業尊嚴

zh-tw.content:
同學會上，有人問我現在在做什麼。
我說我在門市。
他「喔」了一聲，杯子轉了半圈，
就轉頭跟旁邊的人聊起別的。
那個「喔」我聽過很多次，
一年比一年短。
我沒有解釋——
我養得起自己，
也記得每一位常客不用開口的那杯。
只是這種本事，
在那張桌子上，沒有欄位可以填。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在同學會上被一聲「喔」打斷的自己。工作有沒有價值，不是由那張桌子上最大聲的人決定的；你撐住的那一班本來就沒有觀眾，但它真的被撐住了。
variations: 他問我什麼時候找個「正式一點」的工作。我上個月排了二十二天班，每一天都很正式。
我的職業不需要在同學會上，被翻譯成別人聽得懂的樣子。

en.content:
At the reunion, someone asked what I do now.
I said I work retail.
He said "oh," turned his glass half a rotation,
and started a different conversation with the guy next to him.
I've heard that "oh" plenty of times.
It gets shorter every year.
I didn't explain myself.
I cover my own rent.
I know what every regular wants before they ask for it.
That skill just doesn't have
a box to check at that table.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's been cut off by a one-syllable 'oh' at a reunion. Whether your work counts is not decided by the loudest person at that table. The shift you carried never had an audience — it still got carried.
variations: He asked when I'd get a 'real' job. I worked twenty-two days last month. Every one of them was real.
My job doesn't need translating into something that sounds better at a reunion.

items.sourceNote: 104 白皮書：2026 服務業人才缺口龐大，住宿餐飲缺口最大。svc-063 是老闆用「成長機會」包裝一人多工、svc-147 是新聞標題怪年輕人吃不了苦，本則核心是客人當面把缺工誤讀成店員的怠慢

zh-tw.content:
隊伍排到門口，
現場只有我一個。
「你們是不是不想做生意？怎麼只開一個櫃檯。」
先生，開櫃檯的不是我，
是那張排班表；
排班表也不是不肯開，
是我們貼在門上的徵人啟事，
貼了半年還在那裡。
您等的那十分鐘，
其實是整個行業的空缺，
剛好排到您這一號。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給旺季一個人扛整條隊伍、還要代替公司挨罵的夥伴。客人看得到人手不夠，只是他找不到人抱怨；而決定開幾個櫃檯的那個人，從來不站在現場。
variations: 「怎麼只有一個人？」因為另外兩個人的職缺，還在人力銀行上等有緣人。
我沒有慢，我只是被排在一個沒有下一位同事的班。

en.content:
The line runs out the door.
There is exactly one of me.
"Do you people not want business? Why is only one register open?"
Sir, I don't open registers.
The schedule does.
And the schedule isn't holding out on you —
the help-wanted sign we taped to that door
has been there six months.
The ten minutes you waited
is an industry-wide vacancy
that happened to land on your number.
en.editorNote: For anyone holding an entire line alone and eating the complaint on the company's behalf. The customer can see you're short-staffed; you're just the only one there to say it to. Whoever decides how many registers open is never standing on the floor.
variations: "Why is there only one of you?" Because the other two positions are still up on the job board, waiting on somebody.
I'm not slow. I was just scheduled onto a shift with no next coworker.

items.sourceNote: 2026 父親節落在 8/8 週六，餐廳訂位與慶祝檔期爆滿的推薦文。svc-035 是排班表決定人生規劃、svc-018 是提醒客人我們也是誰的家人，本則核心是「幫全城的人過完節，自己的家訊息躺在圍裙口袋裡」

zh-tw.content:
八月八號，訂位表滿到沒有一格空白。
一整天，我幫十七桌拍了全家福，
切了十七次蛋糕，唱了十七次「爸爸辛苦了」，
每一張照片裡，都有一個被兒女圍著的爸爸。
下午三點，我爸傳來一句：
「今天要回來吃嗎？」
我把手機蓋回圍裙口袋，
端起下一桌的湯。
別人的團圓，是我們最忙的那一天；
我們的團圓，排在補休的那一天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給節日當天忙到沒空回家裡訊息的夥伴。你不是不在乎，你只是剛好站在別人團圓的現場；那句「今天回來吃嗎」不會過期，補休那天再回去，一樣算數。
variations: 服務業的節日不是節日，是加倍的班表。
我幫全城的爸爸過完節，回到家時，那盤菜已經在冰箱裡了。

en.content:
August 8th. Not one open slot left on the reservation sheet.
All day I took family photos for seventeen tables,
cut seventeen cakes,
sang for seventeen dads with their kids crowded around them.
At three, my own dad texted:
"Coming home for dinner tonight?"
I slid the phone back into my apron
and carried out the next table's soup.
Everyone else's family day
is our busiest shift of the year.
Ours gets scheduled for whenever the comp day lands.
en.editorNote: For anyone too slammed on a holiday to answer their own family. You're not indifferent, you just happen to be standing inside someone else's reunion. That text doesn't expire. The dinner still counts on your day off.
variations: In this industry a holiday isn't a day off. It's double the shift.
I helped the whole town celebrate their dads. By the time I got home, my plate was already in the fridge.

items.sourceNote: 518 職場熊報談餐廳 no-show／臨時取消訂位的成本與對策。svc-250 是開店前被貼在玻璃上盯著、svc-284 是客人殺價，本則核心是「被留下來的空桌與外面白站的候位客人，成本全留在現場員工身上」

zh-tw.content:
六點半，六個人的訂位。
我把店裡最大的那張圓桌留下來，
七點，門口已經排到第九組，
我一組一組說：「不好意思，那桌有訂位。」
八點十五，電話撥出去——
「喔，我們臨時不去了，這也要講喔？」
先生，一通三十秒的電話，
可以換回我們一整晚最好的位子，
和外面那九組人白站的四十分鐘。
您沒有損失，
是因為損失全部留在我這裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給旺季替人守空桌守到打烊的夥伴。訂位不是許願，是真的有人把位子空下來等你；取消不需要勇氣，只需要三十秒。
variations: 取消訂位不用道歉，但真的要講一聲。三十秒，就三十秒。
那張空著的桌子，不是我們生意不好，是有人忘了打那通電話。

en.content:
Six-thirty. A table for six.
I held the biggest round table in the house.
By seven the wait list outside was nine parties deep,
and I told every one of them, "Sorry, that one's reserved."
At eight-fifteen I finally called.
"Oh, we're not coming. Were we supposed to tell you?"
Sir, a thirty-second phone call
buys back our best table for an entire night,
plus the forty minutes those nine parties spent standing.
You didn't lose anything
because the loss stayed here with me.
en.editorNote: For anyone who guarded an empty table until closing. A reservation isn't a wish. Somebody actually held that seat for you. Canceling takes no courage, just thirty seconds.
variations: You don't owe us an apology for canceling. You do owe us the call. Thirty seconds.
That empty table doesn't mean business is bad. It means somebody never picked up the phone.

items.sourceNote: 2026/07 中秋禮盒早鳥預購開跑，8 月是門市接單高峰。svc-031 是職缺沒寫的工作內容、svc-229 是把 KPI 換算成情緒穩定，本則核心是「員工自掏腰包買下最後幾盒把業績格子刷綠」

zh-tw.content:
八月才剛開始，櫃檯就堆滿了中秋禮盒的預購單。
公司說：「一個人二十盒，不難吧？」
難的不是二十盒，
是我已經問過所有親戚、所有同學，
和每一位只想買一瓶醬油的客人。
結算前一晚，
我用自己的卡刷掉最後三盒，
業績表上那一格終於變綠。
公司說這叫達標，
我這邊的說法是——
我花錢買了一張不用被檢討的門票。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每年檔期都被攤預購數字的門市夥伴。自購湊出來的達標，報表上很漂亮，掏出來的卻是自己的薪水；那不是你的能力問題，是那個數字從一開始就沒打算讓人做到。
variations: 預購目標二十盒，其中有三盒的客人，叫做我。
公司說業績達標了。達標的是報表，付錢的是我的信用卡。

en.content:
First week of August and the counter is already buried in mooncake pre-order forms.
Corporate said, "Twenty boxes each. That's not a lot."
Twenty boxes isn't the hard part.
The hard part is I've already asked every relative, every classmate,
and every customer who walked in for one bottle of soy sauce.
The night before the count closed
I put the last three on my own card,
and the cell on the tracker finally turned green.
Corporate calls that hitting target.
Around here we call it
paying cash for a ticket out of the follow-up meeting.
en.editorNote: For anyone handed a quota every promo season. A target you bought yourself looks great on the report and comes straight out of your own paycheck. The gap isn't your ability. That number was never built to be reachable.
variations: Quota: twenty boxes. Three of those customers were me.
The company hit its target. My credit card took the hit.

items.sourceNote: 2026 中秋早鳥檔期開賣，各家促銷皆附排除條款與期限小字。svc-170、svc-284 走的是客人殺價／討優惠，本則核心是「總部訂規則、決定字級，現場負責念小字並挨罵」

zh-tw.content:
客人把 DM 拍在櫃檯上：「上面就寫買一送一。」
下面那行小字寫著：
不含特價品、不含新品、限指定分店、
每人限一組、活動至前一日止。
那五個條件不是我加的，
我連公告都是昨天下班前才看到。
但站在您面前的是我，
所以那五行字，今天由我一個人念完，
再由我一個人被罵完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給檔期第一天被促銷小字圍剿的夥伴。規則是總部訂的，海報是總部設計的，字要印多小也是總部決定的——只有「解釋」跟「挨罵」這兩件事，外包給了現場。
variations: 促銷是總部想的，例外條款是總部寫的，道歉是我在現場說的。
最大的那行字負責把人吸引進來，最小的那行字負責讓我挨罵。

en.content:
The customer slaps the flyer on the counter. "It says buy one get one."
The line underneath says:
excludes sale items, excludes new arrivals, participating stores only,
one per customer, offer ended yesterday.
I didn't write those five conditions.
I didn't even see the memo until the end of my shift last night.
But I'm the one standing in front of you,
so today I read all five lines out loud by myself,
and then get yelled at for all five by myself.
en.editorNote: For anyone ambushed by fine print on day one of a promo. Head office writes the rules, designs the poster, and decides how small the type gets. The only two parts outsourced to the floor are explaining it and absorbing the anger.
variations: Head office designs the deal, writes the exceptions, and sends me out to apologize for both.
The big print brings them in. The small print gets me yelled at.

items.sourceNote: 2026 三立報導整理店員最常遇到的失格行為，包含在餐桌上替嬰兒換尿布、把髒尿布丟進餐具回收台。svc-276 是小孩打翻飲料被默默擦掉、svc-283 是小孩弄壞商品，本則核心是「客人把最不該留的東西留在回收台，而清的人沒有拒絕的權利」

zh-tw.content:
您在座位上替寶寶換完尿布，
把那包東西放進餐具回收台，
跟別人的碗筷疊在一起，
然後牽著孩子走出門，還回頭說了聲謝謝。
那聲謝謝我收下了。
那包東西也是我收的。
小姐，我沒有生氣，
我只是想讓您知道——
這一區沒有清潔阿姨，
有的是剛剛替您加水、擦桌、拿兒童椅的那個人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每一位在回收台前深呼吸過的外場夥伴。孩子還小不是問題，問題是有人默認「反正有人會收」；那個人有名字，也有下班時間。
variations: 回收台不是垃圾桶，它只是離您最近的那一個。
我可以收碗、收盤、收托盤，唯獨那一包，希望您自己帶走。

en.content:
You changed the baby right there at the table,
then set the bundle in the dish return
stacked in with everyone else's plates,
took your kid's hand, and said thanks on the way out.
I'll keep the thanks.
I also kept the bundle.
Ma'am, I'm not angry.
I just want you to know
there is no cleaning crew for that station.
There's the person who refilled your water, wiped your table, and brought the high chair.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has stood at the dish return taking a slow breath. A baby isn't the problem. The problem is assuming somebody handles it. That somebody has a name and a shift that ends.
variations: The dish return isn't a trash can. It's just the one closest to you.
I'll take the plates, the cups, the trays. That one bundle, please take with you.

items.sourceNote: 2026 主管機關定調不合理客訴不再納入服務評比與記點，律師專文亦說明奧客行為的法律界線。svc-181 是「我也想給客人評分」、svc-034 是客訴法庭，本則核心是「制度第一次替現場分辨客訴與找碴」

zh-tw.content:
以前只要電話一進總部，
不管內容是什麼，我這裡就先扣一次。
「你們憑什麼不給我插隊」也算一次，
「你長得就不像會做事」也算一次。
今年制度改了：
無理的那種，不列入計算。
我看著公告站了三秒——
原來不是我抗壓性太差，
是以前那把尺，
根本沒有分辨過誰在講理。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給曾經被莫名其妙的申訴扣過考績的人。制度會慢，但會動；在它追上來之前，先別急著用那把壞掉的尺量自己。
variations: 客訴跟找碴，終於不是同一格了。
不是我變強了，是那把量我的尺，終於修好了一點。

en.content:
It used to be that any call to head office
cost me a mark, no matter what was in it.
"How dare you not let me cut the line" counted.
"You don't look like someone who works hard" counted.
This year the policy changed:
unreasonable complaints don't go on the record.
I stood in front of that memo for three seconds.
Turns out it was never that I couldn't take pressure.
It was that the old ruler
never once checked who was being reasonable.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose review got dinged by a complaint that made no sense. Systems move slowly, but they do move. Until yours catches up, stop measuring yourself with the broken ruler.
variations: A complaint and a tantrum finally live in different columns.
I didn't get tougher. The thing measuring me just got a little less broken.

items.sourceNote: 2026 Dcard 外送板討論：淡季爆胎加上手機摔壞，等於當月收入直接歸零。svc-267 是雨天爬五樓、svc-290 是客人加碼要求，本則核心是「工具就是生計，一顆輪胎就能讓一個月消失」

zh-tw.content:
早上八點，右後輪壓到一根釘子。
手機從車架上摔下去，螢幕裂成一張蜘蛛網。
修車一千二，換螢幕四千五。
我坐在路邊算了一下——
這個月白跑了。
公司說我是「合作夥伴」，
夥伴的意思是：
車是我的、油是我的、手機是我的、
倒下去的時候，也是我自己爬起來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給用自己的車、自己的手機在賺錢的人。所謂彈性自由，翻過來就是所有風險都算你的；出門前先看一眼胎壓，那三十秒是你這個月最划算的投資。
variations: 一根釘子可以讓一個月消失，這件事沒寫在招募文案裡。
他們叫我夥伴。夥伴的定義是：東西壞了，只有我一個人在付錢。

en.content:
Eight in the morning, the back tire finds a nail.
The phone drops off the mount and the screen webs over.
Tire: forty bucks. Screen: a hundred and fifty.
I sat on the curb and did the math.
This month is gone.
The app calls me a partner.
Partner means
my bike, my gas, my phone,
and when it all goes down, my own two hands picking it back up.
en.editorNote: For everyone earning on their own vehicle and their own phone. Flexible and free, flipped over, means every risk lands on you. Check your tire pressure before you clock in. Thirty seconds, best investment of the month.
variations: One nail can erase a whole month. That part wasn't in the recruiting ad.
They call me a partner. A partner is the only one who pays when something breaks.

items.sourceNote: 518 職場熊報談客訴處理與服務評分機制。svc-259 是客人拿一星威脅、svc-181 是想反過來評分客人，本則核心是「打在我頭上的分數，扣分項目全部不歸我管」

zh-tw.content:
結帳完，系統會寄一封滿意度問卷給客人，
分數會掛在我的工號底下。
這個月我拿到三分。
扣分理由：停車位太難找、東西比網路貴、
還有「等太久」——那天現場只有我一個人。
停車場不是我畫的，
價格不是我訂的，
班表更不是我排的。
但那三分，
穩穩地落在我的名字上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被綁著一個自己控制不了的分數的人。評分不是照妖鏡，它只是把整間公司的問題，濃縮成一個掛在你工號後面的數字；那不是你的成績單。
variations: 我的分數包含停車位、定價和公司的排班，唯獨不包含我做了什麼。
問卷問的是這家店，扣的是我的名字。

en.content:
After checkout the system emails the customer a survey,
and the score lands under my employee number.
This month I got a three.
Reasons docked: parking is hard, prices beat the website,
and "waited too long" — that day I was the only one on the floor.
I didn't paint the parking lot.
I didn't set the prices.
I sure didn't write the schedule.
But that three
sits squarely on my name.
en.editorNote: For anyone chained to a number they can't control. A rating isn't a mirror. It compresses the whole company's problems into one figure stapled to your badge. That is not your report card.
variations: My score covers parking, pricing, and staffing. It covers everything except what I did.
The survey asks about the store. The deduction lands on me.

items.sourceNote: 2026 暑期來台旅客回升，第一線多了語言不通的點餐互動。svc-256 是客人主動收拾說辛苦了、svc-062 是一句謝謝，本則核心是「零共同語言的客人，反而把禮貌做得最完整」

zh-tw.content:
中午進來一對講我完全聽不懂的客人。
我們靠著菜單上的照片、四根手指、
和一個代表「不要辣」的搖頭，點完了餐。
全程大概花了五分鐘。
他們走的時候雙手合十，對我彎了一下腰。
那天下午，另一位客人用我聽得懂的語言
罵了我三分鐘。
原來禮貌從來不是語言能力，
是願不願意。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在被夏季旅客潮淹沒的第一線夥伴。語言不通不會拖慢你，只有不願意好好講話的人會；今天遇到那種比手畫腳還笑著道謝的客人，記得多存一點。
variations: 他一個字都聽不懂，卻把「謝謝」表達得最完整。
我們之間沒有共同語言，卻完成了今天最順利的一次點餐。

en.content:
Around noon a couple walked in speaking a language I don't have a word of.
We ordered using the photos on the menu, four fingers held up,
and a head shake that meant no spice.
The whole thing took five minutes.
On the way out they pressed their palms together and gave me a small bow.
That same afternoon another customer, in a language I understand perfectly,
yelled at me for three minutes.
Turns out manners were never a language skill.
They're a decision.
en.editorNote: For anyone buried in the summer tourist rush. A language barrier doesn't slow you down. Only people who won't bother do. When you get the ones who gesture and still smile their thanks, save that one.
variations: He didn't understand a single word, and still got "thank you" across perfectly.
We had no language in common and still had the smoothest order of the day.

items.sourceNote: PTT CVS 板長期討論「客人講電話不掛就來結帳」。svc-258 是客人講不清楚要什麼、svc-286 是被當成觀光服務台，本則核心是「他願意對電話出聲，卻只肯對我比手勢」

zh-tw.content:
他手機貼著耳朵走到櫃檯，
對電話那頭說：「你等我一下。」
然後轉過來，對我比了兩根手指，
再指指我後面的看板，嘴型動了一下。
我猜了三次都猜錯。
他嘖了一聲：「你聽不懂喔？」
先生，我聽得很清楚。
那通電話您講了七分鐘，
只有對我這一段，
您捨不得出聲。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在櫃檯猜手勢的人。這不是你反應慢，是對方根本沒打算把話說出來；下次可以微笑著說「不好意思我需要您說一次品項」，把責任放回它本來該在的地方。
variations: 他願意花七分鐘跟電話那頭講話，卻不肯花七秒對我說一句「大杯冰美式」。
我不是讀唇專家，我只是剛好站在您不想掛電話的那一頭。

en.content:
He walks up with the phone welded to his ear
and tells whoever's on the line, "Hang on a sec."
Then he turns to me, holds up two fingers,
points at the board behind my head, and mouths something.
I guess wrong three times.
He clicks his tongue. "You can't understand me?"
Sir, I hear you perfectly.
You've been on that call seven minutes.
I'm the only part of your day
not worth saying out loud.
en.editorNote: For everyone playing charades at a register. You're not slow. He simply never intended to use words on you. "Sorry, I'll need you to say the item out loud" puts that back where it belongs.
variations: Seven minutes of talking to his phone, and not seven seconds to say "large iced coffee" to me.
I'm not a lip reader. I just happen to stand on the side of the call he won't hang up.

items.sourceNote: 2026 Dcard 工作板討論交接班文化：上一班留下的狀態決定下一班的前一小時。svc-133 是同事一起苦中作樂、svc-146 是公司挺員工，本則核心是「我把爛攤子止在自己這一班」

zh-tw.content:
下班前十五分鐘，
我把咖啡機拆開洗乾淨，
把冰櫃前排補滿，
把發票紙換上一捲新的。
不會有人知道是我做的，
考核表上也沒有這一欄。
但我還記得三年前那個早上，
我接到的是一個什麼都沒有的櫃檯，
和一個躲在後場哭的自己。
我沒辦法讓這份工作變好，
至少可以讓下一班的第一個小時好一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個默默把爛攤子止在自己這一班的人。這件事沒有獎金、沒有人記錄，但接班的人一定感覺得到；服務業真正撐住彼此的，從來不是公司政策，是這種不用開口的默契。
variations: 我沒辦法讓這份工作變好，但我可以讓下一班的第一個小時好過一點。
考核表上沒有「把機器洗乾淨留給下一個人」這一欄，可是接班的人都知道。

en.content:
Fifteen minutes before I clock out
I break the espresso machine down and scrub it,
face up the front row of the cooler,
drop in a fresh roll of receipt paper.
Nobody will know it was me.
There's no line for it on the review form.
But I still remember a morning three years back
when I inherited a counter with nothing on it
and a version of me crying in the stockroom.
I can't make this job better.
I can make the next person's first hour better.
en.editorNote: For the one who quietly stops the mess at the end of their own shift. No bonus, no record of it, but whoever comes in next always feels it. What actually holds this industry together isn't policy. It's this.
variations: I can't fix the job. I can fix somebody's first hour of it.
There's no box on the review form for leaving the machine clean. The next shift knows anyway.

items.sourceNote: 賣場、量販與連鎖門市普遍配戴耳掛式對講機，員工被以編號呼叫。svc-018 是制服底下不只是一個工號、svc-160 是拿對講機反擊，本則核心是「下班後耳朵裡還在叫我的編號，而那不是我的名字」

zh-tw.content:
耳掛式麥克風戴了八個小時，
右耳一直有人在叫我的編號。
「三號支援收銀。」
「三號來一下後場。」
「三號、三號、三號。」
晚上躺在床上，房間安靜到會耳鳴，
我還是聽見有人在叫三號。
我有名字的。
只是在這裡，
沒有人需要用到它。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給整天掛著耳機被呼叫的人。下班後耳朵裡還在響不是你太敏感，是身體還沒關機；睡前把耳機放遠一點，讓房間安靜到你想得起自己的名字。
variations: 上班八小時被叫了兩百次編號，一次名字都沒有。
耳朵已經下班了，那個聲音還在裡面加班。

en.content:
Eight hours with the headset on
and somebody is always in my right ear calling my number.
"Three to register."
"Three, come to the back."
"Three. Three. Three."
At night I'm lying in a room quiet enough to ring,
and I still hear someone paging three.
I have a name.
It's just that in here,
nobody ever needs it.
en.editorNote: For anyone worked all day through an earpiece. The ringing after you clock out isn't oversensitivity, it's a body that hasn't powered down. Leave the headset in another room and let it get quiet enough to remember your name.
variations: Two hundred pages in eight hours, and not one of them was my name.
My ears clocked out. That voice is still in there working overtime.

items.sourceNote: 2026 薪水板討論精品／甜點／咖啡門市員工買不起自家商品。svc-133 提到員工價只是順帶一提、svc-297 是客人以為起薪很好賺，本則核心是「打完員工折還是等於我站一個半小時」

zh-tw.content:
我顧的這個櫃，
最便宜的一個要三百二。
每天擦玻璃、換標籤、
跟客人講到什麼是尾韻，講到自己都餓了。
下班前同事說：「員工八折欸，買一個？」
我心裡算了一下——
兩百五十六塊，
剛好是我站在這裡一個半小時。
我笑著說不用，
回家煮了一包麵。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天賣著自己買不起的東西的人。那個價差不是你造成的，也不代表你不夠努力；你對這些商品的了解是真本事，只是這家店還沒學會用它該有的價錢買下來。
variations: 打完八折，還是要我站一個半小時。
我講得出它的每一層風味，唯獨講不出把它帶回家的理由。

en.content:
The case I work,
cheapest thing in it is twenty-two dollars.
All day I wipe the glass, swap the labels,
talk people through the finish until I'm hungry myself.
Before close a coworker says, "Staff discount's twenty percent, want one?"
I ran the numbers.
Seventeen sixty.
That's more than an hour of standing right here.
I smiled and said no thanks,
went home and boiled noodles.
en.editorNote: For everyone selling what they can't afford. That gap isn't your fault and isn't a measure of your effort. What you know about this product is real expertise. The store just hasn't figured out how to pay for it.
variations: Even after the staff discount, it still costs me an hour on my feet.
I can name every note in it. I can't name a reason to take one home.

items.sourceNote: 2026 零售討論：實體店淪為免費試衣間，客人試穿問完後當場線上下單。與 svc-077（只是看看卻問到飽）區隔在於「當著店員的面比價下單」

zh-tw.content:
「這件我要試 M 跟 L。」
「有沒有別的顏色？」
「幫我配一條褲子看看。」
四十分鐘後，他站在鏡子前，
低頭滑開手機，
把螢幕轉過來給我看：
「網路便宜三百欸，我線上買喔。」
先生，剛剛那四十分鐘，
您也是在我這裡買的，
只是您決定不付錢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被當成免費試衣間的門市人員。你提供的量身、配色、判斷都是專業，只是這個行業還沒學會把它標上價格——不是你不值得。
variations: 您省下的那三百塊，是我四十分鐘的專業。
網路可以比價，比不了剛剛幫您挑袖長的那雙眼睛。

en.content:
"I'll try this in a medium and a large."
"Got it in another color?"
"Pull me some pants to go with it."
Forty minutes later he's at the mirror,
looking down at his phone,
turning the screen toward me:
"It's ten bucks cheaper online. I'll just order it."
Sir, those forty minutes
you bought from me too.
You just decided not to pay for them.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose store gets used as a free fitting room. Sizing, styling, and judgment are real skills. The industry just hasn't figured out how to put a price tag on them, and that's not on you.
variations: The ten bucks you saved was forty minutes of my expertise.
You can price-match the shirt. You can't price-match the person who checked your sleeve length.

items.sourceNote: 2026 新聞專題「奧客壓垮服務業」提到第一線人員被拍名牌威脅投訴。svc-064 只寫到笑容當盾牌，未觸及名牌被當把柄

zh-tw.content:
「我拍下來了喔。」
他把鏡頭對準我胸前那塊名牌，
喀擦一聲，
然後笑著說：「我知道你叫什麼了。」
先生，那上面只有兩個字，
不是我的住址，也不是我的人生。
您拍走的不是把柄——
那是一個人上班的時候，
唯一還能被叫的名字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被客人拍名牌威脅過的人。名字是拿來被叫的，不是拿來被抓的；你今天做的每一件對的事，都比那張照片清楚。
variations: 名牌不是罪證，是我今天有來上班的證明。
您記住我的名字沒關係，我只希望下次是用叫的。

en.content:
"Got a photo of it."
He aims the lens at the tag on my chest,
one click,
then grins: "Now I know your name."
Sir, there are six letters on that tag.
Not my address, not my life.
What you photographed isn't leverage —
it's the only name
a person still gets called at work.
en.editorNote: For anyone a customer has photographed as a threat. A name badge exists so people can call you, not catch you. Everything you did right today is more legible than that photo.
variations: The badge isn't evidence. It's proof I showed up today.
Remember my name if you want. I just hope next time you say it instead.

items.sourceNote: 2026 打工／零售討論串：打烊對帳短少由當班人員自行補平的常態。svc-269 是與客人爭執找零，本則是無人知曉的自掏腰包

zh-tw.content:
打烊後對帳，短少三十七塊。
我找了四十分鐘，
翻收銀機、倒垃圾桶、重印一次明細，
還是三十七塊。
最後我從自己的皮夾抽出一張，
投進抽屜，
把數字補成剛剛好，
簽名、關燈、走人。
那三十七塊沒有人會知道，
就像今天所有沒有人會知道的事一樣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個默默把帳補平的人。你補的其實不是那幾十塊，是「這班沒出事」的安心；但這份安心不該一直由你的皮夾出錢，該報的還是要報。
variations: 差的三十七塊我補得起，補不起的是那四十分鐘。
帳平了，只有我知道它是怎麼平的。

en.content:
Counting the drawer after close: a dollar fifteen short.
I looked for forty minutes —
pulled the till apart, dug through the trash,
reprinted the whole tape.
Still a dollar fifteen.
In the end I took it out of my own wallet,
dropped it in,
made the number come out exactly right,
signed off, killed the lights, went home.
Nobody will ever know about that dollar fifteen,
same as everything else nobody knows about today.
en.editorNote: For everyone who quietly makes the drawer balance. What you're covering isn't the money, it's the feeling that your shift went fine. That feeling shouldn't keep coming out of your wallet. Report it.
variations: I can afford the dollar fifteen. It's the forty minutes I can't.
The drawer balanced. I'm the only one who knows how.

items.sourceNote: 門市／早班人員談長期熟客突然不再出現的貼文情緒。svc-084、svc-134 講熟客都是負面或吐槽向，站上缺一則溫暖收束

zh-tw.content:
有位先生每天早上七點十分進門，
一個飯糰、一瓶無糖豆漿，
從來不多說一句話，
但零錢總是輕輕放進我手心，
不是丟在檯面上。
上個月開始，七點十分變成空的。
我還是會在那個時間抬頭看一次門口。
櫃檯後面的人不會去問客人去了哪裡，
我們只是會記得——
七點十分，曾經有人來過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那些默默記得熟客的人。你以為自己只是收錢找錢，其實你一直在替這條街保管別人的日常。
variations: 我不知道他姓什麼，但我記得他的七點十分。
有些客人走了以後，門口還是會留一個時間給他。

en.content:
There was a man who came in at 7:10 every morning.
One rice ball, one unsweetened soy milk,
never a word more than he needed,
but he always set the change in my palm
instead of dropping it on the counter.
Last month, 7:10 went empty.
I still look up at the door at that exact time.
People behind a counter don't get to ask where a customer went.
We just remember —
someone used to come at 7:10.
en.editorNote: For everyone who quietly keeps track of their regulars. You think you're just ringing people up. You've actually been holding onto this street's ordinary mornings for it.
variations: I never learned his last name. I remember his 7:10.
Some customers leave, and the door keeps a time slot for them anyway.

items.sourceNote: 門市人員談「幫我留貨、我明天來拿」後失聯，期間還要回絕其他有意購買的客人。站上尚無留貨主題

zh-tw.content:
「幫我留一下，我明天一定來拿。」
我在便條紙上寫下他的姓和電話，
把最後一件收進櫃檯底下。
隔天中午，有人來問一模一樣的那件，
我說不好意思，這件已經有人預訂了。
第三天、第四天，便條紙還貼在那裡。
第五天我把它放回架上，
吊牌上的折痕還在，
就像那句「我明天一定來」一樣，
皺著，但沒有兌現。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被「我明天來拿」放鳥過的門市人員。你留下的不只是一件貨，是對一句話的相信；下次真的不確定，請客人直接說不用留，不會有人生氣。
variations: 我留住的不是商品，是一句話的信用。
不用留也沒關係，真的，我只怕您說了明天。

en.content:
"Hold it for me. I'll come by tomorrow for sure."
I wrote his last name and number on a sticky note
and tucked the last one under the counter.
Next day at noon, someone asked for that exact piece.
Sorry, I said, that one's on hold.
Day three, day four, the note was still there.
Day five I put it back on the rack.
The crease in the tag was still in it,
same as "tomorrow for sure" —
creased, and never honored.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's been stood up by "I'll come back tomorrow." You weren't holding merchandise, you were holding someone's word. If you're unsure, just tell the clerk not to hold it. Nobody will be upset.
variations: What I held wasn't the item. It was somebody's word.
It's fine if you don't want it held. I just dread hearing "tomorrow."

items.sourceNote: 餐飲內場人員談下班後身上洗不掉的油煙味與被閃避的經驗。svc-255 寫的是站太久的身體代價、svc-064 是笑容當盾牌，本則核心是「氣味成為職業標記，被當成髒」

zh-tw.content:
下班的電梯裡，
有人吸了吸鼻子，
往旁邊挪了半步。
我知道。
我身上有八小時的炸油、
四小時的洗碗精，
還有一整晚別人的晚餐。
這個味道我洗過三次，還在。
可是它不是髒。
它是今天有一百多個人
因為我而吃得到熱的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給下班後不太敢站進滿員電梯的內場同事。你身上的味道不是失禮，是勞動留下的收據；真要說難聞，該檢討的是抽風機，不是你。
variations: 我身上這個味道，是一百多個人今天有熱飯吃。
洗不掉沒關係，它不代表我髒，代表我今天有來。

en.content:
In the elevator after shift,
someone sniffs,
then shifts half a step away.
I know.
I'm carrying eight hours of fryer oil,
four hours of dish soap,
and a whole evening of other people's dinners.
I've washed it out three times. It's still there.
But it isn't dirt.
It's a hundred and forty people
who got something hot to eat today because of me.
en.editorNote: For the back-of-house crew who hesitate before stepping into a crowded elevator. That smell isn't rudeness, it's a receipt for labor. If anything needs fixing, it's the exhaust hood, not you.
variations: This smell on me is a hundred and forty people who ate hot food today.
It won't wash out. Fine. It doesn't mean I'm dirty, it means I showed up.

items.sourceNote: 門市失物招領討論：客人找不到自己寄放／遺落的物品後，直接暗示是員工拿走。svc-291 是被拍名牌威脅、svc-263 是找零爭執，本則核心是「清白被一句推測拿走」

zh-tw.content:
「我昨天有一把傘放在門口。」
我陪他翻了失物箱、倉庫、後門走道，
沒有。
他站在原地看了我三秒，
說：「那……應該是你們裡面的人拿走了吧。」
先生，
您的傘不見了，我真的很抱歉。
但您剛剛弄丟的，
是一整組今天什麼都沒做錯的人的清白。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給被客人用「應該是你們拿的」暗示過的人。東西找不到的懊惱是真的，但把它變成指控只需要一秒；你陪他翻遍全店的那十分鐘，本來就不需要向任何人證明。
variations: 傘我可以幫您找，那句話說出口之前的我，找不回來了。
東西掉了有人陪您找，清白掉了沒有。

en.content:
"I left an umbrella by the door yesterday."
I walked him through the lost-and-found bin, the stockroom, the back hallway.
Nothing.
He stood there and looked at me for three seconds.
"So... somebody who works here probably took it, right?"
Sir,
I'm genuinely sorry your umbrella is gone.
But what you just lost
is the good name of every person here who did nothing wrong today.
en.editorNote: For anyone who's had a customer float "one of you must have taken it." Losing something is genuinely frustrating, but turning that into an accusation takes one second. Those ten minutes you spent searching with him never needed defending.
variations: I can help you look for the umbrella. I can't get back who I was before you said that.
Lose an umbrella and someone helps you search. Lose your good name and nobody does.

items.sourceNote: 連鎖門市開店前精神喊話／口號文化的討論。svc-023 是公司教微笑、svc-288 是下班後的教育訓練，本則核心是「士氣被當成音量問題，真正的付出發生在沒人看見的補貨夜」

zh-tw.content:
開店前十分鐘，
我們站成一排，對著還沒拉開的鐵門喊：
「熱情！微笑！全力以赴！」
喊完，副店說再大聲一點，
因為隔壁家聽起來比較有精神。
我很想說——
熱情不是喊出來的。
是我昨天留到十一點半把架補完，
沒有人在看，
也沒有人叫我喊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天被要求喊口號的門市同事。士氣長在班表和人力上，不長在嗓子裡；你已經做完的那些事，比任何一句口號都大聲。
variations: 口號可以再大聲一點，薪水也可以。
我的熱情不在喉嚨裡，在昨天十一點半的補貨紀錄裡。

en.content:
Ten minutes before open,
we line up and shout at a security gate that's still down:
"Passion! Smile! Give it everything!"
Then the assistant manager says do it louder,
because the store next door sounds more into it.
What I want to say is —
passion isn't something you shout.
It's me staying till 11:30 last night to finish the restock,
with nobody watching,
and nobody telling me to shout.
en.editorNote: For everyone made to chant before open. Morale lives in the schedule and the staffing, not in your throat. What you already did last night is louder than any cheer.
variations: Sure, we can go louder. The paycheck could go louder too.
My passion isn't in my throat. It's in last night's restock log.

items.sourceNote: 服務業從業者下班後成為別家店客人時的體感討論。svc-256 是店員收到客人的體貼、本則反過來是「員工作為客人的那一眼互相辨認」，POV 相反不重複

zh-tw.content:
下班後我去買宵夜。
店員手忙腳亂，找錯了錢，
後面的人開始嘆氣。
我說沒關係，你慢慢來。
她抬頭看了我一眼——
那個眼神我認得，
因為一小時前我也是這樣看人的。
我們誰都沒說破在做同一行，
但那一秒她知道，我也知道。
這份工作沒給我們什麼，
只給了一組暗號：
站在櫃檯的哪一邊都一樣，
認得出誰快撐不住了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給下班後還會把托盤收好、不催不嘆氣的你。薪水沒給多少，倒是給了一雙認得出同類的眼睛——你今天讓誰喘到一口氣，自己可能都不知道。
variations: 我們沒交談，但那一眼已經對過暗號了。
這行最值錢的東西，是下班後你還認得出誰在硬撐。

en.content:
After my shift I went out for a late-night snack.
The clerk was scrambling, handed me the wrong change,
and the guy behind me started sighing.
I told her it's okay, take your time.
She looked up at me —
and I knew that look,
because I'd been the one giving it an hour earlier.
Neither of us admitted we work the same kind of job,
but for one second she knew, and I knew.
This work doesn't give us much.
It gives us a signal:
from either side of the counter,
we can spot the person barely holding on.
en.editorNote: For everyone who still buses their own tray and waits without sighing after clocking out. The pay is nothing special, but the job hands you an eye for your own kind. You may never know whose shift you saved today.
variations: We never spoke. We'd already traded the signal.
The best thing this job pays out is being able to spot who's barely holding on.

items.sourceNote: 公司行號中元普渡的職場觀察文。本則取「門市店員同時要顧門口那張桌子和櫃檯」的服務業視角，非民俗教學

zh-tw.content:
早上十點，桌子要擺到大門外。
擺之前得先請三台機車移一移，
其中一台的車主就站在我旁邊，說「喔，那是我的」。
香才剛點沒多久，
玻璃門被推開，客人愣在那裡：
「你們……今天有開嗎？」
有開，一直都有開。
只是這半小時，我是店員，
也是被指派拿香的那一個。
他說「那我等一下再來」，
我說「不用等，裡面請，冷氣是開著的」。
同一條街上，
有人在門口拜，有人照常喝他那杯冰的，
兩件事一起發生，
誰也沒有耽誤誰。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天早上先去移機車、十點半又回櫃檯結帳的那位。門口那半小時最難的不是拜拜，是兩邊同時要顧——你兩邊都顧到了。
variations: 門口那張桌子，是我一個人搬出去、一個人收回來的。
客人問「今天有開嗎」的時候，我一手拿香一手指了指自動門。

en.content:
Ghost Month at our storefront starts with moving three scooters.
The table goes out front at ten.
One of those scooters belongs to the guy standing next to me, who says, oh, that one's mine.
The incense is barely lit when someone pushes the glass door and freezes:
"Are you... open today?"
We're open. We've been open.
For this half hour I'm the clerk, and I'm also the one holding the incense.
He says he'll come back later.
I tell him no need — go on in, the AC is running.
On this street, right now,
someone is making an offering at a doorway and someone is drinking their iced coffee,
both at once,
and neither is holding up the other.
en.editorNote: For whoever moved the scooters at ten and was back on the register by ten-thirty. The hard part of that half hour isn't the ritual, it's covering two posts at the same time — and you covered both.
variations: Carried that table out alone, carried it back in alone.
He asked if we were open. I had incense in one hand and pointed at the door with the other.

items.sourceNote: 職場板關於公司普渡由誰採買、供品事後如何分送員工的討論。與 svc-322 同節日但角度不同：322 是門口現場，本則是採購單與休息室

zh-tw.content:
採購單上那一欄，我填了「祭祀用品」。
底下的明細是三箱飲料、兩袋餅乾、一手布丁，
口味全部照休息室那台冰箱最先空掉的來挑。
店長掃一眼就簽名，什麼都沒問。
桌子擺出去以後，
整箱的要拆開，一樣一樣攤好，
我蹲在那裡拆到手指發疼。
下午收桌，東西全部回到休息室，
變成大家的下午茶。
所以那張單子有兩個名字：
會計看到的那一個，和我們心裡的那一個。
我誠不誠心，自己不敢講，
只敢說——
那手布丁，是一個人一個口味挑的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每年被推派去買供品的那位同事。你在單子上寫的是四個字，背後是把全店的口味默默記了一整年。
variations: 明細寫「祭祀用品」，實際採購邏輯是「休息室冰箱最先空的那幾種」。
蹲在地上拆箱拆到最後的那個人，通常也是下午茶吃最少的那個。

en.content:
"Ritual supplies" is what I wrote on the purchase order.
The itemized list underneath: three cases of drinks, two bags of cookies, a tray of pudding —
every flavor picked from whatever empties out of the break room fridge first.
The manager glanced at it and signed. No questions.
Once the table was out front, the cases had to come open, laid out one by one.
I squatted there breaking down cardboard until my fingers hurt.
By afternoon it all came back inside and turned into everyone's snack break.
So that form has two names:
the one accounting reads, and the one we know.
How sincere I am, I couldn't tell you.
I can tell you the pudding was picked one flavor per person.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who gets volunteered to buy the offerings every year. Two words on a purchase order, and behind them a whole year of quietly tracking what everybody actually likes.
variations: The line item said ritual supplies. The actual logic was whatever the fridge runs out of first.
Whoever flattens all the boxes usually eats the least of what was in them.

items.sourceNote: 門市員工對店內循環廣播的體感討論。既有檔案無「廣播／店內音樂」題材，非重複

zh-tw.content:
今天的活動廣播，一小時播六次。
我算過，一個班下來是七十二次。
下班回到家，電視關掉，
那句「本週限定、買二送一」還在我腦子裡自己播。
洗澡的時候播，
躺平了也播。
最誇張的一次，
我夢到自己對一個陌生人說「歡迎光臨」，
醒來發現我真的講出聲了，
而房間裡只有我一個。
公司花錢買的是客人的耳朵，
我的是買一送一那個「送」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那位下班後在自家客廳脫口說出「歡迎光臨」的同事。那不是職業病，那是聽滿七十二次之後，身體自己幫你記住了。
variations: 離職那天最想帶走的一件事：把那段廣播從我腦袋裡拔出來。
客人聽六次，我聽七十二次，票價一樣。

en.content:
Store announcements loop six times an hour.
I ran the math: seventy-two times a shift.
I get home, shut off the TV, and "this week only, buy two get one" is still playing in my head.
It plays in the shower.
It plays after I lie down.
Worst one yet: I dreamed I said "welcome in" to a stranger,
woke up, and realized I had said it out loud,
alone, in my own room.
The company paid for the customers' ears.
Mine came free with the promotion.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who greeted their own living room after clocking out. That isn't a quirk — after seventy-two plays, your body filed it for you.
variations: Top thing I'd take with me on my last day: that jingle, surgically removed.
Customers hear it six times a visit. I hear it seventy-two. Same ticket price.

items.sourceNote: 門市開店前備零錢的日常討論。既有檔案無「去銀行換零錢」題材，svc-257/316 的零錢是客人端，非重複

zh-tw.content:
早上八點半，我在銀行排隊，
換三千塊的十元和五十元，
再自己把那袋錢抱回店裡。
下午，一位先生買一瓶水，遞了一張千元鈔。
「怎麼會沒零錢？你們不是應該要準備嗎？」
我準備了，先生。
準備的方式是八點半，
用我自己的名字，在窗口前站了二十分鐘。
收銀機不會自己長錢。
抽屜裡那些銅板，
每一枚都是有人先去排過隊，才回得來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給開店前先繞去銀行、把錢袋抱回店裡的那個人。抽屜一拉開大家都覺得理所當然，只有你知道那二十分鐘站在哪裡。
variations: 這份工作有一半的準備，發生在鐵門拉開之前。
客人看到的是抽屜打開，沒看到的是從銀行走回來那一段路。

en.content:
Change does not grow in the register.
At 8:30 this morning I stood in a bank line for twenty minutes, turning three thousand into tens and fifties, then carried the bag back myself.
In the afternoon a man bought one bottle of water and handed me a thousand.
"You don't have change? Aren't you supposed to have change ready?"
We do, sir.
The way we have it is that somebody's own name was on a slip at 8:30 in the morning.
Every coin in that drawer is there because a person went and stood in a line for it.
en.editorNote: For whoever detours to the bank before open and hauls the coin bag back. The drawer slides open and everyone assumes it fills itself — only you know where you spent those twenty minutes.
variations: Half of this job happens before the shutter goes up.
Customers see the drawer open. They don't see the walk back from the bank.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by TVBS 2026-05 「大夜班沒人要做？超商店員吐心聲」 report and its shift breakdown (洗機台／挑報廢／進貨); rewritten as 「客人不在的那六小時最重」 original framing

zh-tw.content:
「大夜比較涼吧，又沒什麼客人。」
十點到十二點，洗兩台咖啡機、挑報廢。
十二點到一點，把報廢一項一項刷進系統。
一點以後開始進貨，一箱一箱搬到天亮。
中間還有掃地、拖地、洗廁所、補鮮食。
先生，大夜沒客人是真的，
但客人不在的那六個小時，
不是留給我休息的，
是留給我一個人做完三個人的事。
門上那張徵人啟事貼了半年，
不是因為大家怕黑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給天亮才下班的大夜同事。外面總說大夜輕鬆，只有你知道沒有客人的那六小時，才是最重的六小時。
variations: 大夜不是沒有事，是沒有人看見你在做事。
這一班最累的部分，剛好發生在沒有人會經過的時間。

en.content:
"Night shift must be easy. Nobody even comes in."
Ten to midnight: scrub two coffee machines, pull everything expiring.
Midnight to one: scan every one of those items into the system.
One onward: unload the delivery, box by box, until the sky changes color.
Somewhere in there: sweep, mop, clean the restroom, restock.
You're right, sir. Nobody comes in.
But those six empty hours aren't given to me to rest in.
They're given to me to do three people's work alone.
That help-wanted sign has been taped to the door for six months,
and it isn't because people are afraid of the dark.
en.editorNote: For anyone who clocks out at sunrise. Everyone assumes overnight is the easy shift — only you know the hours with no customers are the heaviest hours.
variations: The night shift isn't empty. It's just unwitnessed.
The hardest part of this shift happens when there's nobody around to walk past it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 聯合新聞網 2026 「非24小時超商變多了？店員曝辛酸」 and the 「挑報廢」 duty described in it; rewritten as 「一天最餓的時候，親手把十二個晚餐刷成報廢」 original framing

zh-tw.content:
十一點五十分，我站在鮮食櫃前面，
把還冰著、封膜完好的便當一個一個刷過條碼。
螢幕跳出「報廢」，
我再親手放進黑色的袋子裡。
規定寫得很清楚：不能帶走，不能吃。
那是我一天裡最餓的時間，
手上抱著十二個晚餐，
沒有一個是我的。
我不是想爭那一個便當，
我只是每天都得站在垃圾袋前面，
說服自己這件事很合理。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天親手把還能吃的東西刷成報廢的人。這不是在抱怨制度，是那個動作做了幾百次，還是不會變得比較輕。
variations: 這份工作最重的不是搬貨，是丟掉還好好的東西。
今天有十二個晚餐從我手上經過，沒有一個是我的。

en.content:
11:50 p.m. I'm standing at the chilled case,
scanning boxed dinners one at a time — still cold, seals unbroken.
The screen says DISPOSE.
Then I put each one into a black bag with my own hands.
The rule is clear: can't take it home, can't eat it.
This is the hungriest hour of my day
and I'm holding twelve dinners,
none of them mine.
I'm not trying to win an argument over one lunchbox.
I just have to stand in front of that bag every night
and talk myself into believing it makes sense.
en.editorNote: For everyone whose job includes scanning perfectly good food into the trash. Not a policy complaint — just the fact that the motion never gets lighter, no matter how many hundred times you do it.
variations: The heaviest part of this job isn't lifting. It's throwing away things that are still fine.
Twelve dinners passed through my hands tonight. Not one of them was mine.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 聯合新聞網 「客怨飲料多仍不願買塑膠袋，態度差讓店員無奈」 rumor-board story; rewritten as 「那一塊不是我的，我送您的那個才是」 original framing

zh-tw.content:
三杯熱拿鐵，我問要不要提袋，一個一塊。
「一塊也要收？你們是在賺這個喔？」
於是他兩手抱著三杯滿到杯緣的熱飲往外走，
到門口停下來，回頭看我。
我還是拿了一個袋子給他，沒有刷。
他說：「早講嘛。」
先生，那一塊錢從來不是我的，
它寫在法規裡、扣在系統裡、印在您的發票上。
剛剛送您的那個袋子，
才是我自己的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天為了一塊錢被質疑的收銀同事。袋子的價錢不是門市訂的，但被念的永遠是遞袋子的那個人。
variations: 收那一塊的是系統，被罵的是我。
我沒有在賺您那一塊，我只是負責把它念出來的那個人。

en.content:
Three hot lattes. I asked if he wanted a carrier — one dollar.
"You charge for that too? Making money off me now?"
So he walked out cradling three cups filled to the rim,
stopped at the door, and looked back at me.
I handed him a carrier anyway. Didn't ring it up.
"You could've just said so."
Sir, that dollar was never mine.
It's written into the law, deducted by the system, printed on your receipt.
The bag I just gave you —
that one was mine.
en.editorNote: For cashiers who get accused of profiteering over one dollar, every single day. Nobody behind the counter set that price, but the person handing you the bag is the one who hears about it.
variations: The system charges the dollar. I collect the complaint.
I'm not profiting off you. I'm just the one required to say the number out loud.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 華視 2026-05 量販店「售完為止」購物袋話題，特別是「門市無法決定到貨量」這一面向；rewritten as 集點贈品兌換櫃前的門市現場 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「集點那隻公仔，我要三隻。」
「不好意思，昨天就換完了。」
「怎麼可能，是不是你們自己人先拿走？」
先生，我這一檔一隻都沒有。
分配到幾隻不是我決定的，
什麼時候到貨也不是我決定的，
我唯一能決定的，
是我要用什麼表情，
第四十七次說出「真的換完了」。
那個櫃子是空的，
不是被誰藏起來，
是它從來就沒有滿過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給活動檔期站在兌換櫃前的人。贈品的數量從來不是門市能控制的，但客人只看得到你，所以那句「沒有了」只能由你說。
variations: 我沒有把贈品藏起來，我只是最後一個知道它沒到貨的人。
公司負責宣傳「換到手軟」，我負責說「真的沒有了」。

en.content:
"The figure from the stamp promo. I want three."
"I'm sorry, we ran out yesterday."
"No way. You people took them for yourselves, didn't you?"
Sir, I didn't get a single one this round.
I don't decide how many this store is allocated.
I don't decide when they arrive.
The only thing I get to decide
is what my face does
while I say "they're really gone" for the forty-seventh time.
That shelf isn't empty because someone hid them.
It's empty because it was never full.
en.editorNote: For whoever gets stuck at the redemption counter during a promo. Store staff never control the allocation, but the customer only sees you — so "we're out" has to come out of your mouth.
variations: I'm not hiding the prizes. I'm just the last person to find out they never shipped.
Corporate runs the campaign. I deliver the sentence "we're out."

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 台中市交通局公車服務檢舉／脫班機制與近年公車司機勞動討論；rewritten as 起步前多等三秒與班表紀錄的衝突 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「司機你可以開快一點嗎？我快遲到了。」
後照鏡裡，最後上車的阿伯還沒抓到扶手。
我把腳從油門上移開，等了三秒。
車廂裡有人嘖了一聲，
後面那台車按了兩下喇叭。
回到站上，主管手裡拿著紀錄：
這一班，慢了四分鐘。
那四分鐘是怎麼來的，
表格上沒有那一欄。
我只知道今天這一車的人，
每一個都是站著上車、坐著到站。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在「準點」和「安全」之間選邊站的駕駛。時刻表記得住你慢了幾分鐘，記不住你為什麼慢。
variations: 我慢的那四分鐘寫在紀錄表上，我等的那三秒寫在「今天沒有人跌倒」上。
油門踩下去只要一秒，扶手抓穩要三秒，我選那三秒。

en.content:
"Driver, can you go any faster? I'm going to be late."
In the mirror, the last man on board still hadn't found a handrail.
I took my foot off the gas and waited three seconds.
Someone in the aisle clicked their tongue.
The car behind me honked twice.
Back at the depot, my supervisor had the log:
this run was four minutes late.
There is no column on that sheet
for where those four minutes went.
All I know is that everyone who boarded my bus today
was seated before we pulled away.
en.editorNote: For every driver choosing between on time and safe, twice a stop. The timetable remembers how late you were, never why.
variations: The four minutes are in the log. The three seconds are in the fact that nobody fell.
Hitting the gas takes one second. Grabbing a handrail takes three. I pick the three.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 104 職場力〈加油站打工經驗分享〉中的現場工作與客人互動；rewritten as 跳槍之後被要求硬湊整數金額 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「幫我加到五百整。」
跳槍的時候是五百零三。
「你不會控制喔？多的三塊算你的。」
我又壓了兩次板機，
第三次，油從加油口滿出來，
滴在我的鞋面上。
先生，跳槍不是我手抖，
是那台機器在說「夠了」。
您要的那個整數，只有發票上看得到；
溢出來的那一點，
是我等一下要蹲下去擦的地板，
和一雙洗三次還有味道的鞋。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給站在加油島上被要求「湊整數」的人。機器會停是因為它該停，這不是技術問題，是物理問題。
variations: 我可以把發票湊成整數，沒辦法把油湊成整數。
那三塊錢您記到下車，那雙鞋的味道只有我記得。

en.content:
"Fill it to exactly fifty."
The nozzle clicked off at fifty dollars and thirty cents.
"Can't you control it? That extra thirty is coming out of your pocket."
I squeezed the handle twice more.
The third time, fuel welled up out of the filler neck
and ran down onto my shoe.
Sir, that click isn't my hand shaking.
It's the machine saying that's enough.
The round number you wanted only exists on the receipt.
The part that spilled exists as the patch of ground
I'm about to crouch down and wipe,
and a shoe that still smells after three washes.
en.editorNote: For anyone on the island being told to round it up. The pump stops because it is supposed to stop. That's not a skill issue, it's physics.
variations: I can round the receipt. I can't round the fuel.
You'll remember those thirty cents until you drive off. I'm the one who remembers the shoe.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 服務業門市旺季排班與現場討論；rewritten as 八月底文具店的開學採購清單 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
八月的最後兩個星期，
我們店裡只賣一種東西，叫清單。
「老師說要十六格的，不是十二格。」
「書套要那種可以再撕下來的。」
「墊板不可以有圖案。」
有位媽媽在架子前面站了二十五分鐘，
手上那張紙已經摺出四條摺痕。
最後一項是藍色墊板，
只剩最上層那一片，
我搬了張椅子上去拿下來。
她說謝謝的時候，聲音有點抖。
這個月我一天假都沒有，
但我知道開學第一天，
有個小朋友的桌上，什麼都不會少。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給八月底的文具店、書局和制服行。別人準備結束暑假，我們準備把整條街的清單，一項一項湊齊。
variations: 別人的開學是一個新書包，我們的開學是連上十四天。
我背不出自己的班表，倒是背得出今年一年級的指定清單。

en.content:
The last two weeks of August,
our store only sells one product: the list.
"Teacher said sixteen squares, not twelve."
"The book covers have to be the kind you can peel back off."
"The desk pad can't have any pictures on it."
One mom stood in front of the shelf for twenty-five minutes,
the paper in her hand folded down to four creases.
The last item was a blue desk pad.
There was one left, on the top shelf.
I dragged a stool over and got it down.
Her voice shook a little when she said thank you.
I haven't had a day off all month.
But I know that on the first day of school
there's one kid whose desk won't be missing a thing.
en.editorNote: For the stationery shops, bookstores, and uniform tailors working the last week of summer. Everyone else is finishing a vacation; we're assembling a whole neighborhood's supply lists, one line at a time.
variations: Other people's back-to-school is a new backpack. Ours is fourteen shifts in a row.
I can't recite my own schedule, but I can recite this year's first-grade supply list.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 三立新聞網服務業現場客訴與等待壓力討論；rewritten as 窗口替長者填單與後方隊伍的時間拉扯 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
下午三點，窗口前面剩兩個人。
一位阿公第三次把單子推回來，
金額那一格還是空的。
我把筆轉了個方向，指著格子念一遍，
再念一遍。
後面那位先生嘆了第三口氣，
把號碼牌折成一半。
我知道您在趕，我也知道我慢了。
可是這張單子，他一年填一次，
我一天填一百次。
我多花的那幾分鐘，
是為了不要讓他明天再跑一趟。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給在窗口後面同時走兩種時間的人：一種是趕時間的人，一種是慢下來才做得對的事。
variations: 隊伍看得到我停在誰身上，看不到我停下來在做什麼。
我不是慢，我是在幫明天的隊伍少排一個人。

en.content:
Three in the afternoon, two people left at the window.
An older man pushed the form back to me for the third time.
The amount box was still blank.
I turned the pen around, pointed at the box, read it out loud,
then read it out loud again.
The guy behind him let out his third sigh
and folded his ticket in half.
I know you're in a hurry. I know I'm slow.
But he fills out this form once a year.
I fill it out a hundred times a day.
The few extra minutes I spent
are so he doesn't have to come back tomorrow.
en.editorNote: For anyone behind a counter running two clocks at once: the people in a hurry, and the thing that only comes out right slowly.
variations: The line can see who I stopped for. It can't see what I stopped to do.
I'm not slow. I'm making tomorrow's line one person shorter.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 自由健康網報導：長期碰水與清潔劑造成指腹紋路磨損、手機解鎖失敗；rewritten as 門市打卡機認不得我、改按員工編號 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「指紋辨識失敗，請重試。」
今天早上第四次。
洗手、消毒、拆箱、洗杯子，
手套戴上再脫掉，一天七十幾回，
指腹上那幾圈紋路，
被我自己一層一層洗掉了。
打卡機不認得我，
手機也不認得我。
我只好改按員工編號，
七位數字，一次就過。
這雙手每天替兩百個人結帳，
把熱的遞出去，把冷的收回來，
最後連自己是誰都證明不了。
機器認那串號碼，
我認得自己就好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天把手泡在水裡的人：餐飲、美髮、清潔、醫護。這份工作從你手上拿走的東西，只有掃描機看得見。
variations: 我的指紋不是不見了，是被兩百杯飲料一杯一杯帶走的。
打卡機不認得我沒關係，這雙手記得今天做了什麼。

en.content:
"Fingerprint not recognized. Try again."
Fourth time this morning.
Washing, sanitizing, box cutters, glassware,
gloves on, gloves off, seventy-some times a shift —
the ridges on my fingertips
got scrubbed away one layer at a time.
The time clock doesn't know me.
My phone doesn't know me.
So I punch in my employee number instead.
Seven digits. First try, every time.
These hands ring up two hundred people a day,
hand out the hot, take back the cold,
and can't prove who they belong to anymore.
The machine goes by the number.
I know who I am.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose hands live in water all shift — kitchens, salons, cleaning crews, clinics. What the job takes off your fingertips shows up nowhere but the scanner.
variations: Lost my fingerprints to two hundred iced drinks. The scanner noticed before I did.
Time clock can't read me. These hands still remember the whole shift.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 財政部稅務入口網說明：電子發票事後補加買受人統編須作廢重開；rewritten as 收銀台現場的五個補救動作 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「開好了，總共三百二。」
「啊，我要打統編。」
剛印出來的那張要作廢，
交易要重刷，載具要退掉，
存根聯要註明、要黏回去。
您少講的那三個字，
換成我多做的五個動作。
不是我不肯，
是這台機器比我還沒有彈性。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在收銀台跟發票系統搏鬥的人。也適合貼在櫃檯後面提醒自己深呼吸——卡住的是流程，不是你的手速。
variations: 世界上最貴的三個字，是結完帳之後才出現的「要統編」。
我不怕客人有統編，我怕統編比發票晚一秒到。

en.content:
"All set. Three-twenty total."
"Oh — put the company tax ID on that."
The slip that just printed gets voided.
The sale gets rung again.
The digital carrier gets unlinked.
The stub gets marked and pasted back.
Three words you didn't say
turn into five things I have to do.
It isn't that I won't.
It's that this machine bends less than I do.
en.editorNote: For everyone fighting the receipt system at the register. Also good taped behind the counter as a reminder to breathe — the workflow is what jammed, not you.
variations: Three cheap words, priciest possible timing: "tax ID on that."
I don't mind the tax ID. I mind it landing one second after the receipt.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Dcard 工作板長年討論的櫃檯用品消耗（筆、剪刀、膠帶）；rewritten as 一個月七支筆的防護升級史 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
櫃檯這支筆，這個月是第七支。
第一支被帶走。
第二支被帶走。
第三支我用膠帶黏了一朵塑膠花，還是被帶走。
第四支綁湯匙，第五支綁尺，
第六支我在筆桿上寫「請留步」。
現在這支，用鞋帶綁在收銀機上，
長度剛好夠簽名，不夠出門。
我沒有生氣，
我只是有點想知道，
那六支在外面過得好不好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給櫃檯、服務台、收貨處——所有守著那支永遠會消失的筆的人。輕鬆版共鳴，適合直接貼進同事群組。
variations: 我這輩子最扎實的資產管理訓練，是保護櫃檯那支筆。
在筆上綁湯匙不是幽默感，是三個月的實戰結論。

en.content:
Seventh pen at this counter this month.
First one walked out.
Second one walked out.
Third one had a plastic flower taped to it. Walked out.
Fourth had a spoon on it. Fifth had a ruler.
Sixth had "please stay" written down the barrel.
This one is tied to the register with a shoelace,
long enough to sign with, not long enough to leave.
I'm not angry.
I just want to know
how the other six are doing out there.
en.editorNote: For every counter, front desk, and receiving dock guarding the one pen that always disappears. Light enough to drop straight into the staff group chat.
variations: Best asset management training I ever got: one pen, one counter, one month.
Taping a spoon to the pen isn't a joke. It's three months of field research.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 104 人才白皮書：民生服務業每職缺平均分不到 0.3 人應徵、新進人員流動偏高；rewritten as 店長擦掉班表上那個鉛筆名字的早上 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
班表上那一格，我先用鉛筆寫了她的名字。
名牌做好了，
置物櫃貼了標籤，
倉庫翻出一件 S 號，掛在門後。
說好星期一早上九點。
九點十分，訊息還停在已讀。
十點，我把鉛筆的字擦掉，
那一格改成我自己。
我沒有生氣。
這一行來的人多，走的人也多。
只是想跟她說一聲：
哪天想回來看看，
那件 S 號我還留著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每個把一切都準備好、卻等到十點的店長與資深同事。也傳給曾經沒去成的那個自己——這一行不缺責備，缺的是位子還幫你留著。
variations: 缺工的數字聽起來很大，落到現場就是班表上被擦掉的一行鉛筆字。
我準備了名牌、置物櫃和一件 S 號，最後只用到那支橡皮擦。

en.content:
Wrote her name into the schedule in pencil.
Name tag made.
Locker labeled.
Pulled a size small from the back, hung it on the door.
Nine a.m. Monday, we said.
Nine-ten, the message is still just read.
At ten I erased the pencil
and put my own name in the box.
I'm not angry.
People come into this trade fast and leave it faster.
I just want her to know:
if she ever wants to come look around,
the small is still on the hook.
en.editorNote: For every manager and senior who set the whole thing up and were still waiting at ten. And for the version of you who once didn't show — this trade has no shortage of blame; what's short is a spot still held open.
variations: Staffing shortage sounds like a statistic. On the floor it's one penciled name, erased.
Made the tag, labeled the locker, pulled a size small. Only thing I used was the eraser.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 鏡週刊報導：飯店免費升等取決於排房表與住宿天數，非客人態度；rewritten as 櫃檯內心話與嘴上話的落差 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「有沒有機會幫我升等一下？」
「我幫您看看喔。」
我看的不是您的臉，也不是您的語氣。
我看的是那張排房表。
高樓層那間今晚空著，明天有人訂，
您只住一晚——可以。
換成後面那位住四晚的先生，
我這邊再有誠意，
系統也只會跳紅字。
「先生，幫您換到十二樓，看得到河。」
「哇，是不是因為我常住？」
是因為您明天就走。
（我當然是笑著說：「是啊，謝謝您一直支持我們。」）
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給飯店櫃檯與訂房組。也適合分享給以為升等是靠誠意的旅客——那是一張排房表，不是人品評分表。
variations: 升等不是看您多有禮貌，是看您多快退房。
櫃檯講得最溫暖的那句話，背後通常是一張很冷靜的排房表。

en.content:
"Any chance you could upgrade me?"
"Let me have a look for you."
What I'm looking at isn't your face or your tone.
It's the room chart.
The high-floor room is empty tonight and booked tomorrow.
You're here one night — that works.
The gentleman behind you is staying four.
However much I'd like to help,
the system just turns red.
"Sir, I've moved you to twelve. You'll see the river."
"Oh wow, is it because I stay here so often?"
It's because you leave tomorrow.
(Out loud, smiling: "Of course. We appreciate your loyalty.")
en.editorNote: For hotel front desks and reservations teams. Also worth sending to anyone who thinks upgrades are earned by charm — it's a room chart, not a character reference.
variations: Upgrades don't measure how polite you are. They measure how soon you check out.
The warmest line at the front desk usually comes off a very cold room chart.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by CTWANT 報導：服飾店試衣間拍穿搭片後衣服丟滿地、店員抱怨；rewritten as 八件進去一件出來與一句道歉的差別 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
試衣間第三間，簾子拉開。
八件進去，一件出來。
剩下七件躺在地上，
兩件是反的，一件的拉鍊卡在袖口。
她走出來跟我說：「不好意思喔，麻煩你了。」
我說沒關係。
是真的沒關係。
我怕的不是七件衣服，
是那種一邊拍照一邊把吊牌撥到後面、
拍完把整疊留在椅子上、
連頭都不用回的背影。
願意講一句話的客人，
我可以折一整天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給服飾店、運動用品店、所有站在試衣間外面等簾子拉開的人。也提醒逛街的人：把衣服掛回去只要一下下，那一下下會被記得很久。
variations: 八件進去一件出來不可怕，可怕的是一句話都沒有。
我折得動七件衣服，折不動那個拍完就走的背影。

en.content:
Fitting room three, curtain open.
Eight items went in. One came out.
The other seven are on the floor,
two inside out, one with the zipper caught in a sleeve.
On her way out she said, "Sorry about that, thank you."
I said it's fine.
It really is fine.
Seven items don't bother me.
What bothers me is the one who shoots photos
with the tags tucked out of frame,
leaves the whole pile on the stool,
and doesn't look back once.
For a customer who says something,
I'll fold all day.
en.editorNote: For clothing shops, sportswear stores, and everyone waiting outside a fitting room curtain. And a reminder for shoppers: hanging it back takes a second, and that second gets remembered for a long time.
variations: Eight in, one out isn't the problem. Not one word on the way out is.
I can fold seven things. I can't fold the back of someone who just walks off.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 關鍵評論網報導：2026 外送專法上路，明訂最低報酬與備註不得超出合理配送範圍；rewritten as 一天備註欄的五行清單 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
今天的備註欄：
「到了不要按門鈴，狗會叫。」
「飲料放鞋櫃上面，不要放地上。」
「門口那袋垃圾麻煩幫我帶下去。」
「醬料另外裝，你在店裡跟他們講一聲。」
「大門密碼 1234，自己進來放桌上。」
新法寫得很清楚：
備註不該超出合理的配送範圍。
可是備註欄不會自己讀法條，
它只會一直有字。
垃圾我沒帶，
鞋櫃上那杯，我還是幫他放好了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每天在紅綠燈前面讀短篇小說的外送員。新法保障的是報酬和申訴，備註欄那一格，還是得自己拿捏。
variations: 外送員一年的閱讀量，八成來自備註欄。
我送的是餐，不是到府全包——不過那杯我還是幫你放好了。

en.content:
Today's delivery notes:
"Don't ring the bell, the dog barks."
"Drink goes on the shoe cabinet, not the floor."
"Take the trash bag by the door down with you, thanks."
"Sauce on the side — tell them that at the restaurant."
"Door code is 1234, let yourself in and leave it on the table."
The new law is clear enough:
notes shouldn't ask for more than a reasonable delivery.
But the note field doesn't read statutes.
It just keeps filling up.
I left the trash.
The drink went on the shoe cabinet anyway.
en.editorNote: For every courier reading short fiction at a red light. The new rules cover pay and appeals; that little notes box is still yours to judge.
variations: Most of what a courier reads in a year comes out of the notes field.
I deliver food, not full household service — but yeah, I set your drink down properly.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by Dcard 閒聊板服務業經驗分享中常見的「我不是要客訴」開場；rewritten as 否定句開頭、客訴結尾的句型觀察 — original framing

zh-tw.content:
「我不是要客訴啦，我只是想反映一下。」
反映完的隔天，
信箱裡就會有一封客訴。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給客服、櫃檯，還有每個店長信箱。純吐槽用，適合當交接本上的一行，或群組裡那張圖底下的字。
variations: 「我只是想給你們一個建議」，通常是建議公司換掉我。
服務業最快辨識的句型：否定句開頭，客訴結尾。

en.content:
"I'm not filing a complaint, I just want to flag something."
Whatever got flagged
lands in my inbox as a complaint.
en.editorNote: For call centers, front desks, and every manager's inbox. Pure venting — good as a line in the shift log or the caption under that photo in the staff chat.
variations: "I just want to offer a suggestion" usually means suggesting they replace me.
The sentence pattern service workers spot fastest: opens as a denial, ends as a complaint.

items.sourceNote: 2026 七夕落在 8/19（三），餐廳訂位一位難求是每年固定現象；本則為外場視角原創改寫，不涉真實店家

zh-tw.content:
「七夕想訂兩位，靠窗。」
「只剩十點。」
「太晚了吧？」
那是我今天讓出的第九個浪漫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給七夕當天接到手軟的訂位電話的外場。
variations: 浪漫是有限的，靠窗那兩張椅子更有限。

en.content:
"Two for Qixi. Window seat."
"Only 10 p.m. is left."
"That's kind of late."
Sir, that's the ninth romance I've handed out today.
en.editorNote: For anyone working the phone on Qixi night.
variations: Romance is limited. Window seats are more limited.

items.sourceNote: 行號普渡多由老闆或行政主導、全員參與，祈求生意平安；本則為員工視角的溫和幽默，不涉宗教指導

zh-tw.content:
老闆在門口念「生意興隆、客似雲來」。
我小聲補一句：
「來可以，脾氣留在門口。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天陪老闆站在門口那半小時的同事。
variations: 老闆求的是人潮，我求的是好講話的人潮。

en.content:
Out front, the boss prays for good business and steady customers.
Behind him, I add one quiet line:
"Come on in. Leave the attitude outside."
en.editorNote: For whoever stood by the door with the boss today.
variations: The boss prays for a crowd. I pray for a reasonable one.

items.sourceNote: 115 學年度第一學期開學落在八月底，各縣市略有調整；本則寫早餐店視角，不指定全台統一日期

zh-tw.content:
暑假這兩個月，早上七點的店裡只有我跟電視。
開學那個禮拜一開始，隊伍又會排到騎樓外，
「蛋餅不要辣、奶茶半糖、我趕時間」三十個人一起講。
我一邊煎一邊想：終於。
然後又想：怎麼這麼快。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給八月底開始重新設鬧鐘的早餐店老闆和內外場。
variations: 早餐店的學期制：暑假養生，開學拚命。
我不是想念人潮，我是想念有人跟我講早安。

en.content:
For two summer months, 7 a.m. meant me and the TV.
Once school starts back, the line runs out past the awning again — thirty people ordering at once, all in a hurry.
Flipping eggs, I think: finally.
Then I think: that was fast.
en.editorNote: For every breakfast shop resetting its alarm in late August.
variations: Breakfast-shop semesters: quiet in summer, sprinting by September.
I don't miss the crowd. I miss someone saying good morning.

items.sourceNote: 農曆七月期間商家可擇日補辦普渡，日期常視店務安排；本則聚焦排班現實，不做習俗指導

zh-tw.content:
「我們今年哪天拜？」
老闆翻的不是農民曆，是班表。
最後挑了一個下午，
因為那是這個月唯一四個人都在店裡的半小時。
心裡求的是生意平安，
先解決的是有沒有人手。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給每年負責把普渡塞進班表縫隙的那位。
variations: 日子好不好我不知道，人湊不湊得齊我很清楚。
小店的行事曆只有一本，封面寫著班表。

en.content:
"What day are we doing the ghost-month offering?"
The boss doesn't check the almanac. He checks the schedule.
He picks an afternoon — the one half hour this month when all four of us are actually in the shop.
We're asking for a safe, steady business.
First we have to solve staffing.
en.editorNote: For whoever squeezes the offering into the roster every year.
variations: I can't read an almanac. I can read a schedule.
A small shop keeps one calendar, and it's the roster.

items.sourceNote: 情緒勞動中「表層演出」與內在真實感受落差的常見討論；本則為原創的雙軌台詞寫法，不引用個案

zh-tw.content:
「好的，沒問題。」
說出口的是這一句。
腦內同時在跑的是：
問題有三個，等一下我自己吞。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天嘴巴跟腦袋各講一句的同事。上面那句是給客人的，下面那句才是真的。
variations: 沒問題是對外版本，有問題是內部版本。
那三個問題後來都解決了，解決的人是我。

en.content:
Out loud: "Sure, no problem."
Inside my head: there are three problems, and I'll be swallowing every one of them after you leave.
en.editorNote: For the coworker whose mouth and brain ran two different scripts today.
variations: "No problem" is the customer-facing version. The internal version has bullet points.
Those three problems did get solved. By me. Later.

items.sourceNote: 服務現場一人多工、承諾時間與實際處理落差的普遍現象；本則為原創情境，不指涉特定店家

zh-tw.content:
「馬上」不是時間，是順序。
您是今天的第七個馬上。
每一個我都是真心的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在休息室。給每個說完「馬上」又轉身回去忙的人——那不是敷衍，是排序。
variations: 客人問還要多久，我說馬上。我們兩個都知道那是一種溫柔。
我沒有騙您，我只是把您排進了一條您看不到的隊伍。

en.content:
"Right away" isn't a time. It's a position.
You're the seventh right away today.
I meant it every single time.
en.editorNote: For everyone who says "right away" and turns straight back to the queue. Not a brush-off — a sort order.
variations: Someone asks how long. I say right away. We both know it's a kindness.
I didn't lie to you. I put you in a line you can't see.

items.sourceNote: 第一線人員代替不在場的同事或制度道歉，是客訴處理的常見結構；本則為原創寫法

zh-tw.content:
「不好意思，是我們沒做好。」
臉上掛著這句，
腦內只有一句：
沒做好的那位今天排休。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天替不在場的人道歉的同事。道歉的人和出錯的人，很少是同一個。
variations: 我道的歉，有一半是幫別人先付的。
「我們」這兩個字，今天站在這裡的只有我。

en.content:
My face says "Sorry, that's on us."
My brain says the person it's actually on is off today.
en.editorNote: For whoever apologized on behalf of someone who wasn't there.
variations: Half the apologies I make are paid in advance for somebody else.
"We" is a big word for one person standing at a counter.

items.sourceNote: 第一線授權有限、只能傾聽卻無法更動規則的落差；本則為原創的雙軌獨白，不涉真實對話

zh-tw.content:
「您說的我都了解。」
了解是真的，
改不了也是真的。
我只是被派來站在這裡聽完的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給今天被當成規則本人的同事。你聽得懂，不代表你有權限。
variations: 我點的每一次頭都是真的，只是點頭不會改到系統。
公司給我的權限，剛好停在「聽完」這兩個字。

en.content:
"I completely understand."
The understanding is real.
So is the fact that I can't change it.
I was just sent out here to hear it.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who got treated as the policy itself today.
variations: Every nod was genuine. None of them reach the system.
My authority ends exactly where listening ends.

items.sourceNote: 第一線人員長期承受無理對待、卻極少被關心的報導脈絡；本則為原創情境，人物與對白皆為虛構

zh-tw.content:
教育訓練那本手冊有一百多頁。
教我怎麼應付大聲的、
怎麼應付堅持要退貨的、
怎麼在被指著鼻子的時候把手擺在身前。
一百多頁，我幾乎背得起來。
上禮拜有位阿姨結完帳，
把找的零錢收進小包包，抬頭問我：
「妹妹，妳今天看起來很累，還好嗎？」
我說還好，然後轉身去補貨，
在冷藏庫門前站了半分鐘才走出來。
被罵，我有標準流程。
被關心，公司沒教。
zh-tw.editorNote: 轉給還在背話術的新人。會讓你站不穩的，通常不是難搞的那位客人。
variations: 手冊教我怎麼擋住惡意，沒有一頁教我怎麼接住善意。
難的不是有人對我大聲，是有人突然對我很輕。

en.content:
The training manual runs over a hundred pages.
How to handle the loud ones.
How to handle the ones who insist on a refund.
Where to keep your hands when someone points at your face.
A hundred pages. I could almost recite them.
Last week an older lady finished paying,
tucked her change into her purse, looked up and asked,
"Sweetheart, you look tired today. You okay?"
I said I was fine, went to restock,
and stood in front of the cooler door for half a minute before I came back out.
For being yelled at, I have a procedure.
For being cared about, nobody trained me.
en.editorNote: For the new hire still memorizing scripts. The thing that gets you is rarely the difficult customer.
variations: The manual teaches you to block hostility. Not one page covers catching kindness.
The hard part isn't someone raising their voice. It's someone suddenly going gentle.

items.sourceNote: 百貨與零售第一線人員被推到最前面承接情緒的討論；本則為原創獨白，非引述真實店家

zh-tw.content:
多希望有一天，我可以把那句最順的謊忘掉——
「不好意思，店長現在不在。」
店長在。
他在那道門後面，喝著今天第二杯咖啡。
這一行分得很清楚：
門裡的人負責簽名，
門外的人負責挨罵。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合下班後傳給同班的人。有些謊，我們講得比真心話還順。
variations: 要是哪天不必再說那句話，我大概還會不習慣。
講得最順的那句，通常是被逼出來的。

en.content:
Some days I wish I could unlearn my smoothest lie:
"I'm sorry, the manager isn't in right now."
He's in.
He's behind that door, on his second coffee.
This job splits the world cleanly.
Inside the door, you sign things.
Outside the door, you get yelled at.
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever closed with you tonight. Some lies come out smoother than the truth.
variations: If I ever stopped saying that line, I think I'd miss it.
The line you deliver best is usually the one you were forced into.
