items.sourceNote: 零售櫃檯是否能坐著工作的公共討論與職安署設置座椅規定；本則為原創情境改寫

zh-tw.content:
櫃檯後面那張椅子，是法規要我們放的。
三年來它擺過收銀袋、擺過補貨籃、擺過壞掉的掃描槍，
就是沒擺過人。
有一次腰真的撐不住，我坐了一下下，
監視器那頭的電話馬上就來：
「客人看到會覺得妳很閒。」
最近徵人啟事開始寫「可坐式收銀」，
底下一排留言說好棒喔。
一張椅子而已。
我們竟然要把它叫做福利。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個站到腳底發麻還不敢坐的人。坐下不是偷懶，是身體在講話。
variations: 那張椅子最常坐的是備品，不是人。
當坐著上班變成福利，就知道這一行被壓得多低。

en.content:
There's a chair behind the counter. Regulations say we have to have one.
In three years it has held cash bags, restock baskets, a dead scanner gun —
everything but a person.
One shift my back gave out and I sat down for a minute.
The phone rang from the camera room:
"Customers will think you have nothing to do."
Lately job ads have started advertising a "seated register."
The comments underneath call it amazing.
It's a chair.
And we've started filing it under benefits.
en.editorNote: For anyone standing until their feet go numb and still not daring to sit. Sitting isn't slacking.
variations: That chair mostly seats supplies, not staff.
When sitting down counts as a perk, you can guess how low the bar has sunk.

items.sourceNote: 客服中心過度以平均處理時間（AHT）評量人員的管理爭議；本則通話內容為虛構

zh-tw.content:
系統上的平均處理時間，目標是六分鐘。
今天有一通，我講了二十三分鐘。
一位阿姨的帳單多了兩百塊，
原因她自己早就知道，
只是家裡剩她一個人，
這件事沒有第二個人可以講。
掛掉之前，她說了三次謝謝。
月底排名出來，我從第四名掉到最後一名，
主管用紅筆寫了三個字：待加強。
那兩百塊，六分鐘就處理完了。
剩下的十七分鐘，
是我這個月唯一確定做對的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 分享給被秒數追著跑的客服同事。有些對話的價值，報表算不出來。
variations: 報表量得出通話長度，量不出電話那頭的安靜。
六分鐘可以解決帳單，解決不了一個人一整天沒跟誰說過話。

en.content:
Our target average handle time is six minutes.
Today one call ran twenty-three.
An older woman's bill was two hundred over.
She already knew why.
She just lives alone now,
and there was nobody else to tell it to.
Before hanging up she thanked me three times.
When the monthly rankings posted, I fell from fourth to last,
and my supervisor wrote one word in red: improve.
The two hundred took six minutes to fix.
The other seventeen
are the only thing I'm sure I got right this month.
en.editorNote: For every agent being chased by a stopwatch. Some calls are worth more than the report can measure.
variations: The report measures how long the call was, not how quiet the other end had been.
Six minutes can fix a bill. It can't fix a day with nobody to talk to.

items.sourceNote: 2026 美髮業「助理荒」與業者引進 AI 洗頭機的報導；對話為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
店裡新來的那台機器會自己洗頭，
水溫、力道都調得比我的手準。
客人躺下去以前問我：
「那你以後要幹嘛？」
我說，我負責在旁邊聽您講話。
它學得會沖水，
學不會在您說「最近有點累」的時候，
把水放慢一點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給美髮、美容、按摩這類「手上功夫會被機器取代」的朋友。機器接得走流程，接不走那三十分鐘裡有人願意聽你講話這件事。
variations: 機器會照著設定洗完，不會發現您今天比上次沉默。
被取代的是動作，留下來的是那句「最近還好嗎」。

en.content:
The salon got a machine that shampoos on its own.
Water temp, pressure — steadier than my hands ever were.
Before she lay back, a client asked me,
"So what's left for you to do?"
I told her I'm the one who listens.
The machine learned the rinse.
It hasn't learned to slow the water down
when someone says, "I've been tired lately."
en.editorNote: For anyone in salons, spas, or massage work watching a machine learn their hands. It can take the steps; it can't take the half hour where somebody actually listens.
variations: The machine runs the preset. It won't notice you're quieter than last time.
What gets automated is the motion. What stays is "how have you been?"

items.sourceNote: 取材自服務業社群關於「翻場時間被壓縮」的討論；影城場景為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
一場電影一百二十分鐘，我們清場只有十二分鐘。
第七排的爆米花踩下去會響，
第三排的可樂在地毯上乾成一塊深色的圓。
下一場的隊伍已經在門口排好，
有人隔著繩子問我還要多久。
十二分鐘，我從最後一排走到第一排，
把別人兩個小時的快樂，一顆一顆撿起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給影城、球場、展場那些負責「翻場」的工讀夥伴。觀眾記得的是片尾字幕，你們記得的是第七排。
variations: 散場燈一亮，別人的兩個小時就變成我的十二分鐘。
沒有人會為清場的速度鼓掌，只會為慢了三分鐘嘆氣。

en.content:
The movie runs a hundred and twenty minutes. We get twelve to clear the house.
Row seven's popcorn crunches under your shoe.
Row three's cola has dried into a dark circle in the carpet.
The next crowd is already lined up outside, and someone leans over the rope to ask how much longer.
Twelve minutes, back row to front, picking up two hours of somebody else's good time one piece at a time.
en.editorNote: For the crews who turn over theaters, stadiums, and expo halls. The audience remembers the credits; you remember row seven.
variations: House lights up: their two hours become my twelve minutes.
Nobody claps for a fast turnover. They only sigh when it runs three minutes long.

items.sourceNote: 第一線櫃檯與長者互動的日常；診所情境為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
一位阿伯站在櫃檯前，把健保卡推過來又收回去，來回三次。
我以為他是在氣掛號費調了十塊，
正想跟他解釋公告貼在哪裡。
他終於開口：「小姐，我兒子叫我來看醫生，可是我不知道要看哪一科。」
那天我陪他把會痛的地方一項一項寫下來，
掛號單上那三個字，是我們兩個一起選的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給診所、公家窗口、藥局櫃檯的夥伴。有些人不是在刁難，是站在那裡不知道從哪裡問起。
variations: 他推回來的不是抱怨，是一句還沒想好怎麼開口的求助。
櫃檯前那三秒的猶豫，有時候是一個人今天最鼓起勇氣的時刻。

en.content:
An older man kept pushing his health card across the counter and pulling it back. Three times.
I assumed he was upset about the ten-dollar copay increase and started explaining where the notice was posted.
Then he said it: "Miss, my son told me to see a doctor, but I don't know which department I need."
We wrote down every place that hurt, one by one, and picked the department on that form together.
en.editorNote: For clinic, pharmacy, and government-window staff. Sometimes a person isn't being difficult — they just don't know where to start asking.
variations: What he pushed back across the counter wasn't a complaint. It was a question he hadn't figured out how to ask.
Those three seconds of hesitation can be the bravest thing in someone's whole day.

items.sourceNote: 餐飲外場呼叫鈴被連按的日常吐槽，改寫成擬人化視角；情境為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
如果桌上那顆呼叫鈴會說話，它今天大概想請假。
十二號桌按了它十一次，
每一次都是「再一盤肉」跟「怎麼還沒來」。
我端著盤子跑過去的時候，它還在亮。
它亮十一次，一步路都不用走；
我跑十一趟，手上的盤子還不准晃。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給火鍋、燒肉、居酒屋的外場夥伴。鈴聲響起來只要零點五秒，跑完那趟要四十步。
variations: 呼叫鈴是全店最輕鬆的員工：只要亮，不用跑。
按第十一次的時候，第十次那盤正端在我手上。

en.content:
If the call button on table twelve could talk, it would be asking for the day off.
They pressed it eleven times, every time for "another plate of beef" or "where is it."
It was still glowing when I got there with the plate.
Eleven flashes and it never took a step; eleven runs, and I wasn't allowed to let the plate tilt.
en.editorNote: For hot pot, BBQ, and izakaya floor staff. The bell takes half a second to ring and forty steps to answer.
variations: The call button has the easiest job in the restaurant: it only has to light up.
By the time you pressed it the eleventh time, the tenth order was already in my hands.

items.sourceNote: 宴會廳一日兩場、翻場時間極短的外場日常；情境為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
這個廳一天辦兩場，中午送客到晚上進場，中間只有九十分鐘。
三百張椅套要換過、地毯要吸過、氣球要全部換色，
上一對的名字從螢幕上撤下來，再把下一對的放上去。
新娘的媽媽走過來問我：「你們是不是常常看到很感人的畫面？」
我說是啊，一個月看三十場「一輩子一次」，
最後最會哭的，是站在角落數椅套的那個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給婚宴會館、宴會廳的外場夥伴。別人一生一次的那一天，是我們一個月三十次的班。
variations: 螢幕上的名字換得比我們的休息時間還快。
九十分鐘之內，這個廳要從一對新人的回憶，變成另一對新人的開場。

en.content:
This hall books two weddings a day, and between the lunch send-off and the evening arrival we get ninety minutes.
Three hundred chair covers swapped, carpet vacuumed, balloons recolored,
one couple's names pulled off the screen and the next couple's put up.
The bride's mother came over and asked, "You must see such moving moments all the time, don't you?"
I said sure — thirty once-in-a-lifetimes a month,
and the one most likely to cry by the end is whoever's in the corner counting chair covers.
en.editorNote: For banquet and wedding-venue floor crews. The day that happens once in their lives happens thirty times a month on your schedule.
variations: The names on that screen change faster than our breaks do.
In ninety minutes this room stops being one couple's memory and becomes another couple's entrance.

items.sourceNote: 機場報到櫃檯手提行李超重、旅客與地勤僵持的新聞討論；對白為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
「二十三點四公斤，超過兩公斤喔。」
「扣掉箱子本身的重量，應該剛剛好吧？」
「箱子也要飛，它也佔一個位子。」
「後面十七個人在等，您把外套穿上、鞋子換成手上那雙，我們就過關了。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 送給機場報到櫃檯與登機門的夥伴，規則寫在公司的手冊上，被念的卻永遠是站在櫃檯這一側的你。
variations: 磅秤跳出幾公斤就是幾公斤，我這邊能做的，就是照著唸給您聽。
我想做的事情很單純，把您順順利利送上那班飛機。

en.content:
"Twenty-three point four kilos, so you're two over."
"If you subtract the suitcase itself, it should be fine, right?"
"The suitcase flies too, and it takes up a seat's worth of space."
"Seventeen people are waiting behind you, so put the jacket on, swap into the shoes in your hand, and we'll get you through."
en.editorNote: For check-in counter and gate crews, you didn't draw that line, but you're the one standing in front of it.
variations: The number on the scale isn't mine, I'm just the one who has to say it out loud.
I'm not trying to ruin your morning, I'm trying to get you on that plane.

items.sourceNote: 高溫下穿玩偶裝演出的工讀生報導；場景為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
三十四度，玩偶裝裡面再加五度，風扇是脖子後面兩顆三號電池撐著的小東西。
出場十五分鐘，回後台脫下頭套，助理遞來一瓶運動飲料和一條冰毛巾。
手套裡的汗滴到地墊上，圈成一小片深色。
兩分鐘後，頭套戴回去，那隻手又在門邊揮起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給樂園裡穿著布偶裝的夥伴，小孩看到的是魔法，你扛的是三十九度。
variations: 布偶不會流汗，裡面那個人會。
後台那條冰毛巾，是這份工作唯一的冷氣。

en.content:
Ninety-four outside, another nine inside the costume, and the fan is two AA batteries taped behind your neck.
Fifteen minutes out front, then backstage, head off, and an assistant hands over a sports drink and a frozen towel.
Sweat runs out of the glove and pools into a small dark circle on the mat.
Two minutes later the head goes back on, and the hand is waving at the doorway again.
en.editorNote: For everyone working inside a character costume, the kids see magic and you carry the heat.
variations: The costume never sweats, the person inside it does.
That frozen towel backstage is the only air conditioning this job has.

items.sourceNote: 寵物美容師工作心得討論串；電話情境為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
電話那頭的聲音很急：「你們剪完，我家狗一直在抖。」
我翻開今天的紀錄，水溫、吹風時間、電剪的號數，一項一項準備好要解釋。
她接著說：「牠是從你們門口就開始搖尾巴，搖到整隻都在晃。」
「牠十二歲了，我打過三家，只有你們願意接這麼老的狗。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 給寵物美容師，狗會抖，有時候因為怕，有時候因為太開心。
variations: 剪刀之外，我們還得會讀狗的抖法。
願意接老狗的那雙手，值得被大聲說一次謝謝。

en.content:
The voice on the phone came in fast: "Since you groomed her, my dog hasn't stopped shaking."
I pulled up the day's notes, water temperature, dryer time, blade number, ready to explain every line of it.
Then she said, "She started at your front door, wagging so hard the whole dog wobbled."
"She's twelve, and I called three places before yours said yes to a dog that old."
en.editorNote: For pet groomers, the shaking in your hands isn't always fear and sometimes it's joy.
variations: Past the clippers, the real skill is reading how a dog shakes.
Hands willing to take the old dogs deserve a thank-you said out loud.

items.sourceNote: 配鏡價差與實體店被當展示間的網友討論；敘事為原創虛構

zh-tw.content:
我是試戴區左邊第二副鏡框，今天被拿起來十一次。
每一次戴上去，都有人幫我把鼻墊調開一點點，再用麂皮把指紋擦乾淨。
第十一個人戴著我照了三分鐘鏡子，然後掏出手機，把我腳上的型號拍下來。
他說了聲謝謝就走出門，剛剛擦我的那個人，還是笑著說慢走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 給眼鏡行與所有被當成展示間的門市夥伴，你的專業被拍成一張型號照帶走，那句慢走卻還是你自己撐著說完的。
variations: 被拍走的是型號，被留下來的是那條擦拭布。
有人幫你把鼻墊調到剛剛好的那三分鐘，也算在那個標價裡面。

en.content:
I'm the second frame from the left on the try-on wall, and I got picked up eleven times today.
Every time, somebody widened my nose pads a little and wiped the fingerprints off me with a microfiber cloth.
The eleventh one wore me in front of the mirror for three minutes, then pulled out a phone and photographed the model number on my temple.
He said thanks and walked out, and the person who had just cleaned me still smiled and told him to take care.
en.editorNote: For optical shops and every store used as somebody's showroom, your expertise leaves as a photo of a model number and you're still the one saying take care.
variations: What got photographed was the model number, what stayed behind was the cleaning cloth.
We don't only sell frames, we sell the three minutes somebody spent fitting them to your face.
